THAPAL V4

Development and Production Readiness Assessment

10 out of 10 Target Standard \| 9 November 2026 \| Owner: KK \| Review version 1.0

Decision: Thapal must meet a verified 9.9--10/10 quality standard across all major areas before being called production-ready. A target of 10/10 is a required outcome, not a declaration that the application has already achieved it.

# 1 Executive assessment

The approved Signature Flow visual direction and the fourteen P3 accounting-policy decisions are complete at the decision level. The application has not yet met the same standard in accounting implementation, legal-entity isolation, historical reconciliation, security, screen coverage or disaster recovery. We will close the six architectural gaps first, then finish complete user journeys and independent release testing.

Source basis: Thapal V3/V3.1, approved Signature Flow, initial 68-feature/1,536-requirement registers, and Claude's later isolated P1/P2/P3 summary. The latest post-audit registers, hosted migration evidence and actual code have not been independently reviewed for this scoring. All baseline ratings are qualitative, provisional judgments.

# 3 Approved accounting policies

All fourteen Section 10 P3 policy choices are approved for development and isolated testing: 1 A reversal/replacement; 2 A exceptions for unknown counterpart; 3 A sourced opening journal; 4 A skip locked periods; 5 B personal accounting; 6 A functional-currency lines preserving original currency/rate; 7 B owner and authorised accountant access initially; 8 B entity-aware closing checks; 9 A cross-account restore exceptions; 10 A reversal instead of deletion; 11 A reconciliation-only metadata edits; 12 A previewed manual re-sync; 13 mandatory follow-up before authoritative period close; 14 B demo guests cannot post. These decisions do not approve a production database migration or screen activation.

# 4 The six critical foundation recovery gates

## Gate A Security and access control

• P1 containment: company-specific access, personal privacy, document ownership/folder rules, no silent destructive effects.

• P2 roles: old permissions preserved until explicit mapping; scoped grants, identity checks, expiry, revocation and audit.

• External assistant tokens must be revocable; five-minute phone and fifteen-minute desktop session rules; step-up for approvals and exports.

• All High issues closed, including negative permission tests and cross-account restore.

## Gate B Balanced accounting

• One authoritative balanced double-entry journal on the existing architecture.

• One economic event posted once across receipt, statement, card, trip and reimbursement views.

• Personal, company and trust scopes; immutable posted entries, reversal, opening journal, closed-period controls.

• Complete financial reports reconcile with journal and subsidiary records; no fabricated balancing lines.

## Gate C Legal entities and database

• True person/company/trust ownership, distinct from Me/Family/Business UI labels.

• Normalized records and permanent IDs for accounts, assets, properties, investments, claims and trips.

• Reversible, staged migration and before/after data-parity checks.

## Gate D Historical integrity

• Independent opening balance and bank-statement checks from April 2026 onward.

• No double posting, silent deletion, undocumented prior-period changes or missing evidence.

• Reconcile historic GL, bank/card, assets, liabilities and output reports with a documented variance bridge.

## Gate E All-screen UIX

• 111/111 contracts with route, data, role, state, export, screenshot and test reference.

• Real iPhone, iPad portrait/landscape and desktop checks against Signature Flow.

• Smart Add, Statement Desk, Money, Records, Travel, Assets, Property, Investments, Reports, Calendar and professional journeys function end to end.

## Gate F Backup and release

• Full production-like restore, attachments and audit references included; RPO/RTO actually measured.

• Provider outage and interrupted background task recovery verified.

• Separate written KK approval for read-only production checks, P1/P2/P3 application, protected merge, UI activation and publication.

# 5 Mandatory end-to-end financial proof

1\. Create and isolate a company with a source-backed opening balance.

2\. Upload a bank month through Smart Add; retain document bytes and extracted row references.

3\. Match bills, receipts, charges, refunds, partial payments and one duplicate without inventing entries.

4\. Post through the controlled balanced journal and show precise reconciliation.

5\. Create PDF, Excel and CSV GL, trial balance, financial statements and bank reconciliations with identical totals.

6\. Demonstrate card payment versus expense and reimbursement settlement without second expenses.

7\. Close and reopen a month under correct company-specific permissions, with audit-safe correction.

8\. Interrupt processing, retry and restore from backup without duplication or data loss.

9\. Repeat relevant journeys on real iPhone, iPad and desktop, with screenshots and logs.

# 6 Unacceptable release conditions

• Any unresolved Critical or High security vulnerability.

• Any unexplained accounting imbalance, duplicate financial effect, unsafe historical edit or silent deletion.

• Any cross-entity data leakage or permission escalation.

• Failed production-like recovery or missing audit evidence.

• Major broken UI journey, misleading financial balance, unsupported live price or false filing status.

• Incomplete statutory schema validation where required for the released function.

• Unapproved migration, merge, feature activation or publication.

# 7 Evidence-based scoring method

For each area, reviewers record requirements applicable, coverage achieved, automated tests, realistic end-to-end evidence, security/financial checks, device evidence, defects, production parity and owner approval. 10/10 requires all mandatory acceptance criteria and zero release-blocking defects. 9.9/10 may be assigned only when residual issues are explicitly documented as immaterial, approved and outside safety-critical financial or access controls. Not-tested and externally blocked work cannot be counted as passed.

Reported passing test counts---such as the 2,317 isolated tests---are evidence of local test execution, not proof of production readiness. Baseline scores must be recalculated only from current signed registers, migration reports and independently verified outputs.

Use the Thapal V4 Production Readiness Master and the full requirement/screen registers. Preserve existing records and approved Signature Flow. Address the six foundation gaps before feature expansion. For each batch provide exact requirement IDs, code/database changes, tests, negative cases, historic balance parity, security evidence, screenshots, unresolved issues and updated scoring. # 10 Final position

Target: 10/10 across every category. Accounting policies and visual direction are approved at the decision/design level. Actual production readiness remains approximately 3/10 on the earlier qualitative audit until migration, historical, functional, security and restoration evidence changes that assessment. The project is authorised to pursue the target---not to declare it achieved.

## Validation of the 8 November draft

The vision is sound and the accounting controls are unusually strong. The clumsiness comes from structure: too many doors, named after internal machinery, shown the same way to every kind of user.

### What is right and must be kept

-   **Upload-only, no bank linking.** Lower security exposure and no aggregator dependency. Statements, bills and forwarded emails are enough.

-   **One ledger with separate observations and postings.** A receipt, a bank row and a card row are three views of one event. This is the correct engine.

-   **Source-preserving corrections.** Reversals and superseding versions, never silent edits. Auditors will trust this.

-   **Honest status discipline.** Draft, preview, published and verified are kept apart. Test counts are not treated as proof.

-   **Humans approve consequential acts.** Filing, paying, publishing and history changes need a person.

### Why it feels clumsy

Modules appear only when your documents need them

Review opens in place. The Statement Desk engine stays as the single intake behind it

### Gaps against the 360° vision

These are needed for \"a layperson never worries about books, tax or compliance\" but are missing or thin in the draft:

1.  **Sales invoicing** inside Thapal (you asked for it; the draft only mentions invoices as uploads).

2.  **Purchases and payables:** vendor bills, GST input-credit matching, TDS on payments, MSME payment deadlines.

3.  **The company secretary role:** statutory registers, meetings, resolutions, MCA filings, director KYC. Absent today.

4.  **Insurance** as a register: policies, premiums, nominees, renewals, claims, cash values.

5.  **Forex** as holdings: foreign-currency accounts, forex cards, LRS remittances and the TCS credit they create.

6.  **Personal income-tax preparation:** AIS/Form 16 matching, capital gains, regime comparison, advance tax.

7.  **How tax gets paid without bank linking:** prepared challan, paid from your own bank, receipt uploaded and matched.

8.  **Payroll**, at least importing a salary register and producing the salary entries.

9.  **The new income-tax law.** The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 April 2026; FY 2025-26 stays under the 1961 Act ([ClearTax](https://cleartax.in/s/income-tax-act-2025-frequently-asked-questions)). Your history starts in April 2026, so both laws must coexist in the rules library.

10. **Data protection.** Most DPDP Act duties, including consent, children\'s data and breach notification, apply from 12 May 2027 ([AZB & Partners](https://www.azbpartners.com/?p=87799)).

11. **Everyday conveniences:** forward-by-email intake, a monthly summary letter, plain-language questions, nominee and emergency-access readiness.

### Risks to manage

-   **Building everything at once in a prompt-driven tool** is the main source of instability. Sequence the work and freeze scope per phase.

-   **Financial rules living in screen code.** Lovable apps can drift. Balancing, locking and duplicate prevention must be enforced by the database (see Building with Lovable).

-   **\"Fully automatic filing\" needs outside approvals.** Direct GST, e-invoice and income-tax submission run through government-recognised intermediaries; MCA forms need digital signatures and often professional certification. Thapal prepares and tracks; people submit.

-   **Liability for wrong tax figures.** Every computation stays marked draft until a qualified professional reviews it.

-   **Extraction accuracy is unproven on your real documents.** Automation levels must follow measured accuracy, not test counts.

## The simplified product

Thapal becomes four places and one button: **Home**, **Money**, **To-do** and **Records**, with **Add** in the middle.

**The promise to you:** \"You control everything. Upload it once; Thapal keeps the books for every person, company and trust, watches the deadlines and tells you where you stand. You answer only what it cannot know.\"

**Rule zero: you control everything.** You can see and do every action in every workspace you own. Thapal and the professionals you invite prepare and propose; you approve, change or undo. Professionals see only what you grant, for as long as you grant it.

![one document\'s journey · 4 steps, 1 decision, 7 screens](media/image1.png){width="6.0in" height="3.9732141294838144in"}

one document\'s journey · 4 steps, 1 decision, 7 screens

Only uncertain items reach To-do; everything else flows straight to the ledger, and every place and professional workspace reads that same ledger.

### The one-action promise (revision 4)

As an individual you have one job: scan, upload or forward. Everything after that is Thapal\'s job.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  You do                                                                                    Thapal does
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Snap or upload a receipt, one or fifty at a time                                          Reads it; finds the card or account that paid, the category, and the person, company or trust it belongs to; checks GST; links it to the statement row; posts it

  Upload or forward a bank or card statement, or let an upload request collect it           Reads every row; matches transfers, card bills and receipts; checks the balance; posts each item once

  Upload any other document: policy, deed, loan letter, CAS, past return, contractor bill   Recognises it; builds or updates the right register; sets reminders; updates the books and net worth

  Nothing else                                                                              Bookkeeping, reconciliation, statements, month close, tax workings, compliance calendar, reports and evidence packs
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Only three things can still reach you, each as one tap in To-do with the answer already suggested: a genuinely new situation, such as a first payment to someone new; approvals you chose to keep, such as the month lock or a filing; and steps the law or your bank keeps human, such as an OTP on a government portal or approving a payment in your bank. Debits, credits and journals stay out of your sight unless you switch on Accountant view.

### Eight design rules

1.  **One way in.** Every statement, bill, receipt or invoice arrives through Add. There is no second upload place.

2.  **One list of what needs you.** If it is not in To-do, nothing is waiting.

3.  **Ask only what documents cannot tell.** Every question carries a suggested answer and a \"Why are you asking?\" link.

4.  **Plain words first.** Professional terms are one tap away, never the headline.

5.  **Show the effect first; allow undo after.** Every consequential change previews its result and can be reversed.

6.  **Features appear when needed.** Property appears after a deed or lease arrives; Governance appears for companies; Trips appear when travel is detected.

7.  **Every number opens to its proof.** Tap an amount to see its transactions, then the source document.

8.  **One ledger, a lens per role.** Owner, bookkeeper, accountant, auditor and company secretary see the same truth through different screens.

  Records        Show me the proof, or give me a report   Documents, Reports, History (who changed what, when)                                                                                                                           DocuRepo, Reports, Review History, audit trail

  Add (button)   How do I put something in?               Scan, upload, forward by email, create an invoice, record cash                                                                                                                 Smart Add, the Statement Desk front door, manual entry

### Workspaces

A switcher sits at the top of every screen: **Me**, **Family**, each **company**, and **Everything** (a read-only combined view). Each workspace keeps its own owner, books, permissions and tax identity, as v1 §3 requires. \"Everything\" shows combined net worth with intercompany holdings removed, so nothing is counted twice.

A company workspace uses the same four places with business content. Home shows cash, who owes you, whom you owe, draft profit, and tax and compliance due. Money shows Bank, Sales, Purchases and Assets.

## Money Map: every rupee and every action in one window (revision 7)

The Money Map is a living mind map of your whole group: where money came from, where it sits, where it went, what it built up, what is owed, and every action taken or waiting. Open it from Home, then tap any branch to go deeper, down to a single transaction and its receipt.

![Money Map · 6 branches around the centre](media/image2.png){width="6.0in" height="3.3125in"}

Money Map · 6 branches around the centre

Money flows in on the left and out or into savings on the right; the Actions branch shows what Thapal did, what needs you and what awaits approval.

### The six branches

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Branch        What opens beneath it
  ------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Came in       Income by source: salary and professional fees, business receipts, rent, interest and dividends, donations and grants, loans received

  Held in       Every bank account, card, cash wallet and forex card, by entity, with its balance and proof status

  Spent on      Categories, payees, trips, projects, salaries and suppliers

  Built up      Deposits, shares and funds, gold, land, property and other assets, each with a dated value

  Owed          Loans and EMIs, card dues, taxes due, and who owes whom between you, your family, the companies and the trusts

  Actions       Done for you (posted, matched, filed), Needs you, Waiting for approval, and who did what and when
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Reading it

-   **Centre:** the scope you choose: Everything, Me, Family, one company, one trust, a trip or a project.

-   **Thickness and colour:** a branch is as thick as its amount. Money in and money out have their own colours; transfers between your own accounts are dotted, so they never look like spending.

-   **Badges** on any node: \"3 need you\", \"receipt missing\", \"over budget\", \"value is 45 days old\".

-   **Time:** this month by default, a slider for any period, Play to watch money move month by month, and Compare to see each branch against the previous period.

-   **Focus:** search \"Swiggy\", \"Company A\" or \"Dubai trip\" and the map re-centres there; a breadcrumb leads back.

-   **Three layouts of the same data:** Mind map (the default), Flow (left to right, from Came in through Held in to Spent on and Built up) and Network (entities as circles, with arrows for who owes whom).

### Acting from the map

-   Tap a leaf to see its transactions, each with its document and the usual action menu: edit, split, change category, mark personal, add to trip, delete.

-   Drag a payee onto a category to move all its items there, with a preview and undo, and an offer to make it a standing rule.

-   Answer a \"needs you\" badge on the spot, or approve with Face ID, fingerprint or PIN.

-   Every action appears in the Actions branch: who did what, when, and what changed.

### Numbers you can trust

The map is drawn from the same ledger as the reports, so each node\'s figure equals its report and the total of its transactions. Transfers between your own accounts are netted out, so nothing is counted twice. Totals are worked out on the server, so the map opens quickly however many transactions there are; small items sit in \"Others\" until you open it.

  iPad           The same canvas with pinch, zoom and drag; details in a side panel; portrait or landscape, with a keyboard or Apple Pencil

  iPhone         One level at a time: the centre and its branches fill the screen; tap a branch to step in, swipe to step back. A List button shows the same figures as rows

### Language rules

-   At most one professional term per layperson screen, always with its plain meaning beside it.

-   Error messages say what happened and what to do: \"October\'s closing balance is ₹1,250 higher than the statement. Two payments may be missing. Show them.\"

-   Buttons are verbs with counts: \"Add 133 transactions\", not \"Submit\".

-   Amounts use ₹ with Indian grouping (₹12,34,567.00); compact forms (₹12.3 L, ₹1.2 Cr) only in summaries, with the exact figure on tap.

### Financial language on professional pages and in government-ready exports (revision 3)

Two vocabularies, one ledger. Your pages use plain words; the accountant, auditor and company secretary workspaces, and every file meant for a professional or a government portal, use standard accounting and statutory language.

-   **Professional workspaces open in Accountant view:** account codes, Dr and Cr columns, voucher and journal numbers, ledger and group names, schedule references, and GSTIN, PAN, TAN and CIN on every entity.

-   **Statutory captions on statements:** balance sheet and statement of profit and loss in Schedule III format for companies; income and expenditure account, receipts and payments account and balance sheet for trusts; numbered notes to accounts.

-   **Working papers use each portal\'s own field names and table numbers,** so a figure can be keyed or uploaded without translation.

-   **Government upload files** are produced in the format each portal accepts (JSON, text or Excel) and checked against the current schema from the AI rules watch before download.

-   **Every export states** the entity, period, the Act and rules it follows (1961 or 2025 Act), preparer, reviewer and status: Draft, Reviewed, Approved or Filed.

-   **Either way round:** you can switch any screen to Accountant view, and a professional can switch to plain view.

You are at the centre. Seven helper roles work on your ledger; each sees only what you grant and lands on a screen built for its job.

### What each professional workspace holds

-   **Bookkeeper --- Workbench.** The To-do queue at scale, grouped by account and type. Desktop three-pane view: queue, item, document. Bulk rules (\"Always treat NEFT-ABC TRADERS as supplier ABC Traders\"). A missing-documents chase list with expiring upload links. A banner per company: \"Books current up to 6 Nov.\"

-   **Accountant --- Close board.** One row per company per month with the close checklist from the Business section. Journals with effect previews, working papers for GST, TDS and income tax, review notes, and structured questions to the owner. Documents the accountant uploads land in the owner\'s Add queue tagged \"Uploaded by accountant\".

-   **Auditor --- Audit room.** Read-only. Pick an entity and period to freeze an immutable snapshot. Drill from trial balance to ledger to document. Sampling tools, a query tracker (open, answered, closed) and a change log since the snapshot. Records the audit report\'s UDIN on sign-off.

-   **Company secretary --- Governance.** Registers, meetings, resolutions, the MCA filings tracker, director KYC and DSC expiry, capital, and a compliance status board per company (see Governance). Reads the financials it needs; cannot post entries.

### Access rules

-   Every grant names a person, a workspace or company, a role, a start date and an expiry date; revocation takes effect immediately.

-   Invitations verify email and mobile. Professionals record their credentials: ICAI membership and firm registration number for accountants and auditors, ICSI membership number for company secretaries. UDINs are captured when they certify a document.

-   A monthly access review on Home: \"Your accountant still has access to Company A until 31 March. Keep or remove?\"

-   Family members see only what is explicitly shared, account by account or budget by budget.

One directory holds your whole group: you and your family, 7 companies, 4 trusts (2 with 80G approval), about 17 bank accounts and 11 cards. Every rupee carries two tags: who paid it, and whom it belongs to.

### Paid by, belongs to

-   **Paid by** is the instrument: \"Amex ending 1004\", \"Company A HDFC Current\", \"Cash\", \"UPI from SBI personal\".

-   **Belongs to** is who bears the cost: you, a family member, a company, a trust, a trip or a project.

When the two differ, Thapal records the consequence automatically, after you confirm the pattern once.

### Who owes whom

One screen nets every due between you, your family, the companies and the trusts. One tap proposes a settlement plan; the transfers you make are matched when the statements arrive.

**Standing rules you set once,** for example: \"Company A reimburses my travel; Company B records it as a director\'s loan\", or \"Anything paid at the hospital belongs to Trust 2\". You can change or switch off any rule from its action menu.

## Family umbrella: everyone\'s money in one place, each with their own access (revision 4)

Every family member sits under one umbrella. Each stays a separate taxpayer with their own accounts, investments, policies and returns; the family view adds them up; and you set, per member, who sees and does what.

### How it works

-   **Add a member** with name, relationship and PAN, and invite them by email or phone if they want their own login. Members without a login, such as young children or elderly parents, are managed by you as guardian or with their consent.

-   **Documents route themselves:** the name and PAN on a statement, policy or Form 16 decide whose it is.

-   **Family Home:** net worth by member and in total, everyone\'s dues and renewals in one calendar, family insurance cover, and family to-dos.

-   **Money between members:** gifts, loans and shared expenses are recorded on both sides and appear in Who owes whom. Gift and income-clubbing rules from the rules library are flagged for your CA.

-   **Each member\'s tax year** stays separate: their own AIS check, computation and return.

### Access per member

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Level            What the person can do
  ---------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Manage           See and do everything for that member, as you would for a child or a parent you look after

  Contribute       Upload documents and answer their own to-dos; see only their own accounts

  View             See the accounts shared with them; change nothing

  Upload only      Send documents through Add or an upload link; see nothing else

  Private          Keep an account or document hidden from everyone else, including the family view
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Consent and changes

-   An adult member\'s financial data is theirs. They accept the invitation, choose what to share with the family view, and can withdraw it later, as DPDP requires.

-   A minor\'s data is handled by a parent or guardian with verifiable parental consent. At 18, Thapal tells the member and hands control to them.

-   Every grant, change and revocation is logged, and the monthly access review covers family members too.

## Automation and trust policy

Thapal does the work by default, asks when it is unsure, and never acts outside the app on its own. How much it posts without asking grows only as measured accuracy grows.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Level                                           What happens                                                               Examples
  ----------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Always automatic                                Done silently; visible in History                                          Reading and filing documents, duplicate detection, balance recalculation, reminders, refreshing prices, preparing draft invoices from recurring templates, preparing GST and TDS working papers

  Automatic once you have confirmed the pattern   Posted, then listed in a daily \"Done for you\" digest with one-tap undo   A repeat merchant and category you confirmed at least 3 times without correction, under your limit (suggested ₹5,000 personal), in an open month. **Off until accuracy is measured**

  Asks you (To-do)                                Suggested answer pre-selected; nothing changes until you confirm           New payee, unsure category, one-sided transfer after 5 days, amount mismatch, capital versus expense, anything that changes tax treatment, related-party items, amounts above your limit

  Needs an approval                               Routed to the role that can approve                                        Journals, month close and reopen, bulk changes to history, invoice cancellation, writing off dues, company master changes, access grants

  Never automatic                                 Thapal prepares; a person acts outside the app                             Filing any return, paying anyone, cancelling subscriptions, changing bank mandates, deleting history, publishing an app release
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Autopilot setting (per workspace)

-   **Ask me about everything** --- the default until accuracy is proven on your documents.

-   **Ask only when unsure** --- confident items post; unsure ones go to To-do.

-   **Autopilot for routine** --- adds confirmed patterns under the limit.

A document type unlocks the second and third settings only after its measured accuracy passes the bar KK sets (see Decisions). Suggested bar: 99.5% on amounts and dates, 97% on category, per issuer, on at least 200 real rows.

### How confidence is shown

-   Laypeople see three words: **Sure**, **Check this**, **Needs you**. Each has a \"Why?\" that shows the evidence (\"Same amount and date as your HDFC debit; reference matches\").

-   Accountants and auditors also see the score, the rule or model version, and the matching evidence.

### Undo

Every automatic posting is reversible with a source-preserving reversal. The undo bar appears after every action. Undo is blocked only in a locked month, where it becomes a correcting entry for the accountant to approve.

### The 99.9% target (revision 3)

The goal is that 999 of every 1,000 documents and transactions are read, mapped, posted and filed with no human touch. It is reached in steps, because automation that guesses wrong creates more work than it saves.

**How it is measured (shown in Health check, per document type and month):**

-   **Touch-free rate:** items processed with no human action, divided by all items.

-   **Correction rate:** items changed after posting. This must stay below 0.1%, or automation for that type steps back a level by itself.

**What gets it there:**

1.  Fixed readers for each bank\'s statement formats, which are close to exact.

2.  Email forwarding of statements, alerts, tickets and bills, so nothing needs uploading.

3.  Standing rules: \"paid by, belongs to\", merchant to category, entity to trip.

4.  Learning from every correction, per merchant and per entity.

5.  The statement as final proof: a receipt\'s guessed card is confirmed silently when the statement row arrives.

6.  Grouped questions: one tap answers twenty similar items.

**Indicative targets, not promises:** about 80% touch-free in the first month of real use, 95% by month three, 99% by month six, and 99.9% once standing rules cover the group\'s repeating patterns.

**What stays human, as one tap each, and is counted as an approval rather than a failure:** OTP, e-verification or digital signature on government portals; approving a payment in your bank; approving a filing or a month lock; and answering a genuinely new situation, such as a first payment to a new person.

## Architecture: one ledger behind every module (revision 9)

Thapal is one integrated financial platform: every module reads from and posts through a single central ledger. So a ₹50,000 company expense paid on your personal card shows correctly in your card, the company\'s spending, the trip, the claim and the company\'s payable to you, and is still one expense.

![architecture · 6 modules around one central ledger](media/image3.png){width="6.0in" height="3.4821423884514435in"}

architecture · 6 modules around one central ledger

Modules keep the detail a person needs (a trip\'s itinerary, an asset\'s location, a holding\'s tax lots), but no module keeps a balance of its own: its totals are ledger lines tagged with its permanent ID.

### The chain every record follows

Legal entity → financial account → source document → financial event → accounting entry → reconciliation → reports → calendar and reminders → audit evidence. One economic event may appear in several modules; it has only one accounting effect.

### Kept, not rebuilt

Existing records and history; personal, family and company workspaces; Statement Desk as the one document intake; accounting and reconciliation; the document repository and evidence history; reports and settings; permissions; approval and release controls. There is no parallel financial engine and no second accounting database.

### What every financial record knows

Legal owner; accounting entity; paying entity; beneficiary entity where different; financial account; ledger account; source evidence; accounting entry; reconciliation status; approval history. Anything unknown stays visibly unresolved, never guessed.

### Permanent identities

Entity, user, financial account, transaction or event, document, accounting entry, expense, reimbursement, trip, asset, property, investment, loan, tax working, calendar event and report each have a stable ID (formats in Permanent IDs). Existing IDs are reused where they already qualify.

### Safeguards

One controlled posting function; balanced entries; no duplicate effects; immutable posted history; locked periods; reversal-based corrections; exact decimal amounts, never floating point; entity-level permissions; append-only audit evidence.

This is the connection map Lovable builds from. For every module it says where data comes in, which existing parts it reuses, what it posts or settles in the ledger, what it is matched with, and what happens when something is missing. It is written at the logical level; the real table and function names are filled in from the repository in Gate 1 (see Delivery gates), never assumed.

### The mandatory rule

No module is built as a separate financial system: not Investments, Net worth, Tax, Assets, Property, Travel or any other. Every module posts only through the one posting function and reads the same account balances. Each record carries its permanent ID, legal owner, ledger mapping, payment and bank links, source reference, accounting entry ID and reconciliation status, and obeys period locks and the reversal rules.

### What each module\'s blueprint page holds

Gate 1 produces one page per module under ten headings: entry point; existing components reused; database relationships; accounting rules (what creates, updates or reverses entries); automatic matching; navigation; reports that update; permissions; exceptions; and the acceptance tests that prove the linked figures agree.

### Three worked flows

**Share purchase.** A demat statement and a bank statement both show a purchase of 100 shares. Statement Desk reads both, identifies the owner and demat account, and matches the bank debit to the holding. One entry posts, Dr Investments · Cr Bank; Investment Manager, net worth and reports all read it. The second document links to that entry instead of posting again.

**Rent received.** ₹85,000 reaches Company A\'s bank. Thapal identifies the tenant and property and settles the rent receivable raised by that month\'s invoice (or recognises the income, where the policy uses no invoice). It records the TDS the tenant deducted as a tax credit to be matched in the government tax statement, then updates Property Manager, the tax working and reports.

**GST paid.** November\'s GST working shows ₹2,40,000 payable after input credit. Thapal posts the set-off of input credit against output tax, leaving GST payable, and prepares the challan details. When the bank debit and challan match, it posts Dr GST payable · Cr Bank. The payment settles a liability and is never another expense; the compliance status moves to Paid only on that evidence.

### Moving both ways

Every financial detail has **Open accounting entry** where one exists, and every accounting entry has **Open source document**. Back keeps context and filters.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Starting point                 One tap to
  ------------------------------ ----------------------------------------------------------
  An investment                  Transactions, bank link, holdings, gains, tax, reports

  A loan                         Repayments, bank link, interest, liability, reports

  A property                     Owner, books, tenant, rent, bank, tax, reports

  An asset                       Owner, books, invoice, payment, depreciation, reports

  A trip                         Expenses, cards, accounts, claims, books

  A company                      Books, tax, compliance, assets, properties, reports

  A document in Statement Desk   Source, classification, accounting entry, reconciliation

  A report                       Source records, reconciliation, evidence
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Reading quality and safe reprocessing (revision 9)

The 99.9% target is proven field by field, never claimed as one number. Thapal measures how well it reads each kind of document and field, sets how much to automate from that measure, and can re-read old documents with a better engine without ever posting twice. This extends The 99.9% target and How confidence works above.

### Sixteen separate measures

Document type · entity · account or card · merchant · date · amount · currency · tax · category · duplicate detection · bank matching · reimbursement detection · investment holdings · asset-register rows · property documents · accounting classification. Each is measured per issuer (HDFC, Amex, Lulu) and per document type, so one overall figure never hides a weak field.

### Three confidence bands

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Band         What happens
  ------------ -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  High         Supported by evidence and passes every control; posts under your autopilot setting for that document type

  Medium       Prepared as a suggestion for one-tap review

  Low          Asks for clarification or another document
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Thresholds come from real error rates on real documents, per issuer, and move only with evidence.

### The test set

Real documents: different banks and card issuers, Indian and foreign invoices, scans, poor phone photos, multi-page documents, varied spreadsheet layouts, several entities and several currencies. The expected answers are stored apart from the engine under test, so the engine never marks its own work.

### Learning from corrections

A correction you make is kept as an approved example for future reading; it never silently rewrites history. Merchant rules and issuer mappings are versioned and can be rolled back.

### Re-reading an old document

Allowed when the reader improves, an error is found, new information arrives or a rule changes. Thapal then:

1.  Keeps the original document and every earlier reading.

2.  Reads it again and shows old and new side by side.

3.  Lists the money consequences: which entries would change.

4.  Changes nothing posted without your approval, and then only by reversal and re-posting.

5.  Never creates a duplicate entry.

6.  Records every step in the audit trail.

### Document trail

Each document carries its life story: uploaded → read (engine and version) → classified → posted (entry IDs) → reconciled → reported. From any figure in a report you can walk back to the page it came from.

### Automation Quality Dashboard

Documents processed, classified, reconciled, waiting for review and failed; accuracy by field, issuer and type; exception and correction rates; duplicate-detection and wrong-match rates; average processing time; automation rate and human-touch rate; documents re-read and the money corrections they caused.

A feature counts as automation-complete only when real-document tests exist, accuracy is measured, errors are handled, retries are safe, duplicates are prevented, totals stay correct and corrections can be undone.

## Add and Documents

One Add button covers every way of getting information in; the existing Statement Desk engine does all the work behind it, and Documents keeps every original for good.

### Ways in (all land in the same engine)

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Way in                             Notes
  ---------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Scan with camera                   Multi-page, auto-crop, batch mode for a pile of receipts. The image appears immediately (fixes the missing-preview complaint)

  Upload a file                      PDF, image, CSV, XLSX, and JSON files such as GSTR-2B or AIS downloads

  Forward by email **(new in v2)**   Each workspace gets a private address, for example kk-7f3a@in.thapal.in. Forward e-statements, bills and invoices. Only allowlisted senders are accepted. Needs an inbound-mail service, which is paid infrastructure awaiting approval

  Share from another app             Works for installed web apps on Android. On iPhone it needs a thin native wrapper; email forwarding covers the gap until then

  Bulk upload                        A folder or ZIP of past statements for onboarding (April 2026 onward)

  Create                             Sales invoice, quotation, credit note, payment receipt, expense claim, cash entry; manual journal for accountants
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Password-protected PDFs: ask once per issuer. With consent, the password is stored encrypted for that issuer and can be forgotten at any time. The keyboard never opens by itself.

### What happens after Add

1.  **Received.** The original is stored privately and fingerprinted. A repeat upload is caught: \"You added this on 3 Nov. Skip it?\"

2.  **Recognised.** Document type, issuer, period, account, workspace and company are identified.

3.  **Read.** Figures, dates, line items and identifiers are extracted; the printed value and any corrected reading are kept together.

4.  **Checked.** Opening plus movements must equal closing; pages, periods and gaps are checked.

5.  **Matched.** Against prior statements, existing transactions and other documents (a receipt to its bank debit, a card payment to its statement).

6.  **Proposed.** One sentence states the effect: \"Adds 142 transactions to HDFC Savings for October. 9 need you.\"

7.  **Applied once.** Posted atomically with evidence links, or held in To-do. Balances update.

The user sees one progress card (\"Reading... Checking... Done: 133 added, 9 need you\") and can leave the screen. Long imports keep running and resume after a network drop.

### Review (formerly Intelligent Canvas)

The original on the left; \"What we understood\" on the right, as sentences first and fields second. Disagreements are highlighted on the image. Four actions: **Looks right**, **Fix**, **Not mine**, **Ask my accountant**. On iPhone the two halves stack, with a tap to flip between them.

### Documents Thapal should read (phased)

-   **Banking:** bank and card statements, FD advices and interest certificates, loan statements and repayment schedules.

-   **Investments:** NSDL or CDSL consolidated account statements (demat and mutual funds together), CAMS or KFintech mutual-fund statements, broker statements and contract notes (ICICI Direct first), EPF passbook, PPF and NPS statements.

-   **Tax:** AIS, TIS, Form 26AS, Form 16 and 16A, GST returns and GSTR-2B, tax challans and filing acknowledgements.

-   **Business:** sales and purchase invoices, receipts, salary registers, company documents (incorporation certificate, MOA and AOA, PAN, TAN, GST certificate, MCA master data), audited financial statements.

-   **Wealth and life:** insurance policies and premium receipts, property deeds, leases, property-tax receipts, forex card statements and remittance advices, utility bills.

### Documents (in Records)

-   Originals are private, never overwritten, and versioned. Names are automatic: \"2026-10 HDFC Savings statement.pdf\".

-   Each document lists where it is used: \"Used in 142 transactions, October GST working, FY 2026-27 audit pack.\"

-   Search by text, amount, date, party or account. Folders are automatic views by workspace, year and type, plus a \"Tax year 2026-27\" pack.

-   Documents behind filed returns, closed months and audit packs are locked. Replacing one keeps the earlier original and the reason.

-   Missing-document requests go to staff, vendors or the accountant as an upload-only link that expires and is rate-limited.

-   Expiry reminders for insurance, leases, licences and directors\' digital signature certificates.

-   Retention periods come from the rules library (for example, eight years for company books). A ZIP export carries a manifest with file hashes.

-   **Statement gaps:** Thapal learns each account\'s statement cycle and raises \"HDFC Savings: October statement missing\" with the forwarding address as the quickest fix.

### Vault: finding any record in two taps (revision 3)

-   **One search box across every entity:** type words, an amount, a date, a vendor, a GSTIN, a PNR or an invoice number. Each result shows a thumbnail, its entity and what it is linked to.

-   **Smart folders that maintain themselves:** by entity, then year, then type; by trip; by bank account (statements by month, gaps marked); by tax year (everything a return needs); by asset (deed, encumbrance certificate, tax receipts, insurance); by person (Form 16, policies, certificates).

-   **Packs:** select any set (a trip, a quarter\'s GST invoices, an audit sample, a loan application) and export one PDF or ZIP with an index, or share it by an expiring link.

-   **Every document has an action menu:** view, download original, share, move to another entity, link to a record, replace (the earlier version is kept), request a missing one, delete (only if nothing uses it; otherwise it is archived with a reason).

-   **Starred documents** are kept available offline where the device allows.

-   **Professionals** see only the folders of the entities you have granted them.

## Bring in your history: previous returns and regulatory documents (revision 3)

Upload or forward your past filings once. Thapal files each under the right person, company or trust and year, then uses them to fill this year\'s work.

### What you can bring

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Area                           Documents
  ------------------------------ -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Income tax                     Past returns (the portal\'s JSON and PDF), acknowledgements, computations, Form 16 and 16A, Form 26AS, AIS and TIS, tax audit reports, intimations, assessment and appeal orders, notices and replies

  GST                            Registration certificates, past monthly and annual returns, GSTR-2B, cash and credit ledger extracts, e-way bills, notices and orders

  TDS and TCS                    Quarterly statements, challans, certificates issued and received

  PF, ESI, professional tax      Registrations, ECR and contribution challans, returns

  Companies                      Incorporation documents, MCA master data, past AOC-4 and MGT-7 filings with SRNs, statutory registers, minutes, audited financial statements

  Trusts                         Trust deed and amendments, registration and 80G approval orders, past audit reports and returns, donation statements, FCRA papers if any

  Loans, property, investments   Sanction letters, repayment schedules, deeds, encumbrance certificates, CAS and broker statements, deposit advices, insurance policies
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### What Thapal does with them

1.  **Files** each document under its entity and year, named and searchable in the Vault.

2.  **Builds the entity profile:** PAN, TAN, GSTINs, CIN, registration numbers, addresses, tax regime, filing frequency.

3.  **Carries figures forward:** losses and unabsorbed depreciation, tax-depreciation block values, tax credits carried forward, GST credit balances, and opening balances from the last audited accounts. Each figure links to the page it came from.

4.  **Builds the compliance calendar** from past filing dates, frequencies and registrations.

5.  **Opens a notices tracker:** each notice or order with its reply deadline, documents and status, with reminders until it is closed.

6.  **Pre-fills this year\'s drafts:** returns, the trusts\' donation statements and the companies\' annual filings, with last year\'s figures as the comparison column.

7.  **Finds gaps:** \"No GST return found for Company C for August 2026\"; \"Trust 2\'s 80G approval expires in March 2027; renewal is due six months before.\"

Every extracted figure arrives as a proposal with its source page beside it. You, or your CA, confirm the carry-forward figures once per entity.

### Fetching from government portals

With your consent, Thapal can fetch your own data where an approved channel exists, through a registered intermediary: AIS, Form 26AS and pre-filled return data from the income-tax portal; returns and GSTR-2B from the GST portal. This arrives in phase 5 (decision 3). Until then, one download on the portal and one forward to Thapal does the rest.

## Upload requests: scheduled links that collect documents for you (revision 4)

Name a person and a schedule once. Thapal then emails them a secure upload link every period, listing exactly what is still missing, and keeps reminding until everything has arrived.

### Setting one up, once

-   **Who:** the name and email of your preferred person, such as your accountant, an office staff member or a family member. You can have several, one per company or trust. WhatsApp delivery is optional and needs the paid WhatsApp business service (decision 6).

-   **What:** the accounts, cards and documents they look after, for example \"Company A\'s three bank accounts and two cards, GST returns and the salary register\".

-   **When:** monthly on a day you choose, quarterly, yearly (interest certificates and Form 16 each April), or when something happens (a trip ends, a project bill falls due).

### What the person receives

A short email: \"Thapal needs 6 documents for Company A for October. Upload them here.\" The link opens a simple page that needs no login:

-   the checklist of what is needed, ticking itself as files arrive;

-   drag and drop, or the phone camera; one file, a whole folder or a ZIP;

-   an instant check of each file: \"This is September\'s statement; October is needed\", \"Already received\", \"Password-protected: enter the password once\";

-   a summary when everything is in.

### Safe by design

-   **Upload only:** the person sees nothing in Thapal except that request\'s checklist.

-   **Scoped and expiring:** each link belongs to one person and one request, and expires when complete or after the days you set. Revoke any link from its action menu.

-   **Optional one-time code** to the person\'s email or phone before uploading.

-   Size and type limits, malware scanning, and a record of who uploaded what and when.

### What happens next

-   Every file goes straight into the Add engine, tagged \"Received through upload request from (person)\", and is read, matched and posted like anything you upload yourself.

-   Reminders go out after 3 and 5 days. After 7 days you get a To-do item: \"Trust 2\'s SBI statement for October is still missing.\"

-   **Standing drop link:** a permanent, revocable link per person for documents outside the schedule.

-   Each request fills itself from what Thapal knows (statement cycles, filing calendars and gaps it has found), so it always lists what is actually missing. The forward-by-email address still works for anyone who prefers it.

## Getting documents in: automatic email fetching, uploading anywhere, and multi-page documents (revision 6)

Most financial documents already reach a mailbox. Thapal collects them by itself, and wherever you do upload, you can pick many files or whole folders at once. A receipt that runs to two pages is read and kept as one document.

### Automatic email fetching

Two routes, which can run together: forwarding for day one, the direct connection once Google approves it.

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                    Forwarding rules                                                                                                             Direct mailbox connection
  ----------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  How it works      A wizard creates filters in Gmail or Outlook once; matching mail is forwarded to your private Thapal address automatically   You connect the mailbox with read-only permission; Thapal checks it every few minutes

  What it reads     Only mail your filters send                                                                                                  Only mail from known financial senders (banks, card issuers, airlines, hotels, insurers, tax portals, your vendors). Everything else is skipped and never stored

  Past mail         New mail only                                                                                                                Back to 1 April 2026 in one sweep

  Approval needed   None                                                                                                                         For Gmail, Google\'s restricted-scope verification and a security assessment, because Thapal\'s server stores the attachments ([Google](https://developers.google.com/workspace/gmail/api/auth/scopes)). Outlook and Microsoft 365 need their own app consent

  Ready in          Phase 1                                                                                                                      Apply in Phase 0, so approval can arrive by Phase 1 or 2
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   **Several mailboxes:** your personal Gmail, each company\'s and trust\'s mailbox, and your accountant\'s if they agree. Each mailbox has an owner and routes documents to the right entity.

-   **Other providers:** Zoho, company mail servers and others through IMAP, with an app password where the provider allows it.

-   **Password-protected attachments** open with the saved password for that issuer, with your consent.

-   **Mails with a link instead of an attachment** (some banks and portals send these) appear as \"Download needed\", one tap from the original link, because Thapal never signs in to a bank for you.

-   **New senders** are asked about once: \"Always fetch from billing@example.com?\"

-   **Hands off your mailbox:** nothing is sent, deleted or marked. Disconnect at any time; documents already fetched stay in the Vault.

### Uploading anywhere: files, folders, many at once

One upload component, identical on every screen that accepts a document: Add, a trip, a project, an asset, a property, a loan, a filing, a To-do item and every upload-request page.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Device               What you can pick
  -------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  iPhone and iPad      Camera with multi-page scanning; many photos at once; many files at once from the Files app, including iCloud Drive, Google Drive and OneDrive; a ZIP; drag and drop between apps on iPad; paste a screenshot

  Android              Camera with multi-page scanning; many photos or files at once, including cloud drives; a ZIP

  Computer             Many files at once; whole folders including subfolders; drag and drop of files and folders; a ZIP; paste
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Phone browsers do not offer a whole-folder picker, so on a phone you select every file inside the folder, or send a ZIP; on a computer you pick the folder itself.

-   **Multi-select everywhere,** with a count and total size before sending, and a cross to remove any file.

-   **Big batches** of hundreds of files upload in the background, resume after a network drop, and show progress per file while you keep working.

-   **Every common type:** PDF (scanned or password-protected), JPG, PNG, HEIC iPhone photos, Excel, CSV, Word, JSON, ZIP, and saved email files, which are unpacked.

-   **Duplicates** are recognised by fingerprint and skipped with a note.

-   **Context sticks:** a file uploaded inside a trip, project, asset or property is tagged to it automatically.

### One document, many pages

-   **Scanning:** camera mode keeps adding pages to the same document until you tap Done. Reorder, retake or delete pages before saving.

-   **Joining:** separate photos of one receipt are joined automatically when they share merchant, invoice number and date, or when page 1 has no total and page 2 carries it. You can also select pages and tap Combine.

-   **Splitting:** a PDF holding many receipts or invoices is split at each new invoice number or merchant. A 40-page bank statement stays one statement.

-   **Long documents** such as a 300-page statement or a 120-page contractor bill are read page by page in the background, with totals checked across pages: balances carried forward, page subtotals and the grand total.

-   **Many-to-many links:** one invoice can be settled by three payments, and one payment can carry an invoice, a receipt, a delivery note and a photo. Both directions show on the transaction.

-   **Page actions** in the document\'s menu: add page, remove page, rotate, split, combine, replace, and download as one PDF.

## Expense management: scan once, mapped automatically (revision 3)

Snap one receipt or a stack of fifty. Thapal reads each one, picks the category, finds which card or account paid, decides whom it belongs to, and links it to the statement row when that arrives.

### Capture

-   **Single or batch:** camera batch mode, several receipts in one photo split automatically, multiple photos or PDFs at once, or forwarded email.

-   **Offline:** receipts captured without signal queue on the phone and upload later.

-   **Any language or currency:** amount, currency and date are read from foreign receipts too.

### What is read from each receipt

Merchant and its GSTIN, your GSTIN if printed, date, time and place, total, CGST, SGST or IGST, currency, line items, invoice number, and the payment line (\"VISA \*\*\*\*4417\", \"AMEX XX1004\", \"UPI Ref 4123...\", \"CASH\").

### How the paying card or account is found

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Evidence on the receipt               Mapped to                                                   Shown as
  ------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------- ----------
  Card last four digits                 That card in your directory                                 Sure

  UPI reference or UPI ID               The bank account behind that UPI ID                         Sure

  \"Cash\"                              The cash wallet of whoever paid (trip cash or petty cash)   Sure

  Card network only, such as \"AMEX\"   Your only Amex, or the card usually used on this trip       Check

  Foreign currency, no card printed     Your forex card in that currency                            Check

  Nothing printed                       Predicted from merchant, place, trip and history            Check
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**The statement is the final proof.** When the card or bank statement arrives, the receipt is linked to its exact row. A wrong guess is corrected silently and logged. You are asked only when two rows could both match.

### Category, entity and GST

-   **Category** comes from merchant type, items, history and your rules, using the right list for each entity: expense heads for a company, object-wise heads for a trust, household categories for you.

-   **Entity** comes from the paying instrument, the trip, the GSTIN printed as buyer, the place and your standing rules.

-   **GST:** marked claimable only when the bill is a valid tax invoice carrying that entity\'s GSTIN. During an active trip, a bill without your GSTIN prompts: \"Ask the hotel to reissue with Company A\'s GSTIN.\"

-   **Split** any expense by percentage or amount between entities, or between business and personal.

### Review only when needed

A batch ends with one line: \"48 receipts read. 45 filed. 3 need you: two have no total; one could be either card.\" Expense lists can be viewed by day, trip, entity or card, with filters and selected totals.

### After posting

-   **Receipt with no payment found** after the statement period becomes a To-do item (perhaps paid by someone else, or in cash).

-   **Payment with no receipt:** each card shows \"6 rows on the Amex statement have no receipt\", so you can snap or forward them. Company expenses above your threshold without a receipt are flagged for audit.

-   **Reimbursements** are created automatically when you paid for a company or trust (see Your group).

-   **Spending policies** per entity (for example, hotel per night) flag an item; they never block it. You decide.

## One expense, every view (revision 8)

Every expense is stored once, with its evidence, and every view is a filter on that one record. Nineteen views and every expense report read the same rows, so a total never differs between screens and nothing is counted twice. Revision 8 extends Expense management above; it adds no second ledger.

### Every way in

All of these go through the same intake as Add and Documents, with no module to choose first.

-   **Photos:** one receipt, several receipts in one photo, a receipt of many pages.

-   **Files:** one or many PDFs, a ZIP, a folder on a computer, supplier invoices, tickets and travel bills.

-   **Statements:** bank, credit-card and debit-card statements, and UPI history.

-   **Forwarded:** emailed invoices and bookings; WhatsApp forwards once that channel is approved (see Notifications and reminders).

-   **Typed or spoken:** cash spends, recurring bills, and a spend with no receipt (a short declaration, flagged for review, capped by policy).

Thapal decides what each item is: a new expense, a match to an existing one, a refund, a card-bill payment, or a duplicate to skip.

### What is read

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Group       Fields read
  ----------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Money       Merchant or supplier, invoice number, date and time, total, currency, rate, taxable value, GST and other taxes, discount, tip, service charge, line items, paid, refunded or cancelled

  Who         Who spent, who paid, whom it belongs to, and the instrument: bank account, credit, debit or forex card, UPI ID, cash wallet

  Why         Category, trip, project, company or trust, department, cost centre, activity or event, client, asset, reimbursable or not
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Links come from the document, the statement, past choices for that merchant and the trip calendar. Anything uncertain goes to To-do; nothing uncertain is posted silently.

### The views

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Looking by             Views                                                                             Typical question
  ---------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------
  Who paid               Card, Account, Person (payer)                                                     What did the Amex pay for in October?

  Whose it is            Company, Trust, Family, Person (spender)                                          What did Company A spend this quarter?

  What for               Category, Merchant, Project, Department or cost centre, Activity or event, Trip   What did the villa project cost this month?

  When and in what       Date (day to year), Currency, Tax (GST credit, no credit, TDS)                    How much was spent abroad this year?

  Paperwork and status   Receipt, Evidence, Payment status, Reimbursement                                  Which spends have no receipt?
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every view has search, filters, sort, multi-select and one download menu, which produces the Detailed Expenditure Statement with that view as its context.

### Counting rules

1.  A card purchase books the expense (or asset) and the card liability. Paying the card bill settles the liability and never creates a second expense.

2.  Transfers between own accounts, loan principal, investments, tax payments, advances, reimbursement settlements and cash withdrawals are money moved, not spent. Account views list them under **Moved, not spent**.

3.  A split expense shows in each owner\'s view at its share only; group totals add each share once.

4.  Re-uploading a receipt or statement matches the existing record and never adds a row.

5.  A correction is a reversal plus a new entry. Every view and report updates, and the old version stays in History.

### Splits and matching

-   Split one bill across people, entities or categories: equal, percentage, fixed amount or item by item; personal and business portions kept apart.

-   One payment across several invoices; one invoice across several part-payments; several receipts against one consolidated card charge.

-   Partial refunds and reversals link to the original; disputed card charges stay tracked until resolved.

-   Spent in one currency and settled in another: both amounts kept, with the source of the rate.

-   Paid with another person\'s card or from an advance: the payer is recorded and the right person is owed.

-   A receipt can arrive later; the expense waits as **receipt to follow**.

### Bulk actions

Select all, or by date range, card, account, trip, category, merchant, entity or reimbursement status. Then categorise, assign a trip or entity, prepare claims, request documents or run a report. Every bulk change previews the count and money affected, checks permissions, and undoes as one step.

### Analysis

Trends by day, week, month and year; top categories and merchants; unusual or repeated spends; subscriptions and price rises; budget overruns; missing receipts; unclaimed reimbursements; unsettled advances; possible duplicates; and forex conversion costs. Forecasts of recurring spend show the past payments and the assumption behind each figure.

### Expense detail

One screen answers: what was bought, when, how much, who paid, with which account or card, whom it belongs to, which trip or project, whether it is reimbursable and settled, whether it matches the statement, and the original documents. Each answer is a link to the receipt, statement row, trip, entity, merchant, category, project, claim, accounting entry or report. Back returns to where you came from, with filters intact.

## The Detailed Expenditure Statement (revision 8)

Every expense report in Thapal is one statement in one format. Open it from a trip, project, card, account, company, trust, person or family: the layout stays the same and only the context line and filters change. Accountants, approvers and you read every statement the same way, and one engine is far easier to test than a hundred report designs.

### What it contains, in order

1.  **Header:** report number (for example DES-2026-0187), version, date and time generated, prepared by, approved by, the entity\'s letterhead, the context (\"Trip TRP-2026-0042 · Dubai business visit\") and every filter used, in words.

2.  **Summary:** total; by category; by payment method; by entity; reimbursable versus personal; advances; already reimbursed; balance payable or recoverable.

3.  **Detail:** one row per expense line with date, description and merchant, category, spender, payer and instrument, belongs to, trip or project, original currency and amount, rate and its source, rupee amount, GST credit or not, reimbursement status and evidence reference.

4.  **Exceptions:** missing receipts, unmatched card or bank rows, possible duplicates, policy exceptions.

5.  **Approvals and settlement:** shown when the context includes a claim.

6.  **Evidence index:** every row\'s receipt, ticket or invoice with its page in the pack.

7.  **Receipt pages:** the soft copy of every receipt, ticket and invoice is printed inside the statement, after the evidence index, in the same order as the detail rows, two to four to a page.

    -   Placed by shape: small slips (till receipts, card slips) four to a page in a 2 × 2 grid; long receipts three to a page, side by side; full-page invoices and tickets two to a page, one above the other. Mixed sizes are combined to fill each page, never fewer than two except on the last page.

    -   Each copy carries a label with its row number, date, merchant, amount and evidence ID, so it matches its row and the evidence index.

    -   Copies are straightened, cropped and turned upright for printing and must stay readable on printed A4; the untouched original stays in the Document Repository. A multi-page invoice shows each page as its own labelled copy (page 1 of 3).

    -   A missing receipt gets a \"Receipt missing\" box in its place, matching the exceptions list.

    -   On by default in the PDF; the export dialog can switch it off for a summary-only copy. Excel and CSV exports carry a link column and the evidence ZIP instead. Any redaction chosen at export also applies to the receipt copies.

### Formats

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Format   For                                 Holds
  -------- ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  PDF      Submission and printing             All six parts, letterhead, page-numbered evidence index

  Excel    Accountant review                   Summary, detail with formulas, rate workings, exceptions

  CSV      Import elsewhere, including Tally   One row per expense line, with permanent IDs

  ZIP      Auditor or approver                 The PDF, the Excel and every original document, named by evidence reference
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

All four come from one saved report run, so their totals always match. Re-issuing version 1 later reproduces it exactly, even after corrections; a corrected statement becomes version 2 with its changes listed.

### Context and filters

Contexts: one or several trips, project, card, account, company, trust, person, family, category, merchant, department, activity, or a date range. Filters combine freely and are printed on the statement. Examples: Amex spends during the Dubai trip; Company A expenses paid from personal accounts; unreimbursed expenses for 2026-27; hotel spends across all trips; spends above ₹50,000; foreign-currency spends on one card.

### Named reports become presets

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  You asked for                                                                                                                           Produced as
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  Trip expenditure, budget versus actual, daily, category, traveller, card, account and foreign-currency trip reports, missing receipts   The statement with a trip context and a saved grouping

  The 15 card reports and 13 account reports                                                                                              The statement with a card or account context

  Company, trust, person, family, project, department, cost-centre, activity, category, merchant and daily-to-annual expenditure          The statement with that context and period

  Reimbursable, pending, settled, GST-related, cash, recurring, unmatched, duplicate, approval-history and correction-history reports     The statement with a status filter

  Professional travel expenditure statement for a finance department                                                                      The statement with a trip context and that organisation\'s template
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Reports that are not lists of spending keep their own layout on the same data: claim and settlement, advance settlement, group settlement, trip-to-ledger and card reconciliations, asset and property registers, and calendar and notification reports.

### Packs, one tap each

-   **Receipt Evidence Pack:** PDF and ZIP.

-   **Trip Pack:** summary, itinerary, tickets, boarding passes, hotel invoices, other bookings, receipt register and originals, the statement, card and account split, forex workings, advances, claims, settlements, refunds, insurance, missing-document schedule and evidence index; PDF, Excel, CSV and ZIP.

-   **Reimbursement Claim Pack:** claim, approvals, settlement and evidence; PDF, Excel and ZIP.

-   **Monthly and Annual Expense Packs:** by category, person, card, account, trip, project and entity, with missing receipts, reconciliation and claim status; PDF, Excel and ZIP.

Scheduled statements, such as one every month to your CA, use the same engine and follow the sharing rules in Roles.

## Reimbursements (revision 8)

A claim is prepared automatically whenever the payer and the owner of an expense differ, and it closes only when the bank statement shows the money. A reimbursement is never counted as spending: it settles what one party owes another.

### When Thapal proposes a claim

-   Your personal card pays a company or trust expense.

-   An employee pays an official expense.

-   One entity pays for another, or for a project another entity funds.
