-   A traveller pays for several organisations or for other travellers.

-   An advance was given and now has to be adjusted.

Already-reimbursed and non-reimbursable expenses are left out automatically, and one receipt can never sit on two claims.

### The claim

It names the claimant, the payer, the reimbursing organisation and the trip or project. Each line has the date, description, original currency and amount, rate and its source, eligible amount and receipt. Then come advances given, amounts already reimbursed, balance outstanding, policy exceptions and approval status. It prints as the Detailed Expenditure Statement with a claim context.

### From draft to settled

1.  Eligible expenses are found and grouped into a draft claim.

2.  Evidence is attached and policy is checked: limits per category, and per-diem and mileage rates where the entity has set them. Exceptions are flagged, not blocked.

3.  You or the claimant submit; the entity\'s approvers act in the order its rule sets, one or several.

4.  Approval, part-approval or rejection is recorded with the reason.

5.  The payout is matched from the bank statement; part-payments are allowed.

6.  The claim closes only once settlement is verified, and balances update everywhere.

Statuses: Identified · Draft · Ready for review · Submitted · Part-approved · Approved · Rejected · Part-settled · Settled · Cancelled · Disputed. A claim approved but unpaid after 30 days goes to To-do and the calendar.

### The accounting

Example: a ₹18,400 Company A hotel bill paid on your personal Amex.

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Event                      Company A\'s books                              Your books
  -------------------------- ----------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------
  Hotel recorded             Dr Travel -- accommodation · Cr Payable to KK   Dr Receivable from Company A · Cr Amex card

  You pay the Amex bill      No entry                                        Dr Amex card · Cr HDFC Savings

  Company A reimburses you   Dr Payable to KK · Cr Company A bank            Dr HDFC Savings · Cr Receivable from Company A
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The expense exists once, in Company A\'s books. An advance works the same way: Company A records an advance to you, your spends reduce it, and the balance is returned or paid.

### Reports

Claim; by claimant, employee, company, trust, trip, project, category, card and account; pending; approved but unpaid; part-settled; rejected; ageing; approval history; advances versus expenses; settlement statement; evidence pack; annual summary. All come in PDF, Excel and CSV, and packs as ZIP. Most are the Detailed Expenditure Statement with a claim filter; the claim and the settlement statement have their own layout.

## Travel: automatic trips and the Trip Pack (revision 3)

Forward your booking emails and snap receipts as you go. Thapal builds each trip by itself and, at the end, produces one Trip Pack holding every ticket, boarding pass, booking, expense, photo and claim.

### A trip builds itself

-   **Started by** a forwarded flight or train ticket or hotel booking, or by card spending in another city or country, or a forex card load.

-   **Itinerary assembled automatically:** flights (PNR, flight number, times), trains, hotels (check-in and check-out), cabs, visa, travel insurance, forex loads.

-   **Everything inside the trip\'s dates and places attaches itself:** receipts, card rows, cash and forex spends.

-   **One question at the start:** \"Who is this trip for?\" You, Company A, Trust 2, or a split by days or percentage. Your standing rules pre-fill it.

-   **Billing card before you leave:** each entity\'s legal name, GSTIN and address on one screen, to give hotels and airlines so invoices come in the right name and GST can be claimed.

-   **During the trip,** a card on Home shows budget against spent, cash and forex left, and missing evidence: \"Boarding pass for 6E 2134 not added yet.\"

-   **Add anything to a trip:** photos of site visits or events, meeting notes, conference passes, visa copies, any document. Use Add with the trip pre-selected, or the trip\'s action menu.

-   **Boarding passes** are read from a screenshot, photo or PDF: flight, date, seat and name.

### The Trip Pack: one report with all the evidence

1.  **Cover:** traveller, purpose, dates, places, entities billed and their shares, approver, status.

2.  **Itinerary timeline.**

3.  **Expense statement:** date, merchant, category, original currency and amount, rate and its source, INR value, paid by, belongs to, GST claimable, receipt reference.

4.  **Summaries:** by category, entity and paying card or account; budget against actual.

5.  **Advances and reimbursements:** advance received, spent, claimed, approved, paid and balance either way, with the bank reference of each payout.

6.  **Evidence appendix:** every ticket, boarding pass, hotel booking and invoice, receipt, card statement extract, forex purchase receipt, photo and document, numbered and cross-referenced to its expense line.

7.  **Missing evidence and declarations,** for example \"Cab, ₹420, no receipt, self-declared\".

8.  **Audit footer:** time generated, a fingerprint of each attached document, and a verification link.

Formats: one PDF with every attachment merged in order; a ZIP of originals with an index; an Excel file of expense lines. Share by expiring link. The pack is filed in the Vault under the trip.

### Closing a trip

-   After the return date, Thapal waits until card statements cover the trip, then raises \"Trip ready to close: review the pack\".

-   One tap submits a claim to each entity. Approval follows that entity\'s rule; for companies, a second approver strengthens the audit trail. Payouts are matched from the bank statement.

-   A trip shared between entities posts each share to its own books with the same evidence pack.

-   Leftover forex stays on the card for the next trip; exchange gains or losses are recorded.

## Travel Manager in the books (revision 8)

Every trip gets a permanent Trip ID, and every rupee on it is tied to its payer, owning entity, payment instrument and ledger entry. Travel Manager holds no money of its own: trip totals are queries on the central ledger, so the trip, the card, the company and the claim always show the same figure. This builds on Travel above.

### The trip record

-   **Trip ID**, for example TRP-2026-0042, kept from planning to archive, through reopening.

-   Name, destination, dates, purpose, travellers, responsible person or organisation, and budget.

-   Type: personal, family, business, institutional, trust, medical, conference or mixed.

-   Links to bookings, transactions, accounts, cards, forex cards, cash wallets, advances, categories, claims, refunds, ledger entries, documents, reports and history.

-   One trip can carry personal, Company A, Company B and trust spends; each expense is allocated to its owner once.

### Trips that build and complete themselves

From forwarded or fetched emails and uploads (flights, trains, hotels, visas, travel insurance, tours, car hire, conference registrations, itineraries) Thapal finds the destination, dates, travellers, booking references, amounts and paying entity. It groups the bookings of one journey, proposes a new trip or adds to an existing one, replaces revised bookings, marks cancellations, and flags duplicate bookings and trips.

After the journey it looks for each booking\'s invoice, the expected boarding passes, hotel invoices, matched card and bank rows, forex, refunds, claims and advances. Each gap becomes a reminder or an upload request.

### Itinerary

A timeline of flights, trains, hotel check-in and check-out, transfers, meetings, events and activities, with booking references and cancellation terms, shown in the calendar too. Live flight status needs a paid, authorised data provider, so the first release shows booked times and the airline\'s own change emails.

### Travel Money dashboard

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Block                Shows
  -------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Summary              Budget, spent, remaining, committed but unpaid, advances, owed to you, refunds pending, final settled cost

  How it was paid      Credit, debit and forex cards, bank accounts, UPI, cash, company-paid, paid by someone else

  On what              Stay, flights and trains, local transport, food, activities, conference, shopping, other

  Alerts               \"3 card charges have no receipt\" · \"Hotel refund outstanding\" · \"Company A owes you ₹42,600\" · \"AED cash not settled\" · \"12% over budget\"
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every figure opens the transactions and receipts behind it. Budgets (total, daily, stay, transport, food, activities, allowance, emergency) warn and project the final cost; they never block a spend.

### Receipts while travelling

A receipt attaches to a trip from its date, merchant location, currency, booking reference, card, traveller and the itinerary. Uncertain ones ask.

### Foreign currency

Each spend keeps its original currency, the rupee amount actually settled and where the rate came from: card statement, forex-card load or bank. Conversion charges and markups are separate lines. Forex-card loads, ATM withdrawals and foreign cash are balances, not spending, until used; reconversion and leftovers record exchange gains or losses.

### Advances

Advance received and from whom, currency, cash withdrawn, spent, unused, returned, and any extra reimbursement due. The advance settlement statement ties to the providing entity\'s books.

### Refunds, cancellations and insurance

Cancelled bookings, cancellation charges, expected and partial refunds, card reversals, travel credits and vouchers with expiry dates. Refunds are matched to bank and card rows, and one arriving months later still lands on its trip. Travel insurance keeps the policy, period, travellers, insurer, premium and limits; a claim tracks documents, status and money received. Thapal never assumes an incident is covered without the policy wording.

### Shared and group trips

Family holidays, business and institutional trips, conferences and group tours. Splits can be equal, percentage, fixed, per traveller, per organisation, item by item, and personal versus official. Thapal works out who paid, who benefited, who owes whom with the fewest transfers, and what is left. A settlement between travellers is not an expense, and each links back to the spends it settles.

### Travellers and privacy

Names, dates, tickets, boarding passes, insurance, visa validity and emergency contacts. Passport and visa copies live in the Vault, masked by default and visible only to people you allow.

### History and analytics

Every trip stays searchable by year, month, destination, country, traveller, organisation, purpose, payment method, category, currency and status. Analytics cover annual travel spend, personal versus official, domestic versus international, destination, airline, hotel and card, reimbursement and refund history, cost per trip and per day, and year-on-year comparison. Thapal also flags duplicate trips and bookings, missing boarding passes, unclaimed reimbursements, delayed refunds, unused credits, upcoming travel payments and expiring documents.

### Trip screen

Tabs: Overview (both statuses and the money dashboard) · Itinerary · Expenses (with payments and advances) · Documents · Travellers · Claims and refunds · Reports. No menus inside menus.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Device         Layout
  -------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  iPhone         One overview with expandable sections, Scan receipt inside the trip, one-tap actions

  iPad           Two panes: the itinerary or expense list stays visible while a document is open

  Computer       A workspace with filters, the full expense table and document preview side by side
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Accounting treatment

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Travel item                      Usual treatment, subject to the entity\'s policy
  -------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Hotel                            Travel -- accommodation

  Flight                           Travel -- airfare, or a prepayment when the trip falls in a later period

  Official meal                    Travel -- meals

  Advance given                    Advance to the traveller, an asset of the payer

  Personal payment for a company   Company expense and a payable to the person

  Company reimbursement            Settles that payable

  Hotel refund                     Reverses or settles against the original charge

  Forex conversion                 Money moved between currencies; exchange difference recorded

  Company card bill paid           Settles the card liability
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The trip-to-ledger reconciliation shows recorded spend, amount matched to statements, unmatched spends, missing receipts, advances, claims, refunds, differences and final cost, in PDF, Excel and CSV.

### Two statuses per trip

![trip status · 2 independent lanes, 6 travel and 8 finance states](media/image4.png){width="6.0in" height="4.714284776902887in"}

trip status · 2 independent lanes, 6 travel and 8 finance states

Every trip shows two labels side by side, in the trip list and on its overview, for example **Travel: Completed** and **Finance: Settlement pending**. You can filter trips by either. A finished journey never closes its money; the trip stays in pending financial work until it does.

The finance list merges the two lists in the addenda (one of eight states, one of seven) into eight: Not started, Recording expenses, Awaiting documents, Reconciling, Settlement pending (refunds or claims open), Ready to close, Financially closed, and Reopened with approval. Decision 33 confirms the names.

Example: Dubai business visit, 4 to 9 November. Travel: Completed. Finance: Settlement pending, because a hotel refund is awaited, two card charges wait for the statement, one claim waits for Company A\'s approval, and AED cash is not yet settled.

The finance status moves on its own when a statement arrives, a transaction matches, a refund lands, a claim is approved or paid, a missing receipt is uploaded, an advance is settled or an exception is resolved. Closing and reopening follow your approval settings.

**Ten checks before Financially closed:**

1.  All known expenses are recorded.

2.  Required documents are present or formally marked as exceptions.

3.  Card and bank reconciliation is complete for the trip\'s transactions.

4.  Advances are accounted for.

5.  Refunds are settled or carried forward as tracked receivables.

6.  Claims are settled or carried forward as tracked receivables or payables.

7.  Foreign-currency balances are reconciled.

8.  Allocations between entities are complete.

9.  No unexplained duplicate effects exist.

10. The final trip statement ties to the ledger.

You may close a trip with approved, documented balances still open; they stay tracked and on the calendar. A closed trip cannot change silently: any correction needs Reopen with approval, keeps the earlier version and issues a new statement version.

Reports: journeys completed but not settled; closed trips; pending refunds and claims by trip; unsettled advances; missing travel documents; closing exceptions; closure history; final settlement statements. All in PDF, Excel and CSV.

## To-do: one list of everything that needs a person

To-do is the only place anything waits for a person. When it is empty, the books are current.

### How an item looks

One sentence on what and why, the evidence, a suggested answer already selected, and one main button. For example: \"₹4,200 paid to RAMESH K on 4 Nov. What was it?\" with choices **Personal expense** (suggested, because of two earlier payments), Staff advance, Loan given, Supplier payment, Something else.

Similar items are grouped: \"12 payments to Swiggy, ₹3,860 in total. All Food?\" One tap answers all twelve, and the next 50 are remembered.

### Rules

-   The count is the number of saved, unresolved conditions, recomputed on the server. It never comes from screen checkboxes or a cached counter.

-   A checkbox never resolves anything; only a saved action does.

-   Order: money at risk first (balance mismatch, suspected duplicate), then due soon (tax, bills, renewals), then decisions, then tidy-ups.

-   Every item can be assigned: me, my accountant, my bookkeeper, my company secretary. \"Ask my accountant\" moves it with a note.

-   Snooze needs a reason. A compliance item cannot be snoozed past its due date without an explicit acknowledgement.

-   An undo bar follows every action. History (in Records) keeps who resolved what, when, and what changed.

-   Bulk mode for bookkeepers: select all, selected count and total, sub-groups by merchant or account.

-   Long categorisation and matching run in the background; the list stays usable.

-   \"Done for you\" items are a separate digest and are not counted as to-dos.

### Item types

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Type                            Plain wording                                       Usual suggested answer
  ------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------
  Unknown payee or category       \"What was this payment?\"                          Based on payee history and amount

  Possible own-account transfer   \"Did this go to your SBI account?\"                Link to the matching row if one exists

  One side missing                \"Waiting for the other side for 5 days\"           Upload the other statement, or say where it went

  Card bill paid                  \"Is this your card bill?\"                         Link to the card statement

  Balance mismatch                \"Closing balance differs by ₹1,250\"               Show the likely missing rows

  Possible duplicate              \"This looks like one you added on 3 Nov\"          Keep one

  Unclear document                \"We couldn\'t read the total\"                     Type the number, or rescan

  Missing statement               \"October statement for HDFC Savings\"              Forward it by email

  Invoice overdue                 \"Mehta Clinic owes ₹48,000, 32 days late\"         Send a reminder

  Bill or renewal due             \"Car insurance renews on 12 Dec\"                  Mark as planned

  Tax or compliance due           \"GST return for November is due\"                  Open the working

  Approval needed                 \"Accountant proposed a journal of ₹62,000\"        Review the effect

  Question from a professional    \"Your CA asks: is this laptop for the company?\"   Answer in one tap

  Stale valuation                 \"Gold price last updated 45 days ago\"             Update or accept
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Money: accounts, cards, transfers and balance checks

Money lists everything you have and owe, each with a balance you can trust and the date it was last proven against a statement.

### The account list

-   Groups: Bank and cash, Cards, Investments, Property, Insurance values, Loans, Owed to you.

-   Each row: name, masked number, balance, and its proof status.

-   Separate figures, never blended: **Cash you can use**, **Card dues**, **Card limit left**, **Investments at today\'s value**.

-   A new account is created from its first statement (bank, masked number, branch). Thapal asks one question: whose account is it, and which workspace?

### Balance check states

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  State               Shown as                        Meaning
  ------------------- ------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------
  Matches statement   ✓ Matches statement of 31 Oct   Statement closing equals ledger, and every row is linked

  Waiting             Not checked since 30 Sep        The next statement has not arrived

  Differs             ₹1,250 difference --- see why   Ledger and statement disagree; a To-do item exists
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A tick is never shown unless the numbers and links support it.

### Money moving between accounts (v1 §7 rules kept)

-   A transfer between your own accounts is **one movement** seen on two statements. It is never income or spending.

-   A card bill payment reduces cash and the card due. The purchases stay as spending and are never counted again.

-   Matching uses ownership, direction, amount, currency, a date window, reference and narration together, never the amount alone.

-   If only one side is visible, it waits as \"Waiting for the other side\". After 5 days Thapal asks where it went. It never invents the other row.

-   Links are saved in one transaction, with an idempotency key and rollback on failure.

-   **Payments to people are not accounts.** \"₹25,000 to Suresh\" asks what it was: expense, advance, loan given, gift, investment or supplier payment, suggested from history.

### Cash

An ATM withdrawal moves money from bank to a Cash wallet. Receipts reduce it. An optional monthly \"count your cash\" prompt adjusts the difference with a visible entry.

### Foreign currency in accounts

The original currency amount and the rate used (with source and date) are kept. A newer rate never changes a past transaction. Bank charges on conversion are recorded only when the statement shows them.

### Account detail

Balance over time, transactions, statements received and missing, balance checks by month, linked documents. The Accountant view adds the reconciliation statement: statement opening and closing, ledger movement, unmatched items and timing differences.

## Banking hub: every bank and card in one app (revision 3)

Everything a bank app shows, for all 17 accounts and 11 cards at once, without linking to any bank. Balances come from statements and from bank alert emails you forward automatically. Payments happen in your bank\'s own app; Thapal records them.

### What you can see

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Bank-app feature          In Thapal                                                                                              Comes from
  ------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ---------------------------------------------
  Balances                  Every account grouped by entity, each with its \"as of\" time                                          Last statement, updated by each alert email

  Transactions and search   All banks at once; filter by entity, account, payee, amount, date or category                          Statements and alerts

  Statement download        The bank\'s original PDF, plus a standard statement in Excel or PDF for any date range                 Stored originals

  Card summary              Outstanding, unbilled, minimum due, due date, limit and available limit                                Card statements and alerts

  Forex card                Balance per currency; loads with rate and TCS; spends                                                  Forex statements and load advices

  Payees                    Everyone you pay or receive from, with totals                                                          Learned from narrations

  Auto-debits               NACH mandates, standing instructions and card autopay, with next date and amount                       Detected from history

  Cheques                   Issued and deposited cheques: cleared, pending or returned                                             Cheque numbers in statements, cheque photos

  Deposits                  FDs and RDs per bank with maturity dates                                                               Advices and statements (see Wealth)

  Certificates              Interest and TDS certificates per account per year                                                     Uploaded or forwarded

  Alerts                    Low balance, large debit, unusual spend, card due in 3 days, minimum-balance breach, returned cheque   Rules you set
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Near-live balances without linking

-   **Alert emails:** set one forwarding rule in your mailbox. Each alert (\"INR 4,200 debited from A/c XX1234\") updates the balance and adds a provisional transaction within minutes; the statement confirms it later.

-   **SMS alerts** cannot be read automatically by a web app on iPhone, so email alerts are the dependable route.

-   **Optional, your decision:** RBI\'s Account Aggregator framework provides read-only, consent-based data from many banks, with no power to move money. It would make balances live, but it is a form of bank linking, which you excluded. It is listed under Decisions.

### Paying and moving money

Thapal never moves money. From any due, invoice, claim or settlement it offers:

-   **Pay in your bank:** opens your bank\'s app or website with amount, payee and reference ready to copy.

-   **UPI:** a payment link or QR opened in your UPI app, where your phone supports it.

-   **Bulk file:** vendor runs and salaries exported in your bank\'s bulk-upload format.

-   **Expected transfer:** tell Thapal \"Moving ₹5 L from Company A HDFC to Trust 2 SBI\"; it waits for both statement rows and matches them.

### Views

-   **By entity:** each company\'s or trust\'s accounts and cards, and group cash in total.

-   **By bank:** every account at one bank, useful before a relationship-manager meeting.

-   **Today:** cash available across all entities, card dues this week, deposits maturing this month.

## From documents to closed books: the accounting pipeline (revision 3)

Every person, company and trust runs through the same five stages. Thapal does all five; you step in only for something genuinely new and for the one-tap month lock.

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Stage                      What Thapal does                                                                                                                                                                                                               Built-in checks                                                                               Where you come in
  -------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------
  1\. Document extraction    Reads statements, alerts, receipts, invoices, bills, tickets, advices and past filings; keeps the printed value beside every reading                                                                                           Totals re-add; opening plus movements equal closing; repeats caught by fingerprint            Only if a figure cannot be read

  2\. Accounting entries     Turns each economic event into one balanced entry in the right entity\'s books: ledger head, GST split, TDS, capital or revenue, inter-entity due                                                                              Entry balances; posted once; month open; rule version recorded                                A new payee or situation, once

  3\. Reconciliation         Bank and card statements, GSTR-2B, Form 26AS and AIS, lender statements, CAS and broker holdings, inter-entity balances, customer and supplier balances                                                                        Every statement row linked; every balance ties; differences listed with likely causes         A difference no rule explains

  4\. Financial statements   Trial balance; Schedule III balance sheet and profit and loss for companies; income and expenditure, receipts and payments and balance sheet for trusts; net worth and income statement for individuals; notes and schedules   Statements tie to the trial balance; schedules tie to subledgers; last year shown alongside   Read the one-page summary

  5\. Closing                Month: accruals, prepayments, depreciation, interest on loans and deposits, payroll, tax workings, lock. Year: provisions, tax, carry-forwards, audit pack, next year\'s opening balances                                      Close board all green                                                                         One tap to lock the month; year end with your CA\'s review
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Suggested close rhythm

-   **Every day:** documents are read and matched as they arrive.

-   **By day 3 of the month:** statements for all 17 accounts and 11 cards are in and every balance ties.

-   **By day 7:** entries complete; GST and TDS workings ready before the first due dates.

-   **By day 10:** you lock the month in one tap, for all entities at once or one by one.

-   **Year end:** your CA reviews, the auditor receives the pack, statements are approved and the books roll forward.

### Corrections never break the books

A correction found after a month is locked posts in the current open month, linked to the original, unless you choose to reopen the month. A filed return is corrected in the next return or by a revised return, as the rules library prescribes.

## Wealth: net worth, investments, forex, insurance, property, loans and estate readiness

Net worth is everything you own minus everything you owe, and every figure shows its source and how fresh it is.

### Net worth header (top of Money)

\"You\'re worth ₹X today, 3:40 pm. 2 values are older than 30 days.\" Below it: Have and Owe, split by owner (Me, Family, my share of each company) and by type. Change since last month comes with reasons: \"+₹2.1 L, mostly shares rising; −₹40,000 card dues.\" The \"Everything\" view removes intercompany holdings so nothing counts twice.

### Investments

-   **Sources:** NSDL or CDSL consolidated statements cover demat and mutual funds in one monthly file, which removes most manual entry. Also broker statements and contract notes, CAMS or KFintech statements, EPF, PPF, NPS, FDs and RDs, bonds, sovereign gold bonds, physical gold (weight and purity), ESOPs and RSUs, unlisted shares, and virtual digital assets from exchange statements.

-   Securities are identified by ISIN and account. Imported and manual holdings are reconciled, never added together.

-   Corporate actions, dividends (linked to the bank credit), redemptions, and realised and unrealised gains follow the rules library.

-   **Price labels:** Live, Delayed, Closing price of 7 Nov, Entered by you, or Stale. A stale value is never called live. Licensed live feeds remain an external dependency; until then, use end-of-day prices from authorised sources and statement valuations, clearly dated.

-   **Investment cash flows (revision 3):** every purchase, SIP, redemption, dividend and interest payment is linked to its bank row, so money into and out of each holding is complete.

-   **Returns:** annualised return (XIRR) per holding, per account and per owner, since purchase and for the tax year.

-   **Gains:** realised gains by tax lot, first in first out, split short and long term per the rules library and ready for the capital-gains schedule; unrealised gains at today\'s dated value.

-   **Ownership:** each company\'s and trust\'s investments sit in its own balance sheet. Your personal net worth includes your shares in your companies, at cost or a dated valuation you choose. Trust assets are shown as \"held in trust\", never as your wealth.

### Deposits, commodities, gold and land (revision 3)

Every holding shows its owner (you, a family member, a company or a trust), cost, current value with its date and source, income earned and tax flags.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Holding                    What Thapal keeps                                                                                                                                                                                                               Built from                                                       Automatic actions
  -------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Fixed deposits             Bank, owner, masked number, principal, rate, start and maturity, payout or cumulative, auto-renewal, nominee, any lien                                                                                                          Deposit and renewal advices, statements                          Monthly interest accrual for companies and trusts; interest credit matched; TDS matched to interest certificates and AIS; maturity alerts

  Recurring deposits         Instalment, schedule, rate, maturity                                                                                                                                                                                            Advice and bank debits                                           Each instalment matched; a missed one becomes a To-do item

  Commodities                Commodity derivative positions, gold and silver ETFs, sovereign gold bonds, digital gold                                                                                                                                        Broker contract notes and statements, CAS, platform statements   Positions and gains updated per statement

  Physical gold and silver   Weight, purity, purchase bills, valuation rate and date                                                                                                                                                                         Bills and photos                                                 Revalued at a dated rate; a jeweller\'s valuation can replace it

  Land and buildings         Deed, patta, encumbrance certificate, survey number, extent, location pin, co-owners and shares, cost with stamp duty and registration, improvements, guideline and market value (dated), property tax, lease, loan or charge   Deeds and receipts                                               Property-tax reminders; rent matched; encumbrance-certificate refresh before any sale or loan
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

-   **Maturity ladder on Home:** \"₹25 L matures in December across 3 FDs.\" When a deposit matures, the credit is matched; forward the new advice if it is reinvested.

-   **Trust investments:** registered non-profits may invest only in permitted modes, so any trust investment outside them is flagged for review before posting.

### Forex **(new in v2)**

-   Holds foreign-currency bank accounts, forex and travel cards, foreign cash, foreign shares and foreign property.

-   **LRS tracker:** remittances this financial year against the annual limit in the rules library; TCS collected by the bank appears as a tax credit in the tax summary.

-   Prepares the foreign-assets disclosure for the income-tax return from these holdings.

-   Realised exchange gains or losses on conversion are recorded; historical rates are never rewritten.

### Insurance **(new in v2)**

-   A policy register built from policy documents: insurer, policy number, type (term, health, motor, home, endowment or ULIP, personal accident; keyman and directors\' liability for companies), insured people, cover, premium and frequency, due date, nominees, riders, start and maturity dates.

-   Premiums are matched to bank or card debits. Renewal reminders at 30, 15 and 3 days.

-   In net worth, only surrender or fund values count. Term and health cover are shown as protection, not assets.

-   A plain cover summary: \"Life cover ₹1.5 Cr. Health ₹10 L family floater. Motor renews 12 Dec. No health policy found for one family member.\" Facts only, never advice.

-   A claims log with documents and settlement amounts.

### Property (v1 §17 kept)

Revision 5 covers property in full in Property management, below: title, value, taxes, utilities, tenants, income and sale.

### Loans

Revision 3 covers loans in full in the next section, Loans and financed assets.

### Estate readiness **(new in v2)**

-   **Nominee check:** \"3 of 14 accounts and policies have no nominee.\" Each opens the evidence and the issuer\'s form.

-   **Where things are:** location of the will, deeds and key documents, recorded by the owner.

-   **Trusted person:** the owner names someone who can request read-only access to a chosen summary. Access opens only after identity checks and a waiting period with no response from the owner, and every step is logged.

## Investments and net worth in the books (revision 9)

One investment system covers every person, company and trust, fills itself from statements, and posts only through the ledger. Net worth is then a reconciled total of ledger balances and dated valuations, with every estimate labelled. This extends Wealth above.

### What it holds

Listed shares, mutual funds, ETFs, bonds and debentures, government securities and treasury bills, fixed and recurring deposits, gold, silver and other commodities, sovereign gold bonds, foreign investments, unlisted and private company shares, partnership interests, AIFs, PMS accounts and other financial assets. A new type is added as a setting, never as a new ledger.

### Imports

-   **Sources:** demat statements, CAS from NSDL or CDSL, broker contract notes and ledgers, mutual fund statements from CAMS and KFintech, bank investment statements, FD and bond certificates, dividend statements, capital-gains reports, foreign investment statements.

-   **Formats:** PDF including scans, Excel, CSV, authorised structured data, many files at once, ZIP.

-   **Read from each:** investor, legal owner, account, broker or registrar, security name, ISIN, quantity, date, price, transaction type, charges, taxes, income and current holdings.

-   **Controls:** existing holdings recognised; duplicates prevented, since a holdings statement confirms positions and never creates purchases; missing periods identified; history reconciled; originals kept; unmatched rows listed; import versions kept; an exception review and a reconciliation report for every import.

### Tax lots

Every purchase is its own lot with date, quantity, cost and charges, so each sale draws from the right lots and gains use the right cost.

### In the ledger

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Event                    Entry, under the entity\'s accounting framework
  ------------------------ --------------------------------------------------------------------
  Shares or units bought   Dr Investments · Cr Bank or broker

  Sold or redeemed         Cr Investments at cost · Dr Bank · gain or loss for the difference

  Dividend                 Dr Bank and TDS receivable · Cr Dividend income

  FD opened                Dr Fixed deposit · Cr Bank: money moved, not spent

  FD matures               Dr Bank · Cr Fixed deposit · Cr Interest income, with TDS recorded

  Fees and brokerage       Added to cost or expensed, by policy

  Corporate action         Adjusts quantity and cost (below)

  Foreign investment       Original currency kept; exchange differences recorded
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Reconciliation

Transactions, demat holdings, broker statements, the broker\'s cash ledger, bank rows, corporate actions, dividends and interest, realised gains and ledger balances must agree. Any difference stays visible until resolved.

### Corporate actions

Splits, bonuses, rights issues, mergers, demergers, buybacks, delistings, tender offers, dividends, return of capital and conversions. Each keeps its source document and effective date; cost changes are versioned and checked before they touch gains or tax.

### Performance

Invested amount, market value, realised and unrealised gains, absolute and annualised return, XIRR on actual cash-flow dates, dividend and interest income, total return, allocation by asset class, sector and security, results by account and by owner, and value over time. Also diversification and concentration warnings, maturity reminders, income forecasts, tax-impact estimates, fee analysis and stale-price alerts. Forecasts and estimates are always labelled.

### Prices, honestly labelled

Every value shows its price, date and time, currency, source and one status: Live quote · Official close · Delayed · Stale · Valued from evidence · No valuation. An old price is never shown as live. Mutual fund NAVs and exchange closing prices are published daily; live prices need a licensed feed (Decision 41). When no current price exists, the last reliable value stays with its date, marked Stale, and an authorised person can update it with evidence.

### Net worth

Assets: bank balances, cash, investments, deposits, gold and commodities, properties, vehicles, other recorded assets, business interests, loans given and other financial assets. Liabilities: home, vehicle, personal and business loans, card balances, overdrafts and other liabilities.

-   Calculated by legal owner, by family (only from data each member allows), and separately for each company and trust.

-   The group view never double-counts. If you own Company A, it shows either your shares in Company A or Company A\'s assets and liabilities, never both; intercompany balances are eliminated; a building valuation that includes its fittings is not added to those fittings again.

-   Every value keeps its date and basis, estimates are explained, missing information is listed, and financial assets reconcile with the ledger.

### History

Monthly snapshots show changes by month, quarter and year, split into asset classes, liabilities, investment performance, cash flows and revaluation. Any past date\'s statement can be reproduced exactly from the prices and records valid on that date.

### Reports

-   **Investments:** consolidated, owner, company and trust holdings; demat and fund statements; transaction, purchase and sale registers; realised and unrealised gains; tax lots; cost-basis reconciliation; dividend and interest income; corporate actions; performance and XIRR; allocation and concentration; maturity schedule; broker and investment-to-ledger reconciliations; foreign investments; tax summary; valuation history.

-   **Net worth:** personal, family, entity-wise and consolidated statements; by asset class; liabilities; history and monthly movement; annual statement; valuation sources; missing valuations; reconciliation; group eliminations; wealth evidence pack.

All in PDF, Excel and CSV, JSON for authorised exports, ZIP for evidence, and prescribed tax formats where verified.

## Loans and financed assets (revision 3)

Every loan taken or given, by you, a company or a trust, is tracked from sanction letter to closure, and every asset bought with a loan is linked to it.

### Loans taken

Home, vehicle and equipment loans; business term loans; overdraft and cash-credit limits; gold loans; loans against property, deposits or securities; inter-company and director loans; unsecured loans from relatives.

1.  **One document starts it.** Forward the sanction letter or a loan statement. Thapal reads lender, amount, rate (fixed, or floating with its benchmark), tenure, EMI, moratorium, fees, security, guarantors and covenants.

2.  **Schedule.** An EMI calculator builds the repayment schedule and rebuilds it when the rate resets or you prepay.

3.  **Every EMI matched.** Each debit on the bank statement is matched and split into principal and interest. Companies and trusts also get month-end interest accruals.

4.  **Lender reconciliation.** The lender\'s statement is tied to the books monthly; penal interest, charges and rate resets become To-do items.

5.  **Tax.** The interest certificate is matched: deductible housing-loan interest for you, finance cost for companies.

6.  **Overdraft and cash credit.** Limit, drawing power, interest, renewal date, and reminders for the monthly stock or receivables statement the bank asks for.

### Financed assets

-   Buying an asset on a loan creates three linked records: the asset at full cost in the register, the loan, and its insurance policy.

-   EMIs reduce the loan, interest is an expense, and depreciation runs separately on the asset. Nothing is counted twice.

-   A hypothecation or charge is noted on the asset. For a company it opens the charge filing with the company secretary; at closure it prompts the satisfaction filing and the lender\'s no-objection certificate.

### Asset registers and depreciation

-   One register per company and trust, and an optional one for your personal assets: asset, category, invoice, put-to-use date, cost, location, custodian, tag or QR code, insurance, warranty and loan link.

-   Book depreciation (Companies Act Schedule II lives for companies; the trust\'s own policy for trusts) and tax depreciation (block of assets, per the rules library) are kept separately and posted monthly or yearly, as you choose. Land is never depreciated.

-   Sale, scrapping or transfer between entities computes the gain or loss. A yearly physical check runs from a checklist on your phone.

Revision 5 expands registers and depreciation into the full Asset management section below.

### Loans given

Loans to your companies, trusts, staff or relatives: schedule, interest receivable, TDS where applicable and repayment tracking. Loans between your own entities appear on both sides and in Who owes whom. Any loan that benefits a trustee, founder or director is held for your review and flagged to the auditor and company secretary.

### What you see

\"Loans: ₹2.4 Cr outstanding across 9 loans. EMIs this month ₹3.1 L. Company B\'s car loan closes in March: collect the no-objection certificate.\" Each loan\'s action menu: view schedule, record prepayment, change rate, download interest certificate, close loan.

## Projects and large transactions: construction and other big spends (revision 4)

A construction, renovation or any large spend becomes a Project. Bills with hundreds or thousands of line items are read line by line, sorted into cost heads and checked, and you see one screen: budget, spent, committed and what needs you.

### Starting a project

-   From its first document (work order, contract, estimate or bill of quantities, approved plan, loan sanction) or one tap in Add.

-   Owner: you, a family member, a company or a trust. Type: new building, renovation, interiors, equipment installation, or any other large spend such as a CSR project or an event.

-   Budget by cost head, suggested from the estimate: civil, steel, cement, electrical, plumbing, finishing, labour, architect and consultant fees, approvals and fees, interest during construction. Optional splits by block, floor or stage.

-   Contractors and suppliers, each with its work order or rate agreement, and the funding sources: own funds or loan disbursements.

### Thousands of line items, no typing

-   An estimate or bill of quantities in Excel is imported as it is, every line kept.

-   Multi-page bills, contractors\' running bills and material invoices are read line by line: item, quantity, unit, rate, amount and tax.

-   Each line is mapped to a cost head and to its matching estimate item. One correction teaches every future bill from that supplier.

-   Wage sheets, site photos and measurement records attach to the stage they belong to.

-   Big imports run in the background. Tables of 10,000 lines or more stay fast because the server pages, sorts and filters them.

### Checks on every bill

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Check                          Example
  ------------------------------ --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Duplicate lines across bills   \"Lines 14 to 22 of bill 318 repeat bill 301\"

  Rate                           \"Cement billed at ₹410 a bag; ₹385 last week from the same supplier\"

  Quantity                       \"Steel billed to date 42.6 t against 40 t in the estimate\"

  Arithmetic                     A line total that is not quantity × rate, or a bill total that is not the sum of its lines

  Budget                         \"Electrical at 92% of budget with 40% of the work done\"

  Evidence                       \"Running bill 6 has no measurement sheet attached\"
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Contractors and payments

-   One contractor ledger: work-order value, billed, certified, advances paid and adjusted, retention held, TDS deducted, GST charged, paid and balance.

-   An optional certification step by your engineer or architect before a bill becomes payable.

-   Payments on bank statements are matched to bills; advances are adjusted against later bills; retention release dates create reminders.

-   GST credit on constructing a building is largely blocked by law, with narrow exceptions, so each bill is flagged per the rules library for your CA to confirm.

### Accounting, done for you

-   **Companies and trusts:** costs collect as capital work in progress and become a building or equipment in the asset register on completion; depreciation starts from the put-to-use date. Borrowing costs are capitalised where the accounting standard allows.

-   **Your own house:** the full cost record is kept for any future sale, and pre-construction home-loan interest is tracked for the tax rules that apply.

-   Construction-loan disbursements link to project stages and to the loan\'s schedule.

### What you see

\"New building: ₹4.82 Cr spent of ₹6.50 Cr (74%). ₹1.10 Cr more committed. 3 bills need you. Cement rates up 8% this month. Retention of ₹18 L due for release in March.\" From that line, open it by cost head, contractor, stage or month, then down to a bill, its lines and the page of the original.

### Reports and packs

Project cost statement (budget, committed, actual and variance by cost head), contractor statements of account, material register, capitalisation schedule, and a Project Pack built like the Trip Pack: every bill, line, payment, certificate and photo, indexed for your auditor or a bank\'s stage inspection.

## Asset management: every asset, from purchase to disposal (revision 5)

Every asset owned by you, your family, your companies or your trusts, from a laptop to a whole building, sits in one register that builds itself from purchase documents. Thapal then follows each asset through its life: where it is, who has it, whether it works, whether it is insured and compliant, what it is worth, and how it leaves.

![asset life cycle · 6 stages, 1 yearly loop](media/image5.png){width="6.0in" height="2.455356517935258in"}

asset life cycle · 6 stages, 1 yearly loop

Assets enter from an invoice, a finished project or a financed purchase, and leave by sale, scrapping or transfer; the yearly verification loop confirms each one is still where the register says.

### What it covers

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Category                         Examples                                                                                   Special handling
  -------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Land                             Plots, agricultural land, campus land                                                      Never depreciated; land records, guideline value, encumbrance (see Property management)

  Buildings                        Homes, flats, offices, hostels, institutional blocks                                       Depreciated; linked to its property record, completion certificate, building insurance and property tax

  Plant, machinery and equipment   Generators, lifts, air conditioning, kitchen, workshop, medical and laboratory equipment   Maintenance plans, AMCs, calibration, statutory inspections and licences

  Vehicles                         Cars, buses, ambulances, two-wheelers                                                      Registration, insurance, permits, fitness and pollution certificates, fuel and service log, tolls, fines

  IT and electronics               Laptops, servers, phones, network gear                                                     Assigned user, warranty, software licences, data wipe before disposal

  Furniture and fittings           Desks, beds, shelving, interiors                                                           Location and condition

  Intangibles                      Software licences, trademarks, domain names, websites                                      Renewal dates; amortised rather than depreciated

  Leased (right-of-use) assets     Premises or equipment you lease                                                            Lease liability and right-of-use asset under the applicable accounting standard

  Personal valuables               Jewellery, gold, art, watches                                                              Dated valuation, insurance, locker, photos (see Wealth)

  Work in progress                 Buildings or plant under construction                                                      Collected in Projects, moved here on completion
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Items below a capitalisation limit you set are expensed, and can still be tracked as minor assets if you want them tagged and verified.

### Getting assets in, without typing

-   **From a purchase invoice through Add:** capital items (a laptop, an air conditioner, a vehicle, a machine) are recognised and proposed as assets, with cost including freight and installation, entity, location and put-to-use date.

-   **One invoice, many assets:** \"20 laptops\" becomes 20 tagged assets, or one group, as you choose.

-   **Other ways in:** a completed Project, a loan-financed purchase, an existing register in Excel, last year\'s audited fixed-asset schedule, or a walk-through where staff photograph and tag what they find.

-   **GST:** credit on capital goods is flagged where eligible; when credit is claimed, the tax is kept out of the asset\'s cost.

### Identify, locate and assign

-   Each asset gets an ID and a QR label, printed from Thapal as label sheets. Scanning a label with any phone opens the asset.

-   Location by entity, site, building, floor and room; department and custodian; make, model, serial number and photos.

-   **Movements:** transfers between rooms, departments or entities (an inter-entity transfer posts in both sets of books). Portable items such as laptops and cameras are checked out and in, with due-back reminders.

-   **Physical verification:** a yearly or rolling campaign. Staff scan labels room by room on their phones; each asset is marked found, missing, moved or damaged. The exceptions report and verification certificate are ready for the auditor, including the physical-verification point auditors report on under CARO where it applies.

### Keep it working: maintenance

-   **Warranties and AMC or CMC contracts:** vendor, coverage, dates and cost; renewal reminders; AMC invoices linked to the contract.

-   **Preventive maintenance:** schedules by date or by usage (hours, kilometres), work orders to a vendor or your own team, checklists, photos and cost.

-   **Breakdowns:** anyone scans the asset\'s QR to report a fault. Thapal assigns it, tracks downtime and the fix, and records the cost. When repairs pass a share of the asset\'s value you set, it suggests \"repair or replace?\".

-   **Calibration, inspections and licences:** due dates and certificates for lifts, fire systems, pressure vessels, electrical safety, medical and laboratory equipment, radiation-equipment licences, and vehicle fitness and pollution certificates. Alerts start 60 days ahead.

-   **Measures:** uptime, downtime and maintenance cost per asset per year.

### Protect it: insurance and documents

-   Each asset links to its policies: fire, burglary, machinery breakdown, electronic equipment or vehicle. Sum insured is compared with current replacement value: \"Main building under-insured by ₹2.1 Cr.\"

-   Claims are logged against the asset and its repair.

-   The asset\'s folder in the Vault holds the invoice, warranty card, manuals, registration, permits, certificates and photos.

### Account for it: depreciation and value

-   **Book depreciation** by each entity\'s policy: Companies Act Schedule II useful lives for companies, with separate components where a significant part has a different life; the trust\'s own policy for trusts. Straight-line or written-down value; residual value.

-   **Tax depreciation** by block of assets per the rules library, including the reduced rate for assets used for part of a year and any additional depreciation that applies.

-   Depreciation runs post automatically each month or year, as you choose. Idle, damaged or obsolete assets are flagged for impairment review; revaluation is supported where policy allows, with the valuer\'s report attached.

-   Capital grants received for an asset (common for trusts) are recorded against it, per the trust\'s policy.

-   **Values side by side:** cost, accumulated depreciation, book value, tax written-down value, insured value and a dated market or replacement value.

-   **Ties automatically:** the register equals the balance sheet; the tax blocks equal the return schedule; additions and disposals feed the notes to accounts.

### Retire it: disposal

-   Sale, scrapping, write-off, donation, theft or loss (with the insurance claim), trade-in, or transfer to another entity or to you.

-   Gain or loss for the books, the tax block adjustment and the GST on sale of a used asset are worked out and flagged per the rules library.

-   Close-out steps: e-waste and data-wipe certificates for IT, registration transfer for vehicles, the lender\'s no-objection certificate if the asset was financed.

-   Disposal approval by you or the board, with buyer, price and evidence attached.

### Vehicles, in more detail

Registration, insurance, pollution and fitness certificates, permits and road tax, each with renewal alerts. Fuel and toll spends attach from card statements and receipts. Service history, tyres and battery, traffic fines, the assigned driver and that driver\'s licence expiry. Cost per kilometre per vehicle.

### What you see

\"Assets: 1,284 across the group, book value ₹38.6 Cr. 6 AMCs expire this month. 2 lift inspections due. Verification 92% done at Campus A. 14 laptops idle for over 90 days.\"

### Reports

Fixed asset register in statutory format; additions and disposals; book and tax depreciation schedules; physical verification report; maintenance cost and downtime; warranty and AMC expiry; insurance gaps; assets by location and custodian; disposal register; work-in-progress ageing; QR label sheets.

## Property management: land, homes and buildings, from title to tenants (revision 5)

Every property owned by anyone in the group (land, a home, a flat, a commercial building or a campus) has one record covering title, value, taxes, utilities, tenants, income and sale, whether you live in it, let it out, use it for business or simply hold it.

### The property record

-   **Identity:** name, address, map pin, survey, plot or door number, extent, built-up area, type (residential, commercial, agricultural, institutional, vacant land) and use (self-occupied, let out, business use, vacant, under construction).

-   **Units:** a building splits into flats, floors, shops or rooms, each with its own tenant, rent and meters.

-   **Ownership:** owners and their shares (you, a family member, a company or a trust), and how it was acquired: purchase, inheritance, gift, partition or allotment.

-   **Title and approvals:** sale deed and the earlier deeds in the title chain, encumbrance certificates, land records such as patta, mutation status, approved plan, building permit, completion or occupancy certificate, powers of attorney and any litigation papers.

-   **Value:** cost with stamp duty, registration, brokerage and improvements; government guideline value; market value from a valuer\'s report or an estimate, always dated; and the indexed cost the rules library allows for capital gains.

-   **Map view:** every property on one map, coloured by use, with rent due or tax due shown on tap.

### Taxes, utilities and running costs

-   **Property tax:** assessment, due dates, payments matched from the bank, receipts filed, arrears flagged.

-   **Utilities per property or unit:** electricity, water, gas and internet bills by upload or forwarding, consumption trends, and optional recovery from tenants on sub-meters.

-   **Society or association charges** and sinking fund.

-   **Insurance** for building and contents, from the Insurance register.

-   **Land care:** encumbrance certificate refresh before any sale or loan, mutation follow-up, fencing and a dated site-photo log to spot encroachment.

### Letting: tenants and leases

1.  **Lease from the agreement:** forward the signed agreement. Thapal reads tenant, unit, start and end dates, rent, escalation, deposit, lock-in, notice period, maintenance charges, stamp duty and registration, and builds the rent schedule.

2.  **Tenant record:** contacts, KYC documents, the police-verification record where your city requires it, and an emergency contact.

3.  **Move-in:** an inspection checklist with photos and meter readings.

4.  **Every month:** a rent invoice or receipt goes out, with GST where it applies under the rules library and a UPI QR. Rent credits are matched from the bank; late payers get reminders, and late fees apply if the agreement provides for them.

5.  **TDS by tenants** on rent is tracked and matched with Form 26AS and AIS.

6.  **Escalations** apply on their dates, with notice sent to the tenant beforehand.

7.  **Maintenance requests** come from tenants through an upload-request link. Each becomes a work order, recorded as recoverable from the tenant or borne by you.

8.  **Renewal or exit:** alerts at 90, 60 and 30 days. At exit, the move-out inspection is compared with move-in, deductions are listed with evidence, and the deposit refund is matched from the bank.

The security deposit is always shown as money you owe back, never as income. A rent roll shows every unit, tenant, rent, next escalation, arrears and occupancy.

### Renting premises for your entities

When a company or trust is the tenant: rent payable schedule, TDS on rent paid, GST credit or reverse charge where it applies, the deposit given (an asset), escalations and renewals, and right-of-use accounting under the applicable standard.

### Income and tax

-   **Property profit and loss** per property and unit: rent and other income against tax, maintenance, repairs, insurance and loan interest; net yield and occupancy.

-   **House-property income** for each owner, split by ownership share; let-out or self-occupied treatment and interest on housing loans per the rules library.

-   **Companies and trusts:** rental income posts to their books, with GST returns and TDS credits handled automatically.

-   **Selling:** sale agreement, buyer\'s TDS per the rules library, capital-gains working with cost, improvements and indexation where it applies, and reinvestment options flagged for your CA.

-   **Buying:** the TDS you must deduct above the threshold, stamp duty, registration and title checks, with the new property and loan created from the documents.

-   **Building or renovating:** handled as a Project and linked to the property.

### What you see

\"Properties: 23 across the group. Rent due this month ₹14.2 L, received ₹11.8 L; 2 tenants late. 3 leases end within 90 days. Property tax due on 5 properties in December. Occupancy 91%.\"

### Reports

Property register; rent roll; arrears ageing; deposit register; lease expiry schedule; property-wise profit and loss; house-property income schedule per owner; capital-gains workings; utility cost by property; title document index; and a Property Pack (title chain, approvals, tax receipts, valuation and photos) for a loan against property or a sale.

## Assets and property in the books (revision 8)

The Asset and Property managers are views of the ledger, not separate databases. Every asset and property has a legal owner, an accounting workspace and ledger accounts, and every change in value is a ledger posting. If a register ever differs from the books, Thapal shows the difference and its cause; it never invents an adjustment to make them agree. This is a P0 rule that extends Asset management and Property management above.

The chain: legal entity → its ledger → asset or property record → transactions → financial statements.

### Owner and ledger, always

Every record carries its legal owner (individual, family member, company, trust, LLP or HUF), entity ID, ownership percentage, acquisition date and source, funding source, accounting workspace, asset class, ledger account and ownership documents.

-   An asset cannot post to a company\'s books without an ownership or accounting basis.

-   Joint ownership keeps each owner\'s share and treatment separately.

-   The user of an asset, such as a department or another company, can differ from its owner; both are kept.

### Ledger accounts

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Record                           Ledger account, configurable per entity
  -------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------
  Land                             Land -- fixed assets

  Buildings                        Buildings -- fixed assets

  Medical and lab equipment        Medical equipment -- fixed assets

  Vehicles                         Motor vehicles -- fixed assets

  Computers                        Computers -- fixed assets

  Furniture                        Furniture and fixtures

  Under construction               Capital work-in-progress

  Let-out or investment property   Investment property, as the entity\'s policy sets

  Wear and tear                    Accumulated depreciation; depreciation expense

  Rent                             Rental income

  Repairs                          Repairs and maintenance

  Asset insurance                  Insurance expense or prepaid insurance

  Bought on credit                 Accounts payable

  Financed                         The loan account
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Purchase invoice to asset

Upload a purchase invoice and Thapal reads it, finds the buying entity and each asset, and works out what to capitalise: price, freight, installation and tax that cannot be credited. It finds the payment or the unpaid liability, matches the bank or card row, creates the register entries and the ledger entries, links invoice, payment and asset, and keeps the original. One invoice with several assets splits its cost across them while the invoice total still ties. Re-uploading changes nothing.

### Importing an existing register

At onboarding each company\'s Excel, CSV or PDF register is imported and checked against ledger balances, the trial balance, the opening balance sheet, past depreciation, capital work-in-progress and loans.

Example: a register shows computers ₹25,00,000, medical equipment ₹80,00,000 and furniture ₹15,00,000, a cost of ₹1,20,00,000. Thapal compares that with the fixed-asset ledgers after accumulated depreciation, additions, disposals and class differences, and explains every gap. Imported rows stay **provisional** until their values are validated or you accept a documented exception. Nothing is balanced automatically.

### Depreciation

Cost, capitalisation date, date put to use, useful life, residual value, method, changes in estimate, accumulated depreciation and carrying value. Depreciation posts monthly through the ledger and ties three ways: depreciation in the profit and loss, accumulated depreciation in the balance sheet, and the register\'s carrying value. Book depreciation follows the entity\'s policy (Schedule II of the Companies Act for companies); tax depreciation is computed separately on the income-tax block-of-assets basis.

### Property in the books

Purchase price, registration, stamp duty, brokerage, improvements, loans and interest, property tax, insurance, utilities, maintenance, rent invoices and receipts, deposits, sale and capital-gains workings all sit in the owner\'s books.

A lease creates the rent schedule. When rent arrives, Thapal identifies the tenant and property, matches the bank credit, settles the rent receivable, records the tenant\'s TDS, and updates the tenant ledger and property income. Rent is recognised once: the invoice raises the receivable and the receipt settles it.

### Loans on assets and property

Sanction, disbursement, purchase, principal, interest, EMIs, prepayment, closing balance, charge or mortgage, and closure. Principal reduces the loan; interest is an expense, or is capitalised while a building is under construction where policy allows. Repaying a loan is never treated as another asset purchase.

### Running costs

Each maintenance spend links to the asset or property, the entity, the paying account, the invoice, the category and the period. Thapal separates routine costs, capital improvements, replacements, repairs and insurance; an improvement is proposed for capitalisation and waits for your approval.

### A building and what is inside it

A hospital building can hold medical and lab equipment, generators, air-conditioners, computers, furniture and electrical installations. Each stays its own asset, with its own owner, ID, class, cost, depreciation, maintenance, insurance and disposal, and links to the building for location only. No value is counted twice in a balance sheet, register, valuation, consolidation or group net worth: a market valuation of the building is added to separately recorded assets only when its scope excludes them.

### Moves, transfers and disposal

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Event                                      Accounting
  ------------------------------------------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Move between rooms, departments or sites   Location history only; no posting

  Transfer to another group company          A sale by one and a purchase by the other, with tax treatment confirmed by your CA; the asset keeps its permanent ID

  Sale, scrapping or write-off               Removes cost and accumulated depreciation, records proceeds, tax and gain or loss, and settles any linked loan
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Evidence and approvals are kept for each.

### Reconciliation dashboard

Register total, ledger carrying value, difference, unmatched assets, unmatched ledger entries, missing invoices, missing depreciation, wrong classes and pending corrections. Each entity and class shows one status: Reconciled · Partly reconciled · Needs attention · Awaiting documents · Awaiting approval. Reconciled appears only when every check passes.

### Reports

Fixed asset register by company; asset-to-ledger and opening-balance reconciliations; additions and disposals; depreciation reconciliation; carrying values; purchase and payment statement; maintenance by asset; asset loans; property income and expenditure; rental ledger; property-to-ledger and property-loan reconciliations; valuation and net equity; intercompany transfers; disposal accounting; tax schedules; consolidated statement; exceptions; audit trail. All in PDF, Excel and CSV, with evidence packs in PDF and ZIP.

### Getting around

Company → Accounts → Assets or Properties → record → transactions → documents → reports. From any asset or property, one tap reaches the owning company, ledger account, purchase invoice, payment, bank account, loan, depreciation, maintenance, insurance, financial statement and documents.

## Permanent IDs (revision 8)

Every trip, asset and property, and every expense, claim, statement and reminder, gets a permanent ID when it is created. The ID never changes and is never reused. Moves, transfers, depreciation, disposal, reopening and re-imports keep it, so the whole history stays traceable from the record to the ledger and its documents.

### The IDs

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Record                                   Example            Note
  ---------------------------------------- ------------------ -----------------------------------------------
  Trip                                     TRP-2026-0042      Year created and a running number

  Asset                                    AST-000318         Printed on the asset\'s QR label

  Property                                 PRP-0007           One per property, across all owners

  Expense                                  EXP-2026-104233    Each split share points to it

  Claim                                    CLM-2026-0119      

  Statement                                DES-2026-0187      Later versions keep the number and add v2, v3

  Calendar event, reminder, notification   EVT-, REM-, NTF-   Each points to its source record
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Inside the database each record also has a UUID; the readable ID is what people see, print and search. A company\'s own display code, such as CA/IT/0042, can sit beside it and may change; the permanent ID does not.

### What an asset or property ID links to

Legal owner and ownership history; entity; ledger accounts; purchase documents; bank and card transactions; loans; depreciation and carrying value; maintenance and repairs; insurance and warranties; location and custodian; the building it sits in; tax and compliance records; transfers and disposals; reports; audit history.

### Rules

-   A deleted or disposed record keeps its ID in the archive, and the ID is never given to anything else.

-   A move or a new custodian keeps the ID. A legal transfer to another entity keeps it too, while the books record a disposal in one entity and an acquisition in the other.

-   A new invoice, payment, policy or maintenance bill is matched to the right ID automatically; an uncertain match waits for review before any money changes.

-   The ID is what stops duplicate assets, duplicate purchase entries, duplicate depreciation and double-counting in net worth.

### Imports

Thapal recognises existing asset numbers, matches existing records, issues IDs only to genuinely new items, keeps the legacy code, records the source file and row, and keeps the history of each import and correction. Importing the same file again creates nothing.
