Every register, depreciation schedule, maintenance and loan report, ownership history, verification sheet, reconciliation, audit report and disposal statement carries these IDs.

## Business: invoicing, bills, payroll, books and month-end close

For a company, sales, purchases, payroll and the books run on the same engine. The owner sees cash, dues and tax; the accountant sees a ledger ready to close.

### Company setup from documents (v1 §3.3 kept)

Upload the incorporation certificate, PAN, TAN, GST certificates, MCA master data and bank letters. Thapal proposes the entity profile, matched by CIN, PAN or GSTIN rather than by name. Supported entity types: individual, HUF, proprietorship, partnership, LLP, private and public company, trust, society and Section 8 company. One PAN can hold several GSTINs (one per state). A chart of accounts template is chosen by business type (services, trading, manufacturing, healthcare, non-profit) and is editable by the accountant.

### Sales and invoicing **(new in v2)**

-   **Customers and items:** customers carry GSTIN and state; items and services carry HSN or SAC codes, with GST rates from the rules library.

-   **Documents:** quotation, proforma, tax invoice, bill of supply, export invoice (with or without IGST, under LUT), credit and debit notes, delivery challan, receipt for advances.

-   **Numbering:** a separate series per GSTIN and financial year, consecutive and unique, up to 16 characters (CGST Rule 46).

-   **Tax logic:** CGST plus SGST or IGST is chosen from the place of supply automatically.

-   **E-invoicing:** required once aggregate turnover has exceeded ₹5 crore in any year since FY 2017-18; since 1 April 2025, taxpayers at ₹10 crore and above must report each invoice within 30 days ([Accountune](https://www.accountune.com/e-invoicing-compulsory-india-small-business-2026)). Thapal tracks applicability; getting the IRN and QR needs an approved invoice-registration integration (phase 5). E-way bills follow the same route.

-   **Getting paid without bank linking:** each invoice carries a UPI QR for the company\'s own UPI ID. When the bank statement shows the credit, Thapal matches it by amount and reference and marks the invoice paid.

-   Recurring invoices, customer statements, and payment reminders that the owner switches on per customer.

-   TDS deducted by customers is tracked and matched to Form 26AS or AIS credits.

-   Invoices made in Tally, Zoho or other tools can be uploaded instead, as a file or a sales register.

### Purchases and payables **(new in v2)**

-   Vendor bills arrive through Add. A new vendor is created from the GSTIN on the bill.

-   **GST you can claim back:** bills are matched with the uploaded GSTR-2B: matched, missing in 2B (supplier has not filed), missing in books, or amounts differ.

-   **TDS on payments:** a suggested section and rate from the rules library, mapped across the 1961 and 2025 Acts. Net payable, TDS liability and the challan amount are prepared.

-   **MSME vendors:** Udyam number flagged; the 45-day payment limit under the MSMED Act is tracked, with its tax consequence flagged. Outstanding MSME dues feed the CS\'s half-yearly MSME return.

-   **Payment run:** a list of bills due. The user pays from the bank, optionally using a bulk-payment file exported for the bank\'s upload screen. The next statement marks them paid.

-   Expense claims and advances keep the v1 §14 rules.

### Payroll, light **(new in v2)**

Start by importing the salary register from any payroll provider. Thapal creates the salary journal, net-pay list, PF, ESI, professional-tax and TDS liabilities, and matches the payments. Running full payroll inside Thapal is a later option, not an early commitment. From the same data it produces the PF ECR file, the ESI contribution file, professional-tax data and the quarterly salary TDS statement, in formats the AI rules watch keeps current.

### Books (v1 §10 and §16 kept)

-   Chart of accounts per entity; double entry enforced by the database.

-   Journal states: draft, reviewed, approved, posted, reversed. Posted lines are never edited.

-   Opening balances from audited financials, with missing schedules flagged rather than invented.

-   Accruals, prepayments, provisions and recurring journals under a written policy.

-   Fixed asset register from purchase invoices; book depreciation (Companies Act Schedule II useful lives) and tax depreciation kept separate. Depreciation never touches a bank account.

-   Statements: trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet in Schedule III format, cash flow, notes schedules. Marked draft until the accountant reviews them.

-   Several companies: intercompany items tagged on both sides; an elimination log for the combined view.

### Month-end close board

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Step                           Done when
  ------------------------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Statements in                  Every account has the month\'s statement

  Balances match                 Every account shows Matches statement

  To-do clear                    No open items for the month

  Sales and purchases complete   Invoices numbered without gaps; bills matched to GSTR-2B

  Adjustments posted             Accruals, prepayments, depreciation, payroll

  Tax workings tie               GST and TDS workings agree with the books

  Review notes cleared           Accountant\'s questions answered

  Locked                         Accountant locks; owner sees it; you can reopen it with a reason (and a second approver if you set one)
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### The owner\'s one-screen summary

\"November so far: sales ₹18.4 L, costs ₹11.2 L, draft profit ₹7.2 L. Customers owe ₹6.1 L (₹1.4 L overdue). You owe suppliers ₹3.3 L. GST of about ₹2.1 L is due on 20 Dec.\"

## Trusts and 80G (revision 3)

Each of the four trusts keeps its own books in non-profit format. The two with 80G approval also get donation receipts, the annual donation statement and donor certificates prepared automatically.

**The law changed this year.** From tax year 2026-27, valid 12A or 12AB registrations continue as Registered Non-Profit Organisations under section 332, and 80G approval moves to section 354 ([BestTaxInfo](https://www.besttaxinfo.in/?p=2965)). The donation statement Form 10BD is replaced by Form 113, due before 31 May after the tax year ([TaxHeal](https://www.taxheal.com/form-113-income-tax-rules-2026-pdf-download-and-key-points.html)). Donations of FY 2025-26 still use the old forms. The AI rules watch keeps this mapping current.

### Books in non-profit format

-   Income and expenditure account, receipts and payments account and balance sheet.

-   **Funds kept apart:** general fund, corpus fund and earmarked funds, with every donation tagged to one.

-   **Application of income:** the share applied to the trust\'s objects this year, tracked against the minimum the rules library holds, with a warning months before year end.

-   **Accumulations:** amounts set apart for a stated purpose and period, tracked to expiry.

-   **Investments** in permitted modes only; anything else is flagged.

-   **Related-party check:** payments that benefit trustees, founders or their relatives are held for review.

-   **Foreign contributions,** if any trust receives them, stay in their designated account and are reported separately.

### Donations, receipts and certificates

1.  Donations arrive from bank statements, online payment reports and the receipt book. Donors are recognised from narrations.

2.  **Donor directory:** name, PAN, address and contact. A missing PAN triggers an automatic request link to the donor.

3.  **Receipt** issued at once as a PDF by email or WhatsApp, numbered per trust per year, carrying the approval number for the 80G trusts.

4.  **Annual statement** (Form 113, or 10BD for FY 2025-26) prepared from the donor ledger in the portal\'s upload format.

5.  After filing, the **donor certificates** (Form 114) downloaded from the portal are added back; Thapal sends each donor theirs.

### Registrations and compliance

-   Validity of each registration and approval, with renewal reminders. Renewal is due at least six months before expiry ([BestTaxInfo](https://www.besttaxinfo.in/?p=2965)).

-   The trust\'s audit report and return appear in the compliance calendar, with workings from the books.

-   Changes to the trust deed or trustees are recorded with evidence, as Governance does for companies.

-   **Trust Home:** donations this year, share applied so far, funds by type, renewals due.

## Tax and compliance

Thapal prepares every tax working and return file from the books, reminds before each due date and records the filing. A person approves and submits until approved integrations exist.

### How \"paying GST\" works without bank linking

1.  Thapal computes the liability from the books (draft).

2.  The accountant reviews; the owner approves in one tap.

3.  Thapal produces portal-ready return data and the challan amounts.

4.  The accountant or owner files on the portal and pays from the company\'s own bank.

5.  The acknowledgement and challan are forwarded to Thapal. It matches the challan to the bank debit, marks the return filed and paid, and locks that period\'s source documents.

The same five steps apply to TDS, advance tax and income-tax returns. Direct submission through government-recognised intermediaries is a phase-5 option, after accuracy is proven and KK approves.

### GST

-   Registrations per state, filing frequency (monthly or quarterly with monthly payment), composition where chosen.

-   Outward supplies from Sales: return data with HSN and document summaries.

-   Inward supplies: GSTR-2B matching (see Purchases and payables), input-credit reversals and blocked credits flagged, reverse charge identified.

-   Monthly summary return computed and tied to both the outward return and 2B; the annual return and reconciliation prepared as working papers.

-   Every rate and rule carries an effective date, so a past month is always computed with that month\'s rules.

### TDS and TCS

Deductions on vendor payments, salaries, rent and professional fees; a payable ledger; challans; quarterly statement data; certificates to deductees. TDS and TCS credits received are matched to Form 26AS and AIS.

### Income tax for individuals **(new in v2)**

-   One view per person per tax year: salary (Form 16), house property (rent ledger), business or profession, capital gains (from investments and property sales), other sources (interest, dividends).

-   **AIS check:** \"AIS shows ₹42,310 interest from SBI; your books show ₹40,100. Difference ₹2,210.\" Each difference becomes a To-do item.

-   Regime comparison and an advance-tax estimate with instalment reminders, both labelled as estimates.

-   Output: a computation sheet and return-ready data for the e-filing portal; the acknowledgement is uploaded afterwards.

-   Each family member and any HUF is a separate taxpayer with separate access.

### Income tax for companies and firms

Computation working papers, advance tax, deferred-tax schedule and tax-audit working papers where they apply, all from the same books.

### The 2025 Act transition

The Income-tax Act, 2025 governs Tax Year 2026-27 onward; FY 2025-26 returns stay under the 1961 Act ([ClearTax](https://cleartax.in/s/income-tax-act-2025-frequently-asked-questions)). Section numbers and the year label change. The rules library therefore holds both Acts with a mapping between old and new sections, and every working states which Act it uses.

### Compliance calendar

Generated per entity from its registrations: GST, TDS, PF and ESI, professional tax, income tax and ROC. Each item has an owner, status and evidence. Reminders at 7, 3 and 1 days; overdue items escalate to the accountant or company secretary.

### Who approves before filing (revision 3)

You decide, per entity and per filing type, who must approve before a filing goes out. Thapal routes it, reminds each person, and stores the approval with the filing.

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Filing                                       Suggested approval
  -------------------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Monthly GST and TDS                          You, once the close board is green; your CA reviews quarterly

  PF, ESI and professional tax                 You

  Income-tax returns for you and your family   You, after your CA\'s review

  Company and trust income-tax returns         Your CA, then you

  Audit reports (statutory, tax, trust)        The auditor signs and uploads with UDIN; Thapal supplies the pack

  ROC filings                                  Your company secretary prepares and certifies where required; you approve

  Donation statements for the 80G trusts       The trust\'s accountant, then you
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The law requires a professional\'s signature for audit reports and some certifications; everything else is your choice. Each approval is one tap from the To-do item or the filing\'s action menu, with the working, source documents and rule versions attached.

### Tax and compliance rules library (v1 §18 kept)

Each rule carries a source link, jurisdiction, effective-from and effective-to dates, version, tests and approver. Proposed changes go live only after approval. Anything needing judgement is marked \"review required\". Computations are drafts; certification belongs to a qualified professional.

## AI rules watch: rules and filing formats that update themselves (revision 3)

An AI agent reads official sources every day, works out what changed, and updates Thapal\'s rules and government file formats. Changes that affect money or filings go live after one tap from you or your CA; everything else applies itself and tells you.

### What it watches

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Area                      Official sources                                                                                                         What it keeps current
  ------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  GST                       CBIC notifications and circulars, GSTN advisories, GST portal schema releases, e-invoice and e-way bill specifications   Rates by HSN or SAC with effective dates, due dates, return tables, upload formats, thresholds

  Income tax, TDS and TCS   CBDT notifications and circulars, e-filing portal utilities, TDS return utilities, the Finance Act                       Slabs, the 1961-to-2025 section mapping, TDS and TCS rates and thresholds, return formats, due dates and extensions

  PF                        EPFO circulars and file-format notices                                                                                   Wage ceilings, contribution rates, ECR format

  ESI                       ESIC notifications                                                                                                       Wage limits, rates, contribution file format

  Professional tax          Notifications of the states and local bodies where your entities operate                                                 Slabs, due dates

  Companies                 MCA notifications and e-form versions                                                                                    Form versions, due dates, fees

  Trusts                    CBDT notices on non-profits                                                                                              Form mapping (10BD to 113), due dates, renewal rules

  Forex                     RBI directions                                                                                                           LRS limit and related tax collection
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### How a change flows

1.  **Detect:** daily check of official pages and feeds finds a new notification.

2.  **Read:** the AI extracts what changed, from when, and which of your entities it touches, quoting the source with its link.

3.  **Draft:** a proposed rule or format update, shown as before and after.

4.  **Test:** affected calculations are re-run on your data: \"The rate on item X changes from 1 Dec; 3 invoices of Company A are affected.\"

5.  **Apply:** due-date extensions and form versions with no field changes apply automatically and notify you. Anything that changes a rate, threshold, computation or file field waits for one tap. Nothing is ever applied backwards to a filed period.

6.  **Record:** every rule version keeps its source, approver and effective dates; each return states which versions it used; rollback is one tap.

### Government files that stay current

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Filing                                                       File Thapal produces
  ------------------------------------------------------------ -----------------------------------------------------------
  GST returns (monthly, quarterly, annual)                     Portal upload file in the current schema

  E-invoice and e-way bill (phase 5)                           Registration-portal format

  TDS and TCS quarterly statements                             Return file, checked with the official validation utility

  Income-tax returns (individuals, firms, companies, trusts)   Upload file for the e-filing utility

  PF                                                           ECR file

  ESI                                                          Monthly contribution file

  Professional tax                                             Each state\'s format

  Donation statement (Form 113 or 10BD)                        Portal upload format

  MCA forms                                                    Pre-filled data sheet for each e-form
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every file is checked against its current schema before download. When a format has changed, the file says so: \"Updated to the new schema on 14 Nov.\"

### Safeguards

-   AI can misread a notification. Quotes and links make each change checkable in seconds, which is why changes to money need one tap.

-   Only official sources can change a rule. News articles may prompt a check, never a change.

-   This runs on Thapal\'s server with internet access to those sites, and its monthly cost is part of decision 6.

## Governance: the company secretary workspace (new in v2)

The company secretary gets a Governance workspace that keeps each company\'s legal records and ROC filings current from the same documents and books, and signs off its compliance status for the board.

### What it holds

-   **Company master:** CIN, incorporation date, registered office, class, authorised and paid-up capital, financial year, auditors, key managerial personnel. Built from the incorporation certificate and MCA master data; every change carries its resolution and filing as evidence.

-   **People:** directors with DIN, appointment and cessation dates, KYC status, DSC holder and expiry, annual disclosures of interest and non-disqualification; KMPs; shareholders; significant beneficial owners.

-   **Capital:** allotments, transfers, share certificates or demat ISIN, a cap table, and ESOP pool movements.

-   **Statutory registers:** members, directors and KMP, charges, related-party contracts, loans, investments and guarantees. Kept digitally in the prescribed fields and printable.

-   **Meetings:** board, committee, AGM and EGM calendar; notice and agenda drafts; attendance and quorum check; minutes from templates; signed minutes uploaded; resolutions register. A resolution that needs a filing creates the filing task automatically.

-   **Compliance status board:** each obligation per company is green, amber or red with a reason. The CS signs it off monthly; it feeds the board\'s compliance report.

### ROC filings tracker

Thapal prepares the data and tracks each filing. The CS files on the MCA portal with digital signatures, then records the SRN and fee receipt. Form names and due dates live in the rules library.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Filing                                   Trigger                           Data comes from
  ---------------------------------------- --------------------------------- -------------------------------------
  AOC-4 (financial statements)             After the AGM                     Approved statements in Books

  MGT-7 or MGT-7A (annual return)          After the AGM                     Registers, capital, meetings

  ADT-1 (auditor appointment)              Appointment at an AGM             Meetings and resolutions

  DIR-3 KYC                                Periodic, per the rules library   Director records

  DPT-3 (deposits and outstanding loans)   Annual                            Loans in Books and Money

  MSME-1 (dues to MSME suppliers)          Half-yearly                       Purchases and payables

  MGT-14 (filing of resolutions)           Specified resolutions             Resolutions register

  DIR-12 (director changes)                Appointment or cessation          People

  PAS-3 (allotment)                        Share allotment                   Capital

  SH-7 (capital change)                    Increase in authorised capital    Capital

  CHG-1 (charges)                          Secured loan created or changed   Loans linked to the charge register

  INC-22 (registered office)               Office change                     Company master

  INC-20A (commencement of business)       New company                       Company master and bank evidence

  BEN-2 (beneficial ownership)             SBO declaration                   People

  LLP Form 8 and Form 11                   Annual, for LLPs                  Books and partners
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Links to the books (why this belongs in Thapal)

-   Loans to directors, related-party transactions and large investments found in the books are flagged to the CS for approval tracking. Thapal flags; the CS decides.

-   Secured loans in Money prompt a charge entry and filing.

-   DSC expiry and director KYC due dates appear in the CS\'s To-do and the owner\'s Home.

-   A governance evidence pack (registers, minutes, filings, SRNs) exports for a secretarial auditor, read-only.

-   The CS\'s ICSI membership number is recorded; UDINs are captured for certifications.

## Tax and compliance, end to end (revision 9)

Every tax figure is built from the posted books and verified tax data, under the law of its own period, and kept separate from the act of filing. Preparing, professional review, your approval, filing, payment, government acknowledgement and closure are distinct steps, each with its own evidence. This extends Tax and compliance, AI rules watch and Governance above.

### Two income-tax laws at once

The Income-tax Act, 1961 continues to govern all tax years beginning before 1 April 2026, and proceedings for those years continue under it. From 1 April 2026 the Income-tax Act, 2025 applies, and its \"tax year\" replaces the old previous year and assessment year ([Income Tax Department FAQ](https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/all-topics/e-filing-services/objective-and-scope-new-act-faq)). Thapal chooses rules, forms and section references by the period the income belongs to, not the date of filing, and keeps both rule sets live: 2025-26 income is computed under the 1961 Act even though its return is filed after 1 April 2026.

### Steps kept apart

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Step                    What proves it
  ----------------------- -------------------------------------------------------
  Obligation identified   The entity\'s registrations and the verified rule

  Draft computation       Built from posted books; stays Draft until reconciled

  Professional review     The reviewer\'s sign-off in Thapal

  Your approval           Approval with Face ID or fingerprint

  Filed                   The portal acknowledgement, uploaded or fetched

  Paid                    The challan and the matched bank debit

  Closed                  Acknowledgement held and no open item
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Filing statuses: Not started · Collecting documents · Preparing · Reconciliation pending · Ready for professional review · Reviewed · Awaiting approval · Approved · Exported · Submitted · Acknowledged · Completed · Correction required. A return never shows as filed just because an upload file was generated.

### Entity profile

Legal name; type (individual, HUF, private company, LLP, trust, proprietorship); PAN, GSTINs, TAN, CIN or LLPIN; registered address; financial year; tax and statutory registrations; accounting framework; advisers; who files what; who approves. These identifiers are stored encrypted and shown masked.

### Past years

Bring in your history already reads past returns, computations, audited accounts, GST and TDS returns, tax audit reports, challans, orders, notices, loss and depreciation schedules and trust certificates. Each figure now keeps its source page, and opening tax balances and carried-forward amounts stay provisional until you or your CA verify them.

### Income tax

-   **People:** salary, house property, business or profession, capital gains, other income, deductions, credits, advance and self-assessment tax, refunds, carried-forward losses, and an old-versus-new regime comparison where both apply.

-   **Companies and trusts:** book-to-tax reconciliation and adjustments, book versus tax depreciation, deductions, credits, advance tax, tax provision, deferred tax where applicable, trust workings and supporting schedules.

### Matching income with government data

Bank income, salary, rent, dividends, interest, investment transactions and gains, TDS and TCS credits and business records are compared with the department\'s statements (AIS, TIS and Form 26AS). Each line ends as Matched · Partly matched · Unmatched · Missing in books · Missing in tax records · Needs professional review, and every difference becomes a traceable review item.

### GST

Sales and purchase registers, classification and rate, input credit, output tax, credit and debit notes, reverse charge, advances, exempt and non-GST supplies, place of supply, reconciliation, return preparation and payment tracking. The GSTR-2B comparison sorts each purchase invoice as Matched · Not reported by supplier · Amount differs · Tax differs · Duplicate claim · Ineligible or disputed · Needs review. E-invoice and e-way bill files are prepared and validated; direct generation goes only through an authorised channel, with approval.

### TDS and TCS

Which payments attract deduction or collection; rate and threshold by effective date and context; exemption certificates; calculation; liability; challan and challan matching; quarterly return workings; certificates; corrections; history; credit reconciliation.

### Trusts

Registration and renewals, donations and donor identity, corpus and restricted funds, programme spending and utilisation, investment restrictions, audit, donation reporting, certificates, filings and history, with forms taken from the official rules for the period (see Trusts and 80G).

### Companies

Directors, shareholding, statutory registers, board and general meetings, resolutions, annual filings, auditor appointment, director compliance, MCA obligations, filing acknowledgements, SRN tracking and notices. Thapal prepares documents and upload-ready files; it never assumes authority to certify or file them.

### Payroll

The agreed scope stands: salary registers are imported, not processed. Thapal posts salary entries, reconciles payroll liabilities, and supports TDS on salary, PF and ESI schedules, professional tax, employer contributions, payment matching and reminders. Full payroll needs a separate approval.

### Statutory calendar

Obligations are generated from entity type, registrations, period, frequency, financial events and verified rules. Each carries its due date, responsible person, reviewer, documents needed, and preparation, approval, filing, payment and acknowledgement status with completion evidence, and feeds the calendar, notifications and Coming up.

### Rules library and regulatory watch

Each rule records jurisdiction, entity types, source notification, effective date, period, version, calculation, test examples, review status and approvals. The AI rules watch follows fourteen steps: find the change; fetch and keep the official source; identify provisions, dates, affected entities, calculations and forms; run regression tests; show the proposal; get approval; activate; keep the old version; allow rollback. It never changes postings, calculations or consequential rules on an unverified AI reading.

### Government-ready output

Computations, reconciliations, schedules, form data, attachments and validation results, in the officially prescribed PDF, Excel, CSV, JSON or XML schema for that period. Validation against the official schema must pass before export.

### Paying the government

1.  Calculate the liability.

2.  Prepare the payment details.

3.  Get approval.

4.  You pay through your bank or the government portal; Thapal never moves money.

5.  Import the challan.

6.  Match the bank debit.

7.  Match the challan.

8.  Settle the liability.

9.  Keep the acknowledgement.

Nothing shows as Paid without that evidence.

### Notices, assessments and appeals

Notice type, authority, entity, period, date received, reply deadline, documents, assigned professional, reply drafting, approval, submission evidence, final order, appeal and closure, with every deadline in the calendar.

### Professionals

A CA, auditor, CS, tax consultant or internal reviewer sees only the entity and work assigned, for a limited time, with comments, versions, certification status, immediate revocation and a full log. Who must certify what is set per filing type (see Who approves before filing).

### Reports

-   **Income tax:** computations for people, companies and trusts; taxable-income and income-statement reconciliations; capital gains; depreciation; credits; advance tax; payments; refunds; carried-forward losses; provisions; assessment history.

-   **GST:** sales, purchase, output and input-credit registers; GSTR-2B reconciliation; liability; reverse charge; credit and debit notes; payments; annual reconciliation; exceptions; return files.

-   **TDS and TCS:** deduction, collection, challan and certificate registers; return working; reconciliation; outstanding amounts; corrections; credit reconciliation.

-   **Companies and trusts:** compliance calendar; meetings and resolutions; directors and shareholders; ROC tracker; donation register; utilisation; registration and renewal tracker; notices; approval history.

All in PDF, Excel and CSV, JSON or XML where applicable, the official upload formats, and ZIP evidence packs.

## Everyday: bills and dues, budgets and goals, trips and claims

Plan (inside Money) shows what is coming and whether you are on track, and never posts money that has not really moved.

### Coming up (v1 §11 kept)

-   Detected from history: subscriptions, EMIs, premiums, school fees, rent, utilities, card dues, SIPs, tax instalments and compliance dues.

-   Calendar and list views. One line on top: \"December: ₹1.84 L due, ₹1.20 L paid, ₹64,000 left.\"

-   Forgotten subscriptions are surfaced: \"Two streaming subscriptions, ₹1,148 a month together.\"

-   An item is marked paid when the bank or card statement shows the payment. Thapal never pays, cancels or changes a mandate.

### Budgets and goals

-   **Budgets:** suggested from the last three months, adjustable in one tap. Companies add department, project and cost-centre budgets. Each shows budget, committed, spent and remaining, without double counting.

-   **Goals (new in v2):** a target amount and date linked to real accounts, for example a savings or education goal. Progress uses actual balances; the projection is labelled an estimate.

-   **Cash-flow look-ahead:** the next 30 and 90 days from balances, dues and expected receipts, labelled an estimate. \"Your card bill on 12 Dec may exceed the cash in HDFC Savings.\"

### Trips and claims (v1 §13--14 kept, simplified)

Revision 3 expands this into the Travel section (automatic trips and the Trip Pack); the rules below still apply.

-   A trip starts automatically when a ticket or hotel booking arrives, or by hand. Expenses in its dates and places are suggested for it.

-   Participants, splits, and who owes whom, in a compact budget-versus-actual card.

-   Multi-currency with the rate source and date kept.

-   Advances, a reimbursement claim generated in one tap, approval, and the payout matched from the bank.

-   A settlement never duplicates the bank transfer or the expense.

-   Company trips follow the company\'s claim and approval flow; personal trips stay personal.

### Monthly Money Letter (new in v2)

One page on the 2nd of each month, in the app and optionally by email or PDF. Personal: what came in and went out, net worth change and why, what is due next month, to-dos left, and any tax heads-up. Company: draft profit, who owes you, whom you owe, GST and TDS due, compliance due. It replaces the separate monthly commitments PDF.

## Calendar and Coming up (revision 8)

One calendar shows every date that matters across Thapal. Home carries a calendar icon and a short Coming up list, and both open it in one tap. The calendar shows *when* something happens; To-do shows *what someone needs to do*. Both read the same records, so a bill confirmed as paid leaves both at once. This extends Coming up in Everyday above.

### Where each feature lives

Your placement table, adopted as written. None of these adds a tab: the four places and Add stay as they are.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Feature                         Where it appears
  ------------------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------
  Calendar                        Permanent icon on Home, with a small dot when something is overdue

  Coming up                       Compact section on Home

  Notifications                   Bell icon on Home with the count of unread items that need action

  Reminders                       The calendar (by date) and To-do (as tasks)

  Voice                           Microphone in search, Ask Thapal and fields that take typing

  External integrations           Settings → Integrations

  Notification preferences        Settings → Notifications

  Calendar and reminder reports   The Reports centre and each screen\'s download menu
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The approved Signature Flow Home carries Coming up beside the net-worth summary, with the calendar and bell in its header (see Approved UIX).

### Coming up on Home

-   The next 3 to 5 events from every workspace you may see, overdue and urgent first.

-   Each line shows the date (and time when it matters), title, person or entity, a small category marker, the amount where useful, and status. Example: \"12 Dec · Amex card due · Company A · ₹38,920\".

-   Payments, travel, renewals and compliance each have their own restrained marker; overdue dates show in red.

-   Tap a line to open its record; More expands the list in place; View calendar opens the full calendar.

-   You choose which categories appear. One person\'s private workspace never shows on another person\'s Home.

-   An item leaves the list when its source shows it done (a payment, when the statement shows it) and stays in calendar history.

### What feeds the calendar

-   **Banking and cards:** dues and statement dates.

-   **Loans:** EMIs and rate resets.

-   **Travel:** trips, flights, trains, check-in and check-out, visa and insurance expiry, refund follow-ups, claim deadlines.

-   **Assets:** maintenance, AMC, warranty, insurance, physical verification, vehicle papers.

-   **Properties:** rent due, lease renewal and escalation, property tax, utilities, insurance, inspections.

-   **Investments and deposits:** FD and RD maturities, planned investments.

-   **Business:** customer and supplier dues, month-end and year-end close, reimbursement approvals.

-   **Tax and compliance:** GST, TDS and TCS, advance tax, ROC and trust filings and renewals, from the verified rules in AI rules watch, only for the entities they apply to.

-   **You:** recurring commitments and your own reminders.

### Views

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Device         Calendar
  -------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  iPhone         Compact month with dots, agenda below, filters in one sheet

  iPad           Week or month with filters in a sidebar and the event detail alongside

  Computer       Day, Week, Month, Year and Agenda; filters; keyboard shortcuts; bulk actions
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Lists: Upcoming, Overdue and Completed. Filters: personal, family, company, trust, trip, account, asset, property, module, event type, priority, person responsible and status.

### Every event opens its record

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Event                            Opens
  -------------------------------- --------------------------------------
  Card due                         The card

  EMI                              The loan and its schedule

  Flight or hotel check-in         The trip itinerary or booking

  Reimbursement                    The claim

  Rent due                         The property and tenant

  Insurance renewal                The policy

  Maintenance                      The asset

  FD maturity                      The deposit

  Tax deadline                     The working for that filing

  Missing document                 The document request

  Approval                         The approval record
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

Event detail shows date and time, entity, amount, priority, status, source, action needed and documents, with an **Open record** button.

### Staying correct

-   Each event comes from a record and carries a permanent ID, so the same document uploaded twice never duplicates an event.

-   A rescheduled flight, revised EMI schedule, renewed policy, extended lease or verified payment updates its event automatically, with history kept.

-   Time zones are kept: a Dubai check-in shows Dubai time and your time.

-   You can drag only events you created. Statutory, bank and contract dates move only when their source record changes, under its approval rule.

### Apple, Google and Outlook calendars

Phase 3 adds a private subscription link (ICS) per workspace, with a secret token you can revoke, and privacy titles such as \"Payment due\" instead of \"Amex ₹38,920\". Apple, Google and Outlook calendars all accept it. Subscribed calendars refresh on the calendar app\'s own schedule: Google\'s often takes several hours, historically up to about 24, and cannot be forced; Apple Calendar on a Mac lets you choose the interval ([source](https://nocal.app/help/ics-and-subscriptions/why-subscribed-calendars-dont-update-instantly)). So time-critical reminders always come from Thapal itself. Two-way Google and Outlook sync through their own connections comes later (see Decisions).

### Downloads

Calendar PDF; Excel obligations schedule; CSV and ICS export; daily agenda; monthly and annual obligations; compliance calendar by entity; travel itinerary calendar; loan payment schedule; asset maintenance and property obligation calendars; upcoming payments; overdue obligations.

## Notifications and reminders (revision 8)

One notification engine serves every module, and every notification points to a saved record. A notification never creates or changes money by itself, and marking a reminder done never means a bill is paid: only the statement confirms that.

### Five kinds

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Kind               Examples
  ------------------ -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Information        Documents read, report ready, transactions matched

  Action needed      Expense to review, claim to approve, missing document, unmatched bank row, accounting exception

  Upcoming           Payment due, departure, renewal, maturity, compliance date

  Overdue            Unpaid obligation, unsettled claim, missed filing date, unanswered document request

  Security           New device, unusual sign-in, permission change, broken integration
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each notification stores its permanent ID, source module and record, workspace, recipient, category, priority, created and due times, message, actions, channels, delivery status, read and done status, escalation history and audit data. Banking, cards, expenses, claims, travel, loans, investments, assets, properties, business accounting, tax, documents, reports and security all raise notifications through this engine; none builds its own.

### Reminders

Reminders are automatic or your own: one-time, recurring (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly or custom), or triggered by an event, document, payment, approval or follow-up.

Dates are read from documents. A card statement gives a payment reminder, a policy a renewal, a loan agreement an EMI schedule, a lease rent and expiry dates, a ticket a departure, an FD advice a maturity, a tax notice a reply deadline, a warranty its expiry. A date Thapal is unsure of asks you before it counts.

On a reminder you can open it, snooze it, reschedule it (your own only), assign or delegate it, add a note, change priority, mark it done, see its evidence and history, or open its record.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Obligation            Default reminders, all changeable
  --------------------- ------------------------------------------------------
  Card payment          7, 3 and 1 day before, and on the day

  Insurance renewal     30, 15 and 7 days before, and on expiry

  Travel                7 days and 1 day before, and on departure day

  Statutory             Your chosen lead times against the verified due date
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

Also: quiet hours, your time zone, holiday and weekend awareness, repeat-until-done for chosen obligations, escalation to a second person, and silence once the source confirms completion. Month-end schedules and daylight-saving changes abroad are handled.

### Grouping

\"Company A --- 4 documents need attention\" replaces four separate alerts and opens to the four. Grouping is by organisation, person, trip, asset, property, account, due date, category or transaction. Each item keeps its own read and done state; urgent items rise to the top; unrelated money matters are never merged. Security alerts are never grouped.

### Acting from a notification

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Notification           Actions
  ---------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Card due               View card · Review amount due · Payment instructions · Follow up later

  Claim to approve       View claim · See receipts · Approve or reject · Ask a question

  Missing document       Upload · Request it from someone · Open checklist

  Travel                 Open itinerary · View booking · Open documents

  Asset maintenance      Open asset · History · Create work order

  Rent                   Open property · Tenant ledger · Check payment match
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Approving, exporting or changing access from a notification still needs your role and Face ID or fingerprint, and is logged. A notification can never skip an approval or a professional\'s sign-off.

### Delivery, tracked honestly

States: Created · Queued · Sent · Accepted by provider · Delivered (only when the provider confirms) · Failed · Retrying · Read (where visible) · Acknowledged · Cancelled. Accepted by provider is never shown as delivered. Failures retry with growing gaps, never send twice, expire when stale, fall back to the next allowed channel and escalate when critical. Admins see a reliability dashboard: generated, sent, confirmed, failed, retrying, acknowledged, critical unresolved, and failures by channel.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Channel    Works when                                                                                                                                  Note
  ---------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  In-app     Always                                                                                                                                      Notification Centre and the bell count

  Push       Android and computers in the browser; iPhone and iPad on 16.4 or later only once Thapal is added to the Home Screen and opened from there   Apple allows web push only to Home Screen web apps ([source](https://documentation.onesignal.com/docs/en/web-push-for-ios)); first-run setup guides this

  Email      Always                                                                                                                                      The fallback for anything critical

  WhatsApp   After Meta approves a WhatsApp Business account and its message templates                                                                   Meta charges for business messages

  SMS        After sender and template registration on the telecom DLT platform                                                                          Required for business SMS in India
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Notification Centre

Views: All · Unread · Action needed · Upcoming · Overdue · Completed · Security. Search, filter, group, sort, multi-select, mark read, snooze, open record, history and preferences. The bell count is computed from saved unresolved items, so it stays right after refreshes, retries and bulk actions.

### Daily and weekly briefings

Optional. Daily: today\'s obligations, payments coming up, travel, approvals waiting, overdue tasks and exceptions. Weekly: payments this week, trips, renewals, maturities, property obligations, compliance dates and unsettled claims. You choose the time, channel and contents.

### Settings

-   **Settings → Notifications:** channels for each kind, quiet hours, lead times, briefings, who else is reminded, escalation.

-   **Settings → Integrations:** one page for every connection: Gmail and Outlook mail, WhatsApp Business, Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Apple, Google and Outlook calendars, Tally export and import, broker and demat imports, valuation providers, travel booking intake, and the device\'s camera, microphone, files, share sheet and biometrics. Each shows the provider, account, status, permissions, data read, last sync, errors, whether it needs reconnecting, any usage cost, and Disconnect.

Every integration needs your explicit consent, takes the least access, stores secrets securely, can be revoked at once, is monitored for errors, never duplicates, records the source of each item, is audited, never writes money anywhere, and asks before anything with consequences. Availability depends on each provider\'s access rules, approval and cost. This extends Integrations under Security above.

### Reports

Reminder register; upcoming, overdue and completed reminders; agendas; notification history; delivery report; integration health; sync errors; reminder completion audit. All in PDF, Excel and CSV, calendar ones also as ICS, and every export respects the workspace and your access.

## Voice input (revision 8)

A microphone appears wherever speaking saves typing, and what you say always becomes an editable draft. Voice can find, draft and remind; it can never approve a payment, a filing, an access change or anything that cannot be undone.

### Where

Search and Ask Thapal; expenses and cash entries; trips; claims; asset maintenance notes; property inspections; calendar and reminders; comments on documents; questions to your accountant; audit observations.

### How it works

1.  Tap the microphone; a clear recording indicator shows.

2.  Speak.

3.  The words appear as you speak, and you can edit them.

4.  Thapal picks out what it understands: amount, category, payment method, trip, entity, date.

5.  The draft appears, with anything uncertain marked for you to confirm.

6.  Save or submit through the normal flow and its approvals.

### Examples

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  You say                                                                         Thapal prepares
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  \"Paid 1,500 rupees for parking during the Chennai trip using cash\"            A draft expense: ₹1,500, Parking, Cash, Chennai trip, and the entity if clear

  \"Remind me to pay the credit-card bill two days before the due date\"          Asks which card if you have several, then a reminder tied to that card\'s due date

  \"Remind me to follow up on the Dubai hotel refund\"                            A follow-up reminder linked to that refund

  \"Show company expenses for October\" or \"Which payments are due tomorrow?\"   The matching view or list

  \"Download the property expense report\"                                        The statement, after the usual Face ID check for exports
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A voice command never moves a contract or statutory due date, and an ambiguous command asks before acting.

### Languages

English first; Tamil and Hindi, including mixed speech, follow. Speech recognition built into browsers and phones varies in quality for Tamil and Hindi, so those will likely need a paid speech-to-text service charged by the minute. Each language goes live only after passing a test of 200 real financial phrases (amounts in lakh and crore, bank and card names, Indian place names) at an accuracy you approve.

### Privacy

Microphone permission is asked once and recording is always visible. Audio is processed securely and deleted after transcription unless you choose to keep it; only the text is saved with the record. Voice follows the same roles as typing, and consequential actions started by voice are logged.

## Reports, Ask Thapal and Health check

Laypeople get a short shelf of plain reports and can ask questions in their own words; professionals get the full catalogue. Every number traces to its source.

### Reports

**Layperson shelf (six reports):**

1.  Monthly Money Letter

2.  Where my money went (by category, merchant and person)

3.  Net worth statement (with sources and dates)

4.  Coming up (next 90 days)

5.  Tax year summary (income heads, tax paid, credits, what is left)

6.  Trip or claim statement

**Professional catalogue:** the twelve report families of v1 §20 are kept unchanged, with their standards: every report states workspace, basis, period, currency, time generated, filters, completeness and draft or reviewed status; Excel, CSV and PDF totals agree with the screen and with each other; statutory layouts are versioned and never presented as approved forms without validation.

**New in v2:**

-   **Tap any cell** to open its transactions, then the documents.

-   **Scheduled reports** and share links that expire, for a banker or a CA.

-   **Loan or visa pack:** net worth statement, six months of statements, tax returns and GST returns in one watermarked bundle with an expiring link.

### Ask Thapal (new in v2)

-   A question bar on every screen: \"How much did I spend on fuel since April?\", \"Which customers owe more than 60 days?\", \"When does my car insurance expire?\", \"Show me the laptop invoice.\"

-   **How it stays accurate:** a language model turns the question into a defined, read-only query. The numbers come from the database, never from the model.

-   Every answer shows the filters used and the transactions or documents behind it. If it cannot answer, it says so and suggests the nearest report.

-   It can offer actions (open a report, set a reminder) but never posts, approves or files.

-   It sees only what the asker\'s role can see. Questions are logged; only the minimum data needed is sent to the model provider.

### Health check (v1 §21 kept)

-   **Owner view:** \"Books health: 3 things to fix\", each with a plain reason and a button. If a score is shown, its parts are visible: statements complete, balances matching, to-do age, documents attached, returns filed on time, compliance current, valuations fresh.

-   **Daily checks:** missing statements, broken balance continuity, unmatched settlements, unexplained journals, negative balances, stale valuations, unsupported tax treatment, duplicate sources, expired documents.

-   **Accountant and auditor view:** issues by severity, entity, period and owner, with resolution evidence kept.

-   A visible note: a healthy score is not an audit opinion or a statutory certification.

## Completion and Health Centre (revision 9)

One screen answers \"Is everything financially up to date?\" for each person, company and trust, and every tick on it is earned by evidence. It brings the accounting control centre, the cross-module reconciliation and the Health check into one place. Opening a workflow or uploading a file never counts as done.

### What it shows for each entity

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Check                        Done when
  ---------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------
  Statements received          Every account and card has statements covering the period

  Accounts reconciled          Statement closing balances equal ledger balances

  Documents processed          No document is waiting to be read or reviewed

  Expenses classified          No expense lacks a category, owner or evidence decision

  Reimbursements               Every claim is settled or tracked with a due date

  Investments reconciled       Holdings and gains agree with the latest statements

  Asset register reconciled    Register equals ledger carrying value

  Property income reconciled   The rent schedule matches bank credits

  Loans reconciled             Ledger balance equals the lender statement

  Tax workings                 The current period is prepared and reconciled

  Compliance                   No obligation is overdue

  Financial statements         Trial balance balances and statements exist for the closed period

  Approvals                    None waiting

  Exceptions                   None unresolved
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Each amber or red item opens the exact action that clears it.

### Cross-module agreement test

Every day Thapal proves that each module\'s total equals its control account in the ledger: expenses, travel, claims, assets, properties, investments, loans and tax. A mismatch becomes a high-priority item and is never corrected automatically.

### Integrity monitor

It checks continuously for an unbalanced ledger, duplicate posting attempts, orphaned records, missing source references, wrong owners, postings that cross entities, and subledgers that do not reconcile. Any failure is a high-priority review item.

### Risk and exception watch

Duplicate effects, unexplained balances, unusual investment transactions, missing tax credits, unusual deductions, asset-register differences, inconsistent net-worth values, unreconciled loans, missing statutory documents, overdue compliance, permission anomalies, failed integrations and failed backups. Each points to its evidence.

### Group accounts

-   The consolidation scope is set per group view: which entities are in, and how each is owned (fully, jointly, or with a minority share).

-   Intercompany balances and transactions are eliminated; related-party transactions are listed for disclosure.

-   Minority shares are shown separately, and a part-owned entity is never counted at 100%.

-   Consolidation follows each entity\'s accounting framework, and your CA approves the scope (Decision 45).

### Correcting a closed period

A locked period is never edited. A correction found later is posted in the current open period as a prior-period adjustment, linked to the original entry and explained. If it is material and you approve, the period is reopened with a reason, the change is made by reversal, and every affected statement gets a new version. Either way the original stays visible.

### Approvals survive interruptions

A pending approval is saved on the server the moment it is created. A crash, an expired session or a lost connection never loses it; it stays in To-do on every device until someone acts on it.

## Report standard (revision 9)

Every report, financial or statutory, follows one standard, and its preparation status is earned by checks, never picked from a menu. This sits on top of the Detailed Expenditure Statement and every other report.

### What every report carries

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Capability         Requirement
  ------------------ ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  Entity             Person, company, trust, family or group

  Period             Custom dates, month, quarter, financial year or tax year

  Context            Trip, asset, property, account, project or category

  Sources            Every figure traceable to its records and documents

  Rule version       The accounting or tax rule version used

  Reconciliation     Totals agree with the ledger and subledgers, and the report says so

  Version            Each generated version is kept and can be reproduced

  History            Who generated, downloaded and shared it

  Approval           Review and approval history

  Security           Exports respect role and entity permissions

  Schedule           Optional automatic delivery to authorised recipients
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Formats

PDF for the formal report; Excel for the working, with formulas; CSV for transaction-level data; ZIP for evidence and originals; JSON or XML for authorised integrations and prescribed formats; ICS for calendar events; official government formats where verified. Totals agree across every format.

### Preparation status, printed on every report

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Status                          Earned when
  ------------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------
  Draft                           Prepared, checks not yet complete

  Incomplete                      Checks found missing information, listed on the report

  Reconciled                      Every underlying figure agrees with the ledger and statements

  Ready for professional review   Reconciled and sent to the assigned reviewer

  Reviewed                        The reviewer has signed off

  Approved                        You or the authorised approver approved it

  Final, locked                   The period is locked; only a new version can supersede it
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Security, privacy and controls

Keep the v1 §22 security model, enforce it in the database rather than the screens, and add DPDP duties, because Thapal holds many people\'s personal financial data.

### Access

-   **Sign-in:** Google, or a passkey with Face ID (see the next part); email one-time codes as a fallback. Re-authenticate before approvals, access grants and exports.

-   **Authorisation:** row-level security on every table by workspace, entity and role, denying by default. Every server function checks permissions again. Nothing relies on hiding a button.

-   **Sessions:** a device list, sign-out of other devices, and short sessions for professional roles.

-   **Two-person rule, switched on by you per action:** reopening a locked month, bulk history changes, access grants to professionals, company master changes, and journals above the owner\'s threshold.

### Sign-in with Google and passkeys, including Face ID (revision 6)

Two buttons on the sign-in screen: **Continue with Google** and **Sign in with a passkey**. A passkey uses the phone\'s or computer\'s own lock: Face ID or Touch ID on iPhone, iPad and Mac, fingerprint or face unlock on Android, and Windows Hello on a PC.

1.  **First time:** sign in with Google, then answer one question: \"Use Face ID next time?\" One tap creates the passkey.

2.  **Every time after:** tap Sign in and look at the phone. There is no password to type or forget.

3.  **Your other devices:** the passkey syncs through iCloud Keychain or Google Password Manager, so your iPad and Mac sign in the same way.

Passkeys work in Safari and in the installed web app, so no App Store app is needed. Face ID starts when you tap the button; the browser does not allow it to start by itself.

-   **Quick lock:** after a few idle minutes (decision 27), Thapal locks and Face ID unlocks it.

-   **Step-up checks:** approvals, exports, access changes, filings and anything that moves the books ask for Face ID again, even within a session.

-   **Fallbacks:** an email one-time code, recovery codes created on day one, and a second passkey on another device.

-   **Family members and staff** without Google accounts sign up with a passkey or an email code.

-   **Professionals** must use a passkey, or Google with two-step verification.

-   **Device list:** see every passkey and signed-in device, and remove a lost phone\'s passkey in one tap.

### Fingerprint and 4-digit PIN (revision 7)

When Thapal opens, it offers Face ID or fingerprint first, with **Use PIN** just below.

-   **Fingerprint** works through the same passkey, with no extra setup: Touch ID on iPads, Macs and iPhones that have it, the fingerprint reader on Android phones, and Windows Hello on PCs.

-   **4-digit PIN:** set on a device that is already signed in, for opening Thapal quickly when Face ID or fingerprint is not available, such as wet fingers, a mask or an office computer without a reader.

Safety rules for the PIN:

-   It only unlocks a device that is already signed in. It can never sign in on a new device.

-   Each device has its own PIN.

-   Five wrong tries lock the app until a full sign-in with Google or a passkey.

-   Easy PINs such as 1234, 0000 or a birth year are refused.

-   It is kept only as a protected hash, never in readable form.

-   Approvals, exports, access changes and filings above your limit still need Face ID, fingerprint or a passkey (decision 30).

-   A 6-digit PIN can be switched on for anyone who wants extra safety.

Each person chooses Face ID, fingerprint, PIN or any mix. Family members and staff on shared office computers will usually use the PIN.

### Data

-   Files in private storage with short-lived signed links; malware scanning and PDF sanitising on upload.

-   Encryption in transit and at rest. Stored statement passwords are encrypted per workspace and can be deleted by the user.

-   An append-only event log: actor, time, source, before and after values, approval, and recovery route.

-   Point-in-time database recovery and a quarterly restore test.

-   Expiring share links, download watermarks, rate limits and protection against duplicate requests.

-   Public market prices, where licensed, may be readable without sign-in; nothing else is.

### DPDP Act and Rules (new in v2)

The Rules were notified on 13 November 2025, and most duties apply from 12 May 2027 ([AZB & Partners](https://www.azbpartners.com/?p=87799)). Build for them now:

-   A plain-language notice and consent at sign-up, with a consent log and purposes stated.

-   Rights screens: see my data, correct it, export it, and request erasure, with the legal retention that blocks erasure explained.

-   Children: a family workspace may include minors, so verifiable parental consent is needed before their data is processed.

-   A breach response runbook with the notification steps the Rules require.

-   A named grievance contact and a response tracker.

-   Processor agreements with OCR, AI-model and email providers; a preference for India-hosted processing; no use of user data to train third-party models.

### Controls carried from v1 §29

No developer or automation may delete financial data, reset workspaces, fabricate entries, double-post transfers, silently recategorise history, change historical exchange rates, start payments or mandates, file returns, enable paid infrastructure or publish without the required approval.

### Integration, backup and recovery (revision 3)

Integrations run through one controlled layer: inbound email, document reading and the AI model provider, price data, the AI rules watch, and later the approved government intermediaries. Each has its own credentials, log and off switch. If one fails, work waits in a queue and you are told; no document is lost.

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Risk                                       What protects you
  ------------------------------------------ ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  A wrong action by you or anyone else       The undo bar; every change reversible from History; deleted drafts restorable for 30 days

  A bad bulk change, import or rule update   Preview before applying; one-tap rollback of a whole import, standing rule or rule version

  Database loss or corruption                Continuous backup with point-in-time restore. Suggested target: lose at most 15 minutes of data and be back within 4 hours (decision 20)

  A lost or stolen phone                     Sign that device out remotely. Only starred documents are kept on the phone, encrypted

  Losing your Google sign-in                 Recovery codes and a second sign-in method (passkey or email code), set up on day one

  Thapal itself becoming unavailable         A full export you own: every document with an index, ledgers in Excel and CSV, and an import file for Tally if your accountant uses it. Sent monthly to storage you choose

  Backups that were never tested             A restore drill every quarter into a separate environment, with totals compared before and after
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Security, recovery and release (revision 9)

Every safeguard is enforced on the server and in the database, never only on screen, so nobody reaches another entity\'s data by changing a link, an API call or a record ID. Posted history cannot change, backups are proven by restore drills, and nothing reaches thapal.in without your explicit approval. This extends Security, privacy and controls and Building with Lovable.

### Sign-in and sensitive actions

Google sign-in, passkeys with Face ID or fingerprint, quick lock with the PIN for low-risk use, device and session lists, and remote sign-out are already specified. Face ID, fingerprint or a passkey is asked again for sensitive exports, permission changes, consequential approvals, reopening a locked period, bulk financial corrections, security settings and production releases.

### Roles and permissions

Roles: owner, family member, delegate, bookkeeper, accountant, auditor, company secretary, authorised reviewer and system administrator. Each permission is granted separately: view, upload, edit draft, propose correction, approve, post, export, share, delete unposted data, manage access, reopen periods. All are enforced by database row-level security and server functions.

### Protecting the money record

1.  Posted history is immutable.

2.  Corrections happen only by reversal.

3.  Every journal balances.

4.  Posting is idempotent: the same event never posts twice.

5.  Closed periods are locked.

6.  Source documents are preserved.

7.  The audit log is append-only.

8.  Approval history is kept.

9.  Duties are separated where more than one person works: the preparer is not the approver.

10. Bulk changes are previewed and approved.

The integrity monitor in the Completion and Health Centre watches these continuously.

### Privacy and consent

Privacy notice, consent records, purpose-based access, requests to see, correct, delete (subject to legal retention) or move data, access history, consent withdrawal, retention schedules and a breach-response workflow, on the DPDP Rules timetable above. Adult family members control their own data: managing the family umbrella never opens their private accounts.

### Documents and AI

Every uploaded file is untrusted. File types are checked, malware scanned where supported, size and processing limited, instructions hidden in documents ignored, extraction kept strictly structured, AI given only the data the task needs, credentials never exposed, model and parser versions recorded, evidence kept and accuracy measured. AI providers are approved under suitable data-processing terms and can be replaced without rebuilding the ledger.

### External connections

Explicit consent, least access, encrypted tokens, expiry and revocation, sync history, failure detection, data origin, duplicate prevention and cost monitoring. Read-only stays read-only, and no integration can bypass accounting approvals.

### Backups and restore

Backed up: the database, user and entity settings, document records, original documents, audit and approval history, and integration settings. Backups are automatic, encrypted, integrity-checked, kept under a retention policy, copied independently and proven by restore.

Proposed targets: lose at most 15 minutes of data, be back in service within 4 hours, run a restore drill every quarter, and send you a full export every month. The hosting plan must support them. If the database is on Supabase, as Lovable projects usually are, the Pro plan keeps 7 days of daily backups and point-in-time recovery is a paid add-on ([Supabase](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/backups)); daily backups alone could lose up to a day. Original documents in file storage need their own copy. See Decision 40.

### After a restore

A restore succeeds only when ledger balances, account balances, transaction counts, document links, owners, audit records, permissions, reconciliation states and reports all match. The app opening is not proof. A recovered document never posts again.

### When services fail

If document reading, email, market data, storage, notifications, government portals, background jobs or the network fail, queued work is kept and resumes safely without duplicate effects. Status shows in plain words, retries are measured, manual upload stays available, and everything that can still work keeps working. Accounting never depends on every outside service being up.

### Undo everywhere

Drafts, categories, merchant merges, asset links, trip assignments, claims, document links and bulk changes can be undone; posted entries are corrected by reversal. Each change keeps the original, the old and new values, who, when, why, the approval and the money effect.

### Environments and database changes

Development, preview and production are separate, with separate databases, and preview can never write to production. Database changes are versioned migrations: reviewed, tested on a copy, preceded by a backup, with a rollback plan and the money invariants re-tested.

### Releases need your approval

1.  Define the scope.

2.  Build.

3.  Run automated tests.

4.  Review the code.

5.  Run financial regression tests.

6.  Check permissions.

7.  Test the main user journeys.

8.  Test any data migration.

9.  Write the release summary.

10. List known limits.

11. Get your explicit approval.

12. Deploy.

13. Verify in production.

14. Keep the evidence.

Statuses: Development · Preview · Tested · Ready for approval · Approved · Published · Production verified · Rolled back. A deployment is not production-verified until step 13 passes.

### Monitoring and incidents

Failed sign-ins, unusual access, permission changes, sensitive exports, integration failures and suspicious activity raise alerts. Incidents are recorded, investigated, contained, recovered and reviewed. Legal duties apply: CERT-In requires specified cyber incidents to be reported within 6 hours of noticing them ([AZB & Partners](https://www.azbpartners.com/bank/cert-in-directions/)), and the DPDP Rules require breach notices. The incident record keeps the evidence for both.

### Your complete export

Accounts, transactions, journal entries, expenses, claims, investments, assets, properties, loans, trips, documents, schedules, reports and audit references, in Excel, CSV and JSON, with PDF reports and a ZIP of documents. It carries a documented structure, entity and permanent IDs, relationships, and a manifest with checksums, and it is tested by re-importing. Thapal is never the only place your records can be used.

### Reports

Access register; role and permission matrix; sign-in and device history; professional access; sensitive actions; approvals; corrections and reversals; exports; integration permissions and failures; AI processing audit; backup status and integrity; restore drills and verification; incidents; releases; migration checks; performance; integrity exceptions; document recovery; retention; privacy requests; complete audit pack. PDF, Excel, CSV and JSON, for authorised users only.
