### Nine journeys

1.  **First setup:** sign in, choose a workspace, upload registration, identity and bank documents, see the originals beside suggested fields, confirm or correct, map accounts, import opening schedules, validate. \"Setup complete\" appears only when the records meet requirements.

2.  **Daily review:** Home priority, To-do, Inbox, Statement Desk, original lines beside parsed transactions, matches, duplicates and part-payments, reconciliation, updated Money totals, review history. A duplicate debit cannot reuse an invoice, and a short payment stays outstanding.

3.  **Smart Add:** any Add button; camera, Files, share sheet, voice or drag-and-drop; preview and progress; classification; fields with clickable source evidence; account, entity, trip or project suggestions; duplicate and currency checks; correct or defer; an explicit confirmation of the effect (draft, link, or post only if authorised); Statement Desk intake if it holds statement lines; back to where you started. No field is ever guessed, offline uploads queue visibly, and cancelled drafts never touch the books.

4.  **Travel:** a trip from a booking, itinerary and calendar, budget, receipts and card lines linked, allocation, claim, approval and payment, refunds awaited, statement and evidence ZIP, then finance marked complete separately from the journey.

5.  **Assets and property:** upload a deed, invoice or register; owner, location, cost and account; payment and depreciation; link to a building; dated valuation; net-worth review; report. No fitting is counted twice.

6.  **Investments:** demat statement, holdings and tax lots, quantities and cash reconciled, permitted prices with their time, Stale or Unavailable when needed, net worth and report. Never \"live\" for a previous close.

7.  **Reports and close:** Report Studio, scope and format, preview with unresolved items, background export, download with an integrity check, evidence pack, accountant review, sign-off and lock. A failed export stays retryable, with no false success message.

8.  **Calendar and notifications:** an account, trip, property or recurring payment creates an event; Home and Calendar show it; a tap opens the exact record; snooze or reschedule if allowed; optional external sync with clear status.

9.  **Access and recovery:** the owner grants a scoped accountant role, identity is verified, only that workspace is visible, every action is logged, and revoking ends access at once across tabs and downloads. Interrupted work resumes without duplicates, and restores are tested in isolation.

### Screen states and words

Every screen has loading, loaded, empty (with a useful next step), partial or stale, offline, permission denied, recoverable error, hard failure, cancelled, saved-draft and success states, where they apply. Labels are plain: \"Needs your review\", \"Matched to statement\", \"Couldn\'t read this line\", \"Choose an account\", \"Saved as a draft\". Accounting terms sit behind explanations but are never hidden from accountants. Never \"100% accurate\", \"guaranteed\", \"all done\" or \"live\" without evidence. Rupees use Indian grouping, the ISO code appears when a symbol is ambiguous, negatives, zero and refunds look distinct, and every value drawn from a source shows its date and source.

Every action gives visible feedback, a link to its source, a safe retry and an undo or correcting action. Checks also cover table headers, time zones, Indian digit grouping, refunds shown distinctly and multi-currency precision.

### How it is built

1.  **Audit first:** inventory routes, components, schema and services against this section and the 111 screens, mark each Done, Partial, Missing or Blocked with evidence, and keep Statement Desk, accounting history and permissions.

2.  **Design system:** freeze tokens, type, icons, header, sidebar, bottom bar, breadcrumbs, empty, loading and error states and dialogs; compare screenshots with the captures before rolling out.

3.  **Vertical slices:** shell and Home, then accounts and Statement Desk, Smart Add, travel and claims, investments, assets and property, reports and close, and settings and security. No blank placeholder screens.

4.  **Real records:** stable IDs, server-side authorisation and one calculation layer, as in the Module-to-accounting blueprint; demo data only in preview; every write keeps provenance and approval status.

5.  **Automate safely:** extraction and suggestions are automatic; uncertain money decisions, professional sign-off and filing need explicit approval.

6.  **Test every slice:** unit, integration, accessibility, visual-regression and end-to-end tests on seeded data with hard cases, plus a defect log and a screen-by-screen coverage report.

7.  **Protect the live app:** work in preview; migrations reversible and backed up; publish only on KK\'s explicit approval, with commit, notes, screenshots, test evidence and rollback.

After each cycle the report keeps five things apart that are easily blurred: implemented, automated tests passed, tested on a real device, compliance reviewed, and approved for production. It also lists screens built, changed and untouched with routes and the preview link; before-and-after captures on all three devices; journeys run and test counts; records connected and any demo data still visible; fixes, limits, migration impact and rollback; and the status of every screen from A01 to K12.

### Release gate

KK\'s 10/10 sets the look. Production needs every critical journey, every mandatory screen, the iPhone experience, security and accounting correctness verified on a real iPhone, iPad and computer. Smart Add must be shown on safe real documents, and independent reconciliation, reports, roles and release parity demonstrated. A missing screen or an unreliable figure means not ready; a beautiful preview or a passing unit-test count is not proof.

## UIX: design language (earlier proposal; Signature Flow wins where they differ)

A fresh, Apple-inspired direction built from zero: content first, one main action per screen, numbers as the hero, calm colour, and motion that explains what changed. Nothing is reused from the discarded concepts.

### Principles

1.  **One summary and one list per phone screen.** No mosaics of cards.

2.  **One primary button per screen**, at the bottom within thumb reach.

3.  **Numbers first, words second.** Amounts are large, aligned and calm.

4.  **Colour means something.** Green only for \"matches\", amber only for \"needs you\", red only for errors and overdue items. Ordinary spending is never red.

5.  **Nothing surprises.** No auto-opening keyboard, no redirects, no stacked pop-ups; every sheet can be swiped away.

### Tokens (starting values)

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Token                  Value
  ---------------------- --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Font                   System font (SF Pro on Apple devices), Inter elsewhere; tabular figures for every amount

  Type scale (pt)        Large title 34, Title 28 / 22 / 20, Headline 17 semibold, Body 17, Callout 16, Subhead 15, Footnote 13, Caption 12

  Background, light      #FFFFFF; grouped #F2F2F7

  Background, dark       #000000; raised #1C1C1E

  Text                   Primary #1C1C1E (light) or #F5F5F7 (dark); secondary #6E6E73

  Accent (one only)      Working choice: deep green #0E7C66, to be confirmed in design review

  Matches                #34C759

  Needs you              #FF9F0A

  Problem or overdue     #FF3B30

  Spacing                4-point grid; screen margins 16 (iPhone), 24 (iPad), 32 (desktop)

  Touch targets          At least 44 × 44 pt

  Corners                12 for panels, 10 for controls; hairline separators; almost no shadows

  Motion                 200--300 ms ease-out; respects Reduce Motion
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Amounts

-   ₹ with Indian grouping (₹12,34,567.00). An option switches to international grouping.

-   Summaries may show ₹12.3 L or ₹1.2 Cr; a tap shows the exact amount. Rounding is display-only; arithmetic stays exact.

-   Money in shows as \"+₹\" in green; money out shows \"−₹\" in primary text.

-   Every amount has a screen-reader label in words.

### Components (one library, used everywhere)

Summary header · grouped list row · amount cell · status pill (Matches, Waiting, Needs you) · evidence chip (\"From HDFC statement, Oct, page 3\") · bottom sheet · Review split view · progress card · undo bar · empty state with one action · skeleton loading · segmented control · \"Why?\" popover.

### Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA contrast (4.5:1 for body text), Dynamic Type up to the largest sizes without truncating amounts, full VoiceOver and keyboard support, and dark mode on every screen from the start.

An **Accountant view** switch, available to owners and professionals, adds account codes, debit and credit columns, journal numbers and confidence scores to any list.

### The first ten minutes (new in v2)

1.  Sign in, then one question: \"Who is this for?\" (Just me / Me and my family / My business / I was invited as a professional).

2.  \"Add your latest bank statement\" (upload or forward). Thapal creates the account, shows the balance and last month\'s spending in under a minute.

3.  At most three questions: which accounts are yours, which are business, and your name for the household.

4.  Home appears with a first insight and a **Complete your picture** checklist: bank accounts, cards, investments (one CAS), insurance, loans, property, tax (AIS), company documents. Each item says what it unlocks.

No setup screens come before value. Everything in Setup can be changed later.

### UIX acceptance (revision 9)

Signature Flow is the approved look; release still needs testing on a real iPhone, iPad and computer, and these rules hold in the approved Signature Flow design.

-   **Home holds** the money overview, key accounts, pending actions, Coming up, the calendar icon, the bell, quick Add, search and the workspace switcher. Personalisation never hides an obligation.

-   **Navigation:** Home · Money · Add · To-do · Records, with search, reports, calendar, notifications, settings and the workspace switcher one tap away.

-   **Search everywhere:** transactions, accounts, documents, companies, expenses, trips, claims, assets, properties, investments, loans, reports and calendar events; each result opens the exact record.

-   **Smart Add:** an instant preview, no unexpected redirects, no keyboard popping up unasked, visible progress for long work, clear extracted fields, bulk review, safe correction, original kept.

-   **Two kinds of action look different:** everyday taps are light and instant; consequential approvals (money, filings, access) get their own clearly marked step with Face ID.

-   **No clutter:** no unnecessary cards, menus or confirmation screens.

-   **iPhone:** one-handed, bottom navigation, fast scanning, voice, compact calendar, large touch targets. **iPad:** split views, sidebar, document beside the data, keyboard and trackpad, both orientations. **Computer:** dense tables, filters, multi-select, shortcuts, resizable panels, document and accounting side by side.

-   **Speed:** Home, Money and To-do show useful content in about 2 seconds and Add in about 2.5 seconds, measured on named devices, connections and data; large uploads and reports run in the background.

**The non-accountant test.** Someone with no accounting training must, unaided, upload a statement, understand their balance, see what needs them, review an expense, find a receipt, open a trip or asset, view a report and download the records they need.

## Action menus: on every record (revision 3)

Every row and every detail screen has a ••• menu, swipe actions on iPhone and right-click on desktop. You see plain actions such as Edit, Delete and Cancel; Thapal keeps the books audit-safe behind them.

  Receipt or document      View, download, share, move, link, replace, rename, request missing, delete

  Trip                     Edit, add document or photo, add expense, change billing split, generate Trip Pack, submit claims, close, reopen, cancel, delete

  Sales invoice            Edit (draft), send, duplicate, record payment, send reminder, issue credit note, cancel, download

  Vendor bill              Edit, approve, schedule payment, record payment, dispute, cancel

  Bank account or card     Rename, change owning entity, set alerts, add statement, close, archive

  Deposit or investment    Edit, record renewal, record maturity, revalue, sell or redeem, close

  Donation (trusts)        Edit, issue receipt, resend receipt, move to fund, cancel receipt

  To-do item               Answer, assign, snooze, ask my accountant, dismiss with reason

  Standing rule            Edit, pause, apply to past items (preview first), delete

  Report or Trip Pack      Regenerate, download (PDF, Excel, CSV, ZIP), share link, schedule, revoke link

  Access grant             Extend, change scope, revoke now

  Journal (accountant)     Edit (draft), submit, approve, reverse, copy

  Filing                   Open working, open portal, mark filed, add acknowledgement, add challan
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### What Delete and Cancel really do

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Record\'s state                Delete                                                                                                        Cancel
  ------------------------------ ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Draft, never posted            Removed; restorable from History for 30 days                                                                  Draft discarded

  Posted, month still open       A reversal is posted; History shows \"Deleted by you on 8 Nov\"; balances update                              Invoices: credit note, or e-invoice cancellation within the portal\'s window. Bills: reversal

  Month locked or return filed   Shown as \"Correct in next period\": a correcting entry is proposed for your accountant, and you approve it   Same as delete

  Document used by records       Archived with a reason instead                                                                                Not applicable
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every action ends with an undo bar. Bulk actions work on selected rows. Anything destructive states its effect before you confirm: \"Removes ₹4,200 from Travel and restores the Amex ending 1004 balance.\"

## Building with Lovable and GitHub: technical guardrails

Lovable can build this, provided the financial rules live in the database and each prompt changes one small, tested thing.

### 1. Put the rules where every prompt sees them

-   Commit this specification to the repository as /docs/spec-v3.md, plus /docs/glossary.md and /docs/invariants.md.

-   Paste the condensed invariants and naming rules into Lovable\'s project-level instructions so every prompt inherits them.

-   When ChatGPT or Claude writes a prompt, it works from these files, not from memory of earlier chats.

### 2. Enforce money rules in the database

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Invariant                        How it is enforced
  -------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Every posting balances           A deferred constraint trigger checks that each entry\'s lines sum to zero per currency

  Posted history is never edited   A trigger blocks UPDATE and DELETE on posted lines; corrections are reversal rows

  Locked months stay locked        A trigger rejects any posting dated inside a closed period

  No duplicate effects             Unique keys on (workspace, source fingerprint) for observations and on the idempotency key for posting requests

  Money is exact                   Integer paise (bigint) or numeric with a currency code; never floating point. Rates are numeric with source and date

  One way to post                  All postings go through a single database function in one transaction; the app never inserts ledger rows directly

  Access is scoped                 Row-level security on every table, deny by default, by workspace membership and role

  Everything is traceable          An append-only event table written by the same functions
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 3. Background work

A job table with status, progress, attempts and error; a worker with retries and back-off; resumable steps. The screen subscribes to progress rather than waiting.

**Revision 8 additions.** Six tables carry the new engines: events for the calendar and reminders, unique on source record and kind so re-uploads never duplicate; notifications and notification_deliveries, one row per channel attempt; report_runs, the frozen snapshot each statement version prints from; id_sequences, one running number per prefix and year, never reset or reused; and trip_status_history. Trip, asset, property, claim and statement totals are database views over ledger lines, never stored numbers. Reminders, retries and briefings run as scheduled jobs in the job table above.

### 4. Environments and Git

-   Separate preview and production databases. Preview never touches production data.

-   Schema changes only as SQL migration files in Git, reviewed before they run.

-   Protect the main branch. One branch and one pull request per batch, carrying the v1 §29 handover checklist.

-   Tag every release. Publishing to thapal.in happens only on KK\'s explicit approval.

### 5. Tests that prove money is right

-   **Extraction golden files:** real sample documents per issuer with expected outputs; accuracy reported per field.

-   **Ledger properties:** balances always tie, a re-upload changes nothing, undo then redo returns the same totals.

-   **Journeys:** end-to-end tests at iPhone, iPad and desktop sizes, then on physical devices.

-   **Before and after totals** per account, category and company for every batch that touches posting.

### 6. How to prompt Lovable

-   One change per prompt, with acceptance criteria and a \"do not touch\" list.

-   Ask for the tests first, then the code.

-   Review the diff on GitHub after each batch; reject any change that writes ledger rows outside the posting function.

-   Use the existing component library (Lovable\'s default shadcn/ui and Tailwind) with the design-language tokens; ban one-off styles.

### 7. Reading documents reliably

Use fixed parsers for known bank CSV and Excel formats first; they are the most accurate. Use OCR plus an AI model only for PDFs and photos, with the output validated against a schema. Store the model and parser version with every reading.

### 8. Speed

Keep the v1 targets: first useful content in about 2 seconds for Home, Money and To-do, and 2.5 seconds for Add, measured on stated devices and data. Paginate lists, index queries, and keep running balances updated inside the posting transaction.

## Delivery gates and the requirement register (revision 9)

Nothing new is built until the existing app is mapped, and every phase passes nine gates, each with a written acceptance report. Every requirement in this document gets a permanent ID and moves forward only with evidence. The guiding journey: one upload → understanding → right entity and account → accounting entry → reconciliation → reports → reminders → audit evidence.

### Map before building (Gate 1)

Inspect the real repository and database: schema, tables and relationships, migrations, sign-in, workspaces, ownership, bank and card accounts, Statement Desk, document processing, classification, ledger and posting, reconciliation, expenses, claims, investments, travel, assets, properties, reports, calendar, background jobs and security policies. The output is the Existing Application Architecture Register: one row per feature with its current implementation, database objects, code location, API or service, screen route, related entities, posting mechanism, permissions, dependencies, tests, known problems and changes needed. Existing IDs and components are reused wherever they already meet the requirement; table names in this document are logical and never assumed.

Gate 1 is complete when tables and services are mapped, relationships are documented, no second ledger exists or is planned, every module has a defined source of financial truth, every financial event traces to evidence, cross-entity access is restricted, and any schema change has a tested migration path.

### The nine gates

  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Gate                             Proves                                                                           Evidence (revision 11)
  -------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 Existing application mapping   We know exactly what exists                                                      All seven audit registers populated; one blueprint page per module; current architecture and defects evidenced

  2 Financial integrity            One ledger, correct owners, document identity, posting controls, no duplicates   Balanced journals, duplicate protection, entity ownership, reversals and locks tested before automation expands; integrity monitor clean

  3 Automation quality             Real-document accuracy is measured and processing is safe                        Field and no-touch measures on independent real documents; an explicit threshold for graduated autopilot

  4 Cross-module integration       One event agrees everywhere                                                      Expense, claim, investment, loan, asset, property, tax, net worth and reports agree for the same event

  5 External connectivity          Approved connectors work and fail safely                                         Provider feasibility, with safe-failure and retry evidence

  6 Regulatory validation          Right rules for each period, official formats, approvals                         Official schemas, effective-date rules and professional validation for that specific feature

  7 UIX and navigation             Usable on every device and true to Signature Flow                                The 111-screen audit; visual regression against the captures; iPhone, iPad and computer accessibility and usability checks; your visual approval separately

  8 Security and recovery          Permissions, restore and performance                                             Access control, penetration and regression checks, a production-like restore, performance under load

  9 Release approval               You approve with the evidence in front of you                                    The exact build, changelog, test results, database migration and rollback, and the preview; your explicit decision
  -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Gates 1 and 2 belong to Phase 0 and must pass before Phase 1 continues; gates 3 to 9 are passed by each phase for its own scope.

### Requirement IDs

Each requirement gets a permanent ID by area, such as REQ-EXP-014 for expenses or REQ-TRV-031 for travel, with REQ-AST, REQ-PRP, REQ-INV, REQ-TAX, REQ-GST, REQ-SEC, REQ-UIX and REQ-CAL for the other areas. IDs are never reused (Decision 46). The Requirement Completion Register holds, for each: ID, section of this document, module, priority, dependencies, code location, database relationship, status, test reference, financial, security and device verification, production status, known limits and approval.

Statuses: Proposed · Approved · Not started · In development · Implemented · Partly tested · Fully tested · Production verified · Blocked. None moves forward without evidence.

### What every development batch reports

Requirements addressed; existing components reused; files and database objects changed; tests run; financial reconciliation evidence; security checks; open issues; known limits; and the next batch proposed. The standing instruction to Lovable: inspect before changing, keep what works, make small tested changes, never rebuild, never add a second financial engine, never alter live financial history without authorisation, never publish without your approval.

### The final acceptance journey

In personal, family, company and trust workspaces alike: a document is uploaded; Statement Desk reads it; the legal entity and the account or card are identified; it is matched with existing transactions; duplicates are prevented; the entry is generated and reconciled; related modules, tax workings, calendar and reminders update; reports are produced; every figure traces to evidence; authorised people review and approve; and the system recovers safely from an interruption at any step.

## V3.1 development contract (revision 11)

KK\'s gap-closure contract of 9 November 2026 controls the code audit and all development from here. It adds no new product features: it closes documentation gaps and makes acceptance measurable. Nothing in it weakens an earlier requirement, and all 50 decisions stand as agreed. It is not permission to publish.

### Precedence and conflicts

When two requirements disagree, the higher one wins:

1.  KK\'s explicit later decision.

2.  Applicable law and authoritative government forms, subject to professional review.

3.  This contract\'s technical and acceptance clarifications.

4.  The functional requirements in the rest of this document.

5.  The approved Signature Flow captures, for visual questions.

6.  Existing production behaviour, only where compatible and safe.

A conflict is never settled silently. The developer writes a Decision Needed record that cites both requirements, gives the options, their impact and a recommendation, and stops work on the affected part until KK decides. A new proposal never replaces an agreed decision on its own.

### What needs KK\'s separate authorisation

The GitHub repository may be audited, and changes prepared in an isolated branch or preview. Each of these needs a separate, explicit authorisation from KK:

-   Migrating live records or repairing production data.

-   Filing with, or paying, any outside body.

-   Transferring ownership of anything.

-   Deploying or publishing.

-   Changing DNS, including moving users to thapal.in.

ledgerline.biz stays running and untouched throughout.

### Five states, never blurred

A requirement is **specified**, **coded**, **tested**, **deployed** or **production-verified**. These are different states. Nothing is called complete because it appears in this document, a screenshot, a unit test or a developer\'s summary. The Requirement Completion Register records which state each requirement has reached, with its evidence.

### Seven audit registers

The audit delivers these seven registers from the real repository and database before any feature development is authorised. Each row keeps its evidence links and revisions.

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Register                                 One row per                 What it records
  ---------------------------------------- --------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1 Existing Application Architecture      Feature                     Route; source file; UI component; API or service; database table; migration version; relationships; owner boundary; row-level policy; posting mechanism; background job; existing tests; Implemented, Partial, Missing or Blocked; defects; proposed change

  2 111-Screen Coverage                    Screen, A01 to K12          Route or panel; parent navigation; entry and exit; purpose; source of its data; actions; approvals; layout on each device; required states; screenshot; tests; KK\'s review status

  3 Requirement Completion                 Requirement, REQ-AREA-NNN   Section of this document; contract clause; priority; dependency; implementation file; evidence; tests; financial, security and device verification; production status; known limits. IDs are never reused

  4 Financial Event and Module Blueprint   Kind of financial event     Input evidence; document identity; owning entity; financial account; duplicate-protection key; double-entry posting; matching and reconciliation; reversal; period lock; reports it feeds; permissions; exception queue; test

  5 Integration Feasibility                Outside service             Provider; API or file format offered; approval and licensing; data permissions; cost; frequency; timestamps; stale and failure behaviour; retry and back-off; duplicate protection; sandbox; status with proof. Unsupported is a valid result

  6 Visual Baseline                        Demonstrated screen         The exact approved capture; type, icons, tokens, spacing and breakpoints; the visual difference found; screens beyond the captures clearly marked as not yet approved

  7 Release and Recovery Evidence          Release                     Backups; restore point; migration forward and rollback; unbroken audit log; deployment match; results of critical journeys; security findings; KK\'s explicit approval
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every register exports to Excel and CSV. A blank or undocumented field is an open task, not a pass. Registers 1, 3 and 5 extend the ones already named in Delivery gates and the Integration feasibility register; register 4 holds the per-module blueprint pages.

### Workspaces, one intake and navigation

-   **Separate in law and in the database:** personal, adult family members, minors, companies, trusts, HUFs and other supported organisations. A combined group view shows ownership and its consolidation assumptions, and never replaces each entity\'s own books. Owning one entity never opens another adult\'s private data.

-   **One intake:** Add, email, the file picker, scheduled upload links and actions inside modules all reach the same Statement Desk path for source, reading, duplicate checks and posting.

-   **Never lose your place:** every action keeps the workspace, filters, scroll and return point. Back, Forward, deep links, Cancel, Resume draft, breadcrumbs and notification links all open the same record with the right permissions. Smart Add never redirects to a second entry screen.

### The accounting data contract

This refines the chain in Architecture: one ledger behind every module. Every financial fact travels this path, and each step keeps its own record:

source file → document version → what was read from it → economic event → owner and account → approval policy → balanced posting → bank or card reconciliation → module views → statutory drafts → reports and reminders → audit evidence.

**IDs that never change:** workspace, legal entity, person, account or card, source, document version, reading attempt, financial event, posting, posting line, match, expense, reimbursement, trip, asset, property, investment lot, loan, tax working, calendar event, report, approval and audit event. Valid existing IDs are reused, and history is never overwritten.

**Rules the database itself enforces**, not only the screens:

1.  Amounts are signed, exact decimals.

2.  Debits equal credits in every posting, for each legal entity and each currency.

3.  Each economic event has one unique key against duplicates, so it appears once even when several source files show it.

4.  One invoice cannot settle two duplicate debits in full.

5.  A part-payment leaves the balance due.

6.  Paying a card bill creates no expense.

7.  Moving money between your own accounts creates no income.

8.  Reconciled amounts agree with the bank\'s own statement balances.

9.  Posted entries cannot be edited silently.

10. A change inside a locked period needs an authorised correcting entry.

11. A reference to another workspace cannot get round its row-level permissions.

**When something is unknown:** an unknown owner, account or currency, documents that disagree, or a tax treatment Thapal does not support becomes a To-do item, never an invented posting. Automatic posting grows only after the per-document, per-issuer evidence bar of Decision 4 passes and KK\'s policy allows that kind of event. Payroll, property sales, taxes, unusual journals, locked periods and consequential approvals keep their higher approval steps however confident the reading is.

**Reading again:** each reading records the reader\'s name and version and where every field came from. Reading the same document again creates a new reading attempt and a comparison, never a second posting. Interrupted work resumes safely from durable job records, and drafts can be reversed (see Reading quality and safe reprocessing).

### Status words that are never interchangeable

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Status               Means
  -------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------
  Unknown              Not yet known; shown as unresolved

  Estimated            From an alert, a forecast or an unconfirmed source

  Source-confirmed     Matches a document such as a statement or invoice

  Reconciled           Agrees with an independent balance, such as the bank\'s statement

  Reviewed             Checked by an authorised person

  Filed                Accepted by the authority, with its acknowledgement

  Paid                 Payment proven by bank evidence and the challan or receipt

  Locked               The period is closed; changes need a correcting entry
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Filing is not payment. Reading a document is not verifying it. An alert email is not a bank statement, and a market quote is not an audited balance: bank alerts stay Estimated until the statement confirms them. Every screen says what it covers and as of when, in plain words.

### Measuring automation

This tightens The 99.9% target and Reading quality and safe reprocessing.

-   **A goal, not a release claim.** The 99.9% no-touch figure is never stated as achieved without the evidence below.

-   **Everything counted.** Each result records the total it is measured against, plus issuer, format, field, period, confidence, human corrections, exceptions and late matches.

-   **Separate measures for:** amount, date, currency, entity, paying account, category, tax, duplicate detection, card matching, bank reconciliation and posting.

-   **Money fields need control checks.** Fields with money consequences need explicit checks, such as a total that agrees with the statement, not just an AI confidence score.

-   **The bar is a minimum.** Decision 4\'s bar (99.5% on amounts and dates, 97% on category, over 200 real rows per issuer) only qualifies a document type for automation. It is not proof of a 0.1% end-to-end error rate.

-   **Independent test documents.** Proof uses documents held out from training, across formats and over time.

-   **Honest results.** Results publish confidence ranges and real failure examples. The acceptance set must show no unexplained money differences.

-   **Automation steps down** by itself when corrections or drift exceed the agreed policy.

-   **Tests stay separate.** A test document is never used to train the rule it tests.

-   **The dashboard shows its basis.** Every accuracy figure shows what was counted, out of how many, and the date.

### Integrations: at launch, later, and what they must never do

  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Integration               At launch                                                          Later, after approval                                                 Must never
  ------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------ --------------------------------------------------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Banks and cards           Statements by upload or email; alert emails give estimates only    Read-only Account Aggregator data, after a separate approval          Show a \"live balance\" it does not have, or scrape bank passwords

  Gmail and Outlook         Forwarding and intake rules                                        Direct read-only access once the provider approves                    Lose a receipt: a missed sync is flagged, tokens can be revoked, manual upload stays open

  Market data               Licensed or official end-of-day prices and NAVs, where permitted   Intraday prices, only with an approved feed                           Invent a quote: date, exchange and Stale or Unavailable are always shown

  Income-tax, GST and MCA   Prepare, validate and export                                       Direct filing through an intermediary, after that phase is approved   Imply filed, paid or certified without the authority\'s acknowledgement

  Calendars                 A private, revocable ICS link per workspace                        Two-way Google and Outlook sync in its approved phase                 Hide a delay or create duplicate events

  Voice                     English, then Tamil and Hindi once validated                       An approved speech provider                                           Act before showing the transcript, or approve anything by voice

  WhatsApp and SMS          Not needed for launch                                              After provider consent, templates and cost approval                   Treat a delivered message as the financial task being done

  Storage and exports       Original files and a complete export                               Outside cloud storage you choose                                      Skip checksums, quota and failure handling, recovery or scoped permissions
  --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The provider register records, for each service: capability; its documentation link and revision date; who owns the credentials; data permissions; where data is hosted and the processor\'s terms; cost per action; test account; approved environment; sync interval; retry budget; failure states; feature switch; and KK\'s approval. An outside service being down never blocks manual or offline work.

### Statutory output: earned, not claimed

The Income-tax Act, 2025 applies from 1 April 2026, and earlier periods keep their own rules (see Tax and compliance, end to end). Neither fact certifies any schedule Thapal produces. For every entity, year and filing type, Thapal records the rule source, official form or schema, effective date, applicability, amendment history, validation result, professional reviewer, submission and acknowledgement, and later the payment proof. A secondary article is never treated as the official format. The same applies to GST, TDS and TCS, trusts and 80G, Companies Act and MCA filings, payroll statutory data, Malaysian reporting (only for entities with that profile, Decision 49) and the DPDP privacy duties as each phase begins.

An output may be called **regulatory-ready** only when it uses the specific official form or schema and a qualified reviewer confirms it applies. Any rule change that alters money, filing content or classification needs explicit approval and regression tests. The rules watch may apply a harmless due-date extension by itself (Decision 16) only after the government source is authenticated, the effective date checked, the change logged and kept reversible.

### Access, sessions and recovery checks

This sharpens Security, recovery and release.

-   **Permissions on the server and database:** view, upload, edit draft, propose, post, approve, export, share, delete unposted data, manage access and reopen. A professional\'s verification is real, never a cosmetic label, and adult family members opt in to shared visibility.

-   **Cross-entity tests** try direct record IDs, exports, search, background jobs and share links.

-   **No weaker route in:** Google sign-in, passkeys, Face ID, fingerprint and the 4-digit PIN never become an easier path to privileged actions. The PIN is tied to its device, rate-limited and revocable, never replaces server sign-in, and never allows consequential approvals or sensitive exports.

-   **Sessions** lock after 5 idle minutes on phones and 15 on computers (Decision 27), with a fresh check before privileged actions. Expiry and revocation are tested across open tabs and on downloaded report links.

-   **Recovery targets** of 15 minutes of data and 4 hours of downtime are targets, met only with paid capabilities and proven restores. Restore tests cover separate database and file-storage copies, point-in-time recovery, checksums, encryption keys, identities and permissions, reconciled totals, job resume and the original evidence. Quarterly isolated restore drills and a monthly full export to KK stay mandatory.

-   **Security minimums belong to Phase 0**, not Phase 5 (see Roadmap).

### Building in slices

-   Gate 1 finishes before any feature grows.

-   Before each batch, write down its REQ IDs, affected screen IDs, dependencies and the tests that prove nothing else broke.

-   Small, isolated commits. Modules that already pass are not rebuilt.

-   One vertical slice must run from source to books, reconciliation and reports, with evidence, before another feature family can be called integrated.

-   **Speed:** Home, Inbox and Expenses within 2 seconds and Statement Desk within 2.5 seconds, measured at the median and the 95th percentile, cold and warm, recording data size, device and network. Longer work shows a skeleton and plain progress.

-   Imports, reading, report jobs and bulk changes run in the background, durably, with progress and resume.

-   No success message before the work is real: not for unsaved writes, unverified balances, undelivered notifications or unfinished exports. A failed export retries under the same job ID and keeps its integrity check.

### Sign-off checklist

Release needs every box ticked, each with its evidence.

-   [ ] Every requirement in this document mapped without loss; all 50 agreed decisions kept.

-   [ ] All 111 screen IDs have an owner, route, data contract, actions and states, and real-device screenshots or an explicit Blocked status.

-   [ ] The exact approved captures used for the screens they show; every other screen approved separately by KK.

-   [ ] The final Thapal Option 02 SVG and wordmark reviewed in every context; no placeholder logo or lowercase name.

-   [ ] The existing database, code, permissions, history and upload engine audited; no second ledger or intake.

-   [ ] The ledger reconciles independently to bank statements; duplicate, part-payment and refund cases pass.

-   [ ] The integrated journeys pass in personal, family, company and trust workspaces, with nothing leaking between them.

-   [ ] Real-document automation figures and exceptions reviewed by KK.

-   [ ] Market and statutory sources dated, licensed or verified; no unsupported \"live\" or \"filed\".

-   [ ] Every acceptance test in this document mapped to a real test and its evidence; failures stay open.

-   [ ] Security, backup, restore and release match verified.

-   [ ] All blocking findings resolved, and KK explicitly authorises the intended deployment.

### Standing instruction to the developer

> You are auditing and implementing Thapal against this master specification and its V3.1 development contract. Keep every requirement, all 50 decisions, the Signature Flow visual target, the central Statement Desk intake engine and the existing financial records. First produce the seven evidence-backed registers from the real repository and database. Documentation is not implementation. Reconcile every one of the 111 screen IDs and every acceptance test to code, routes, data, screenshots and tests. Raise conflicts or missing evidence to KK with options, impact and a recommendation. Work in isolated previews and small, tested vertical slices. Never invent an account, balance, price, transaction, tax rule, source, provider capability or completion status. Never touch production data, post consequential entries, file, pay, deploy, rename the live domain or publish without KK\'s explicit authorisation. After each batch, report changed files, register IDs, passing and failing tests, financial integrity results, visual comparisons, unresolved blockers, rollback and the preview. Approval is separate from implementation, testing and publication.

### Still awaiting evidence

The code audit is in progress, so nothing yet proves:

-   That the code covers the requirements, or that the architecture register is complete.

-   That the database enforces the posting and permission rules.

-   The final Option 02 logo, or approved designs for all 111 screens; an accurate iPad capture does not exist yet.

-   Real iPhone, iPad and computer testing.

-   Market-feed licences, provider approvals or tested government templates.

-   Production backups and recovery, or release match.

These are evidence tasks that block release, not gaps in the specification. The specification is complete as a development contract; the application is not yet verified.

## Roadmap and build batches

Six phases follow your own workstreams, each ending at a gate that must pass before the next starts. Correctness and navigation come first because everything else depends on them.

![roadmap · 6 phases, 6 exit gates](media/image7.png){width="6.0in" height="5.491070647419073in"}

roadmap · 6 phases, 6 exit gates

Phase 0 is in progress. Monthly GST and TDS workings already arrive with Phase 1\'s month close; Phase 4 completes the filing files, trusts, ROC filings and the AI rules watch.

### Phase 0 build batches (one Lovable prompt series each)

1.  **Posting function and database invariants** (see Building with Lovable, item 2). Pass: a re-upload of any statement changes no totals; an unbalanced entry is rejected.

2.  **Event log and reversals.** Pass: every change in History shows actor, before, after and a working undo.

3.  **To-do engine.** Saved unresolved conditions with a server-side count. Pass: the count equals the open conditions after refresh, retry and bulk actions.

4.  **Navigation shell.** Four places, Add sheet, workspace switcher, the action-menu component, new labels, existing screens placed inside. Pass: no screen is reachable only by redirect.

5.  **One Add flow.** Smart Add uses the same engine; image preview at once; no keyboard opening by itself; no redirect. Pass: photo, PDF and CSV all reach Review in place.

6.  **Review pattern.** The side-by-side screen used by every document type.

7.  **Transfers and card bills.** One-sided items wait; card payments settle without new spending. Pass: v1 journeys 4 and 5.

8.  **Balance check states** per account. Pass: no tick without matching numbers and links.

9.  **History audit from 1 April 2026.** Every account and statement checked for gaps, breaks and duplicates; findings become To-do items, not silent fixes.

10. **Regression pack for the v1 §25 complaints:** stale counts, select-all, third-party transfers, auto keyboard, blocking jobs, Home layout, Smart Add behaviour, redirect, image preview, account saves, report retry, download integrity, Excel/CSV mismatch, budget safeguard, merchant merge undo, iPad split view, decimals, net worth visibility.

11. **Sign-in with Google and passkeys (Face ID and fingerprint), the 4-digit PIN,** quick lock and step-up checks. Pass: test 49.

12. **Shared upload component** used by every screen: multi-select, folders on computers, ZIP, background upload with resume, and multi-page joining and splitting. Pass: tests 51 and 52.

13. **Apply for Google\'s Gmail verification and security assessment.** Paperwork that runs alongside the build. Pass: application submitted with everything Google asks for.

**Revision 9:** Phase 0 now starts with Gate 1, mapping the existing application into the Architecture Register and one blueprint page per module, and ends with Gate 2, financial integrity. Gates 3 to 9 apply to every later phase for its own scope (see Delivery gates and the requirement register).

**Revision 11:** Gate 1 now delivers all seven audit registers of the V3.1 development contract. Security minimums are part of Phase 0, not postponed to Phase 5: server and database permission checks, session locking, the append-only audit log, configured backups with a tested restore, and the release approval steps. Phase 5 extends them with point-in-time recovery, regular drills and incident response.

### Later phases, matched to your workstreams

-   **Phase 1 --- Real document extraction, accounting entries, reconciliation, financial statements and closing:** group directory, Money Map, family umbrella, upload requests, passkey sign-in, Add with automatic email fetching and bank alert emails, the shared upload component with multi-page documents, expense management, banking hub, Vault, history import, action menus, the pipeline, close board, bookkeeper workbench, accountant workspace and Audit room, Coming up with the Home calendar icon, the unified calendar, the notification engine and Notification Centre, Settings → Integrations, one-expense views and the Detailed Expenditure Statement, permanent IDs, Money Letter, the Completion and Health Centre, the report standard, the reading quality dashboard, first-ten-minutes onboarding, and added features 2 to 7.

-   **Phase 2 --- Loans and financed assets, and investments and net worth (side by side):** loan intake, EMI schedules, lender reconciliation, financed assets, asset management (registers, labels, verification, depreciation, register import and asset-to-ledger reconciliation); CAS and broker import, deposits, commodities, gold, land, insurance, forex and LRS, returns and gains with tax lots, corporate actions, price status, dated and consolidated net worth, estate readiness, and added feature 8.

-   **Phase 3 --- Business operations:** invoicing with UPI QR, customers, suppliers and GSTR-2B matching, property management, tenants and property-to-ledger reconciliation, asset maintenance and compliance, projects and large transactions, Travel Manager in the books with both trip statuses, group settlement and the Trip Pack, claims and reimbursements matched to settlement, reminder grouping, actions, delivery tracking and briefings, the calendar subscription link, payroll import, who owes whom, and added features 1, 9 and 10.

-   **Phase 4 --- Taxation and corporate compliance:** GST, TDS and TCS, PF, ESI and professional-tax files, income tax for every person, company and trust, trusts and 80G, Governance and ROC filings, the AI rules watch, notices tracker with appeals, professional approvals, rules for both income-tax Acts, AIS matching, GSTR-2B outcomes, evidenced filing and payment statuses, Ask Thapal, and added features 11 and 12.

-   **Phase 5 --- Integration, security and recovery:** approved government intermediaries (decision 3), e-invoice and e-way bill, licensed prices, a native iPhone wrapper for the share sheet, two-way Google and Outlook calendar sync, WhatsApp and SMS channels, voice input in English, Tamil and Hindi, point-in-time recovery and restore drills, release control, incident response, the complete export, DPDP readiness, final visual design, added features 13 and 14, and release on KK\'s approval.

  108    Restore                   A point-in-time restore matches ledger totals, counts, document links, owners, permissions and reports before it is declared successful

  109    Interrupted work          A background import stopped midway resumes without duplicates; a pending approval survives a crash

  110    Release control           A release without your approval cannot publish; an approved one is verified in production with its evidence kept

  111    Complete export           The export opens in Excel, its checksums verify, and re-importing reproduces the same totals

  112    Environments              Nothing run in preview ever writes to production data

  113    Incident drill            A simulated suspicious sign-in raises an alert, opens an incident record and produces the evidence pack within the 6-hour window

  114    Health Centre             Each check turns green only on evidence; uploading a file alone changes nothing

  115    Cross-module agreement    The daily test shows expenses, travel, claims, assets, properties, investments, loans and tax equal to their ledger control accounts

  116    Re-reading                Re-reading 50 invoices with a newer engine shows old and new side by side, posts nothing without approval and creates no duplicates

  117    Report status             A report missing a statement shows Incomplete and reaches Final only after reconciliation, review and approval

  118    Group accounts            A part-owned entity counts at its share, and related-party transactions are listed

  119    Prior-period correction   A correction to a locked month posts in the open month, linked to the original, with the locked statements unchanged

  120    Non-accountant            A person with no accounting training completes the eight tasks in UIX acceptance unaided

  121    End-to-end journey        The final acceptance journey passes in personal, family, company and trust workspaces

## Appendix: what carries forward from the 8 November draft

Nothing in v1\'s controls is dropped. Its ten non-negotiables stand, with one reworded, and every section has a home in v2.

### Non-negotiables (v1 §1)

1.  Preserve the existing app, its financial history, configuration and shared ledger. No rebuild or reset.

2.  **Reworded:** one intake engine (today\'s Statement Desk), reached through one Add button. Smart Add and every contextual action use it.

3.  No duplicate financial effects from re-uploads, transfers, card settlements, retries, OCR or imports.

4.  Never invent balances, transactions, documents, company details, prices, rates or accounting facts.

5.  Minimise manual entry; confirm only where evidence is uncertain or approval is required.

6.  Keep originals, readings, versions, corrections, actions, approvals and reversals as evidence.

7.  Controlled rules with effective dates; certification and filing stay human.

8.  Draft, preview, tested, published and verified stay distinct; nothing is published without KK\'s explicit authorisation.

9.  Protect history, ownership, confidentiality and access boundaries.

10. Premium, minimal, calm on iPhone, iPad and desktop; plain language is mandatory.
